Frame blocks: N_PRE=660, N_HDR=2640, REF_PERIOD=16, N_HDR_BITS=2474, N_INFO_BITS=142, POLAR_N=2048, FORMAT_VERSION=2, FORMAT_VERSIONS=(1,2), SPREAD_RHO=0.054, WAVEFORM_CE=0/L=1, LEAD_IN_MAX_S=10. Callsign windows: CW_WINDOW=384 symbols, CW_UNIT=2, CW_UNITS=192, CW_LEAD_UNITS=8, CW_ROOM_UNITS=176, CW_AFTER_FULL=(13888,28350,42812,57274). INT8_SCALE=20. Receiver: FE_FS=4000, FE_CENTER_HZ=1500, CARRIER_BAND_HZ=(300,2700), CH_FS=250, CH_DECIM=16, Z_ACCEPT=6. L: L_T_NUM=970 (T_L=0.060625 s), L_N_PRE=330, L_N_HDR=1320, L_CW_WINDOW=192, L_CW_AFTER_FULL=(6944,14175,21406,28637), L_EDGE_HZ=920/97, L_PILOT_HZ=12207/970 (exact Fractions), L_PILOT_FRAC=3/20, L_CLIP_HEADROOM_DB=0, L_CLIP_OVERSHOOT=(1,1.5,2), L_CLIP_GUARD_HZ=1. modules.determinism: Integers and rationals are exact. A0/K_LIN/CARRIER_FRAC/USEFUL_FRAC come from math.exp at import, so a C++ port must NOT recompute them with std::exp (libm can differ by an ulp across glibc/MSVC/Apple); emit them as float.hex literals from a generator, as tools/gen_config_header.py already does for config.hpp. Rationals should be carried as num/den integer pairs (L_PILOT_HZ = 12207/970) so mixing stays in integer turns.
modules.io_state: None; pure constants. Imports sstvae.config for FS (and other modules import TRANSMIT_LATENTS_PER_GROUP=50600, GROUP_LATENTS=52800 from there).
modules.parity_test_idea: Generate native/core/qrss/constants.hpp from this module (plus frame presets and polar.INFO_SET) with a --check CI staleness gate like config.hpp; a pybind test walks every public name in sstvae.qrss.constants and compares to the C++ value bit-for-bit (float.hex) and rationals as (num, den).
risks: Hand-copying any constant into C++ is the classic silent on-air incompatibility; must be generated.
tools/gen_qrss_tables.py already emits a C subset (qrss_beacon_c/qrss_tables.h); a second generator for native/ must stay consistent with it (or share code).
The asserts at the bottom (T_DEN % FS == 0, FE_FS == CH_FS*CH_DECIM, CW lead+room+lead == 192, L_PILOT_HZ == 12207/970) should become static_asserts.

modules.purpose: All closed-form SHA-256 bit streams (decision D5): block b = SHA256(domain || prefix || uint32_be(b)); bit i = bit (7 - i%8) of byte (i%256)//8 of block i//256 (MSB first); 0 -> +1, 1 -> -1. Domains (ASCII, no terminator): 'QRSSTVAE CE preamble' (660 bits), 'QRSSTVAE CE reference' (one stream per frame, reference m takes bit m; FULL n_ref=3539), 'QRSSTVAE scramble' with prefix uint64_be(q) (FULL: 50600 bits = 198 hash blocks), 'QRSSTVAE CE spread header' (whitener, NOT keyed by q), 'QRSSTVAE L preamble' (660 bits -> 330 QPSK), 'QRSSTVAE L reference' (2 bits per ref). qpsk: bit 2i -> I, 2i+1 -> Q, each pm1/sqrt(2). Also slot clock: q = floor(unix_utc(QH)/900), parse_utc/parse_slot ISO-8601-with-zone parsing, quarter_hour_start.

pm1(bits) -> int8 (+1 for 0, -1 for 1)
preamble_ce() -> int8[660] (cached, read-only)
references_ce(n_ref) -> int8[n_ref]
qpsk(bits) -> complex128[len/2]

references_l(n_ref) -> complex128[n_ref]
spread_whitener(n) -> int8[n]
scrambler(q: int (uint64), n) -> int8[n]
quarter_hour_count(utc: aware datetime on a QH) -> int
parse_utc(s) -> aware datetime (refuses no-zone)
parse_slot(s) -> q
quarter_hour_start(q) -> datetime

modules.determinism: Fully bit-exact by construction (integers + SHA-256). qpsk values are +-1/np.sqrt(2.0) in float64 -- std::sqrt is correctly rounded, so exact too. q is Unix time ignoring leap seconds (std::chrono::system_clock since C++20 has the same epoch semantics).
modules.io_state: lru_cache'd read-only arrays (preamble, references, whitener); no files, no threads.
modules.parity_test_idea: Golden/pybind: sha_bits for each domain at n in {1, 7, 255, 256, 257, 660, 3539, 50600} with and without prefix; scrambler at q in {Q_TEST=1954752, Q_TEST+1, 2^40+12345} (the same triple test_qrss_c_ref uses), spread_whitener(50600), preamble_l, references_l(83+...), all np.array_equal. Also FIPS 180-4 vectors for the SHA-256 itself. Time: quarter_hour_count/parse_slot on edge strings, off-QH rejection.

q must be treated as uint64 big-endian (tests use q > 2^32).

parse_utc relies on Python 3.11+ datetime.fromisoformat after replacing Z with +00:00; a C++ parser (QDateTime ISODate or std::chrono::parse) will accept a different set of strings -- CLI-only, but document it.
Reference streams are shared prefixes across frame lengths (shorter frames' refs are a prefix) -- keep one stream, not per-frame regeneration with different counters.

modules.purpose: The CE frame: one place frame lengths live. FrameSpec(name, n_pre=660, n_hdr in {0,2640}, n_data, cw_after, hdr_rho) with derived n_data_sym (smallest L with L - ceil(L/16) == n_data), n_sym, n_pos (= n_sym + 384*n_win), n_ref, duration_s, win_start_pos, keyed_end/start_pos, pos_of(s) = s + 384*|{w: cw_after[w] <= s}|. Presets: FULL (n_data 50600: n_data_sym 53974, n_sym 57274, n_pos 58810, n_ref 3539 = 165 hdr + 3374 data, 1782.678 s), MEDIUM (16384; 20777/21545), SHORT (4096; 7670/8438), TINY (no header, 1024, no windows; 1753), plus LEGACY v1 copies (hdr_rho=0) and PROTOTYPES (full-spreadonly). layout(spec): references at j=s-660>=0, j%16==0; header non-ref symbol i carries coded bit i (bit 0 -> +1) for i<2474, the 2475th (stream index 3299 in FULL) is a spare sending +1; data non-ref symbol i carries precoded x_i. Spread header (format v2): data symbol i += sqrt(hdr_rho) * w_i * (1 - 2*bit[i mod 2474]).

modules.determinism: Bit-exact: all integer index arithmetic; assemble writes +-1, x, then adds sqrt(rho)*(+-1) -- one IEEE multiply and one add per data symbol, reproducible if C++ does out = x; out += sqrt(rho)*h in the same order (not fused: compile with -ffp-contract=off or write it so FMA cannot change it).
modules.io_state: lru_cache(16) of Layout per FrameSpec; read-only numpy arrays.
modules.parity_test_idea: For every preset (PRESETS, LEGACY, PROTOTYPES) compare all derived lengths and every Layout array (np.array_equal), and assemble() on random x and random 2474 header bits (array_equal on float64 bits). Also pos_of over all s and window_spans_s. Existing tests/test_qrss_format.py (frame counts, windows, reference grid) becomes the acceptance suite under pytest --native.
risks: FMA contraction in out[data] = x + sqrt(rho)*h would break bit-exactness (MSVC /fp:contract, GCC -ffp-contract=fast default for non-ISO modes on some targets).

lframe.LFrameSpec is a separate dataclass reusing _data_symbols, _ro, spread_signs and Layout; the C++ port needs a CE/L frame abstraction (waveform, t_sym, cw_window are class attributes used by tx.py to dispatch).
Frame names ('full', 'medium', 'short', 'tiny', 'full-v1', 'full-spreadonly', and L's 'l-full'...) are persisted in PassResult.frame and stores; keep them verbatim.
n_data must be a prefix of air order; FrameSpec validation (cw_after strictly increasing inside (n_pre+n_hdr, n_sym]) must be ported, since a malformed spec otherwise silently misplaces windows.

modules.purpose: Per-pass precoder (spec 2.4, decision D6): x = WHT_blocks(c_q * a) where c_q = sequences.scrambler(q, n) and blocks are 64 at a time then the binary decomposition of n % 64 in descending order (50600 = 790x64 + 32 + 8 = 792 blocks; 16384 = 256x64; 4096 = 64x64; 1024 = 16x64). Each block is the orthonormal Sylvester Hadamard H[i,j] = (-1)^popcount(i&j)/sqrt(M) of its own size, self-inverse, so unprecode(y, q) = c_q * WHT(y).
public_api: BLOCK = 64
block_sizes(n) -> list[int]
wht(v) -> float64 (blockwise orthonormal WHT over last axis; batch axes allowed)
precode(a_air, q) -> float64[n]
unprecode(y, q) -> float64[n]
block_mean(v) -> per-block mean broadcast back
block_index(n) -> int64[n] block id per symbol
numeric_primitives: in-place unnormalised fast WHT butterflies in Sylvester order: for h=1,2,4,..,M/2: first half += second; second = old_first - second
division by np.sqrt(M) after the butterflies (M=64 -> /8 exact; 32, 16, 8, 2 -> /sqrt(M) inexact)
np.repeat / mean for block_mean
modules.determinism: For .qrsp sources (fp16 latents, values on a 2^-24 grid below 2^16) the butterfly sums are EXACT in float64 in any order (verified: fsum-by-matrix equals the butterfly bit-for-bit for 64- and 32-blocks), and the final /sqrt(M) is one correctly-rounded op, so bit-exact is easy. For beacon-file / use_int8 sources the inputs are q/20 (inexact) and the result depends on summation order at 4.4e-16 (verified: matrix-fsum and integer-WHT-then-scale both differ from the butterfly). A bit-exact C++ port must replicate the exact butterfly order (h ascending, x+y then x-y) and the q/20.0-then-multiply-by-sign path; the C reference (qrss_beacon_c, integer WHT) only agrees to atol 1e-12. block_mean uses numpy's mean (pairwise/8-way-unrolled summation) -- receiver-only, tolerance parity.
modules.io_state: lru_cache of block sizes/runs; no files.
modules.parity_test_idea: pybind wht/precode/unprecode on (a) fp16-valued vectors and (b) from_int8(to_int8(.)) vectors for n in {1..200 random, 1024, 4096, 16384, 50600} and q in the C-ref triple: np.array_equal for both when the butterfly order is replicated. Round trip unprecode(precode(a)) within 1e-15. block_index/block_sizes exact.
risks: Using a matrix multiply, a different FWHT ordering, or integer WHT (as the C beacon does) for the int8 path gives ulp-level differences -- harmless on air but breaks 'bit-exact' parity claims.
_runs groups equal-size blocks; since tail sizes are descending powers of two below 64, the block order equals block_sizes order -- a C++ port must not reorder tail blocks.
Batch (leading-axis) use is relied on by EM/demod (2-D inputs).

modules.purpose: The 142-bit header and its coded form. Fields MSB first in table order: callsign 48 (8 x 6-bit codes in SSTVAE's beacon alphabet 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789/-. ?!...', space padded), grid 15 (((F1*18+F2)*10+D1)*10+D2, 32767=none, 32400..32766 invalid), picture_id 32, mode 2 (A=0,B=1,C=2), segment 2 (<= mode), codec_id 16, version 4 (FORMAT_VERSION=2), reserved 7 (=0), CRC 16 over bits 0..125. The CRC is SSTVAE's beacon._crc16 bit for bit (reg=0xFFFF; per bit: top=reg>>15; reg=((reg<<1)&0xFFFF)|b; if top: reg^=0x1021; not augmented), check value 0xA69D over ASCII '123456789' (NOT CCITT-FALSE 0x29B1, D8). Acceptance (D9): CRC AND version in `versions` AND reserved=0 AND mode<=2 AND segment<=mode AND valid grid AND callsign rstrip(' ') matches [A-Z0-9/]{1,8}. encode = polar_encode(pack(h)); decode = CA-SCL list 8 returning the most likely path that unpacks.
public_api: HeaderFields(callsign, grid|None, picture_id, mode, segment, codec_id, version=2, reserved=0) frozen dataclass
grid_encode(g|None) -> int; grid_decode(v) -> str|None
crc16(bits) -> uint8[16]
pack(h) -> uint8[142] (refuses anything unpack would reject)
unpack(bits, versions=(2,)) -> HeaderFields|None
encode(h) -> uint8[2474] coded bits
decode(llr[2474], list_size=8, versions=(2,)) -> HeaderFields|None (sum of passes' LLRs for soft combining)
CALL_CHARS=8, GRID_NONE=32767, MAX_MODE=2; re-exports INFO_SET, polar_encode, polar_decode
numeric_primitives: CRC-16 shift register (SSTVAE beacon variant)
bit packing int<->bits MSB first
regex validation of callsign and grid
modules.determinism: pack/unpack/encode exact. decode exactness is the polar decoder's (see polar.py).
modules.io_state: None.
modules.parity_test_idea: pack/encode byte-exact for the test headers (K1ABC/P FN42 0xDEADBEEF mode 2 seg 1 codec 0xD1D8, VK2/W1AW RR99, 00000000 JO62); unpack accept/reject agreement over ~1e5 random 142-bit vectors plus every single-bit flip of valid headers and CRC-valid headers with bad fields; grid round trip over all 32400 codes; crc16('123456789')=0xA69D. tests/test_qrss_header.py runs as-is under --native.
risks: Native already has beacon::crc16, ALPHABET and callsign_to_codes in native/core/beacon -- reuse them, but beacon.hpp's comment wrongly calls it CCITT-FALSE (as Python's does); do not 'fix' it to true CCITT-FALSE.
callsign_to_codes upper-cases and maps unknown chars to space; QRSS must validate first (pack refuses lowercase), so do not rely on the mapping.
The version-fallback path decode(versions=(1,2)) uses a custom accept callback; preserve 'first list path that unpacks', not 'first CRC-valid path'.
beaconfile/tx rely on encode() being a pure function of HeaderFields; FORMAT_VERSION is implicit in HeaderFields default.

modules.purpose: Polar (2048, 142) header code (D9). Encoder (format): u[INFO_SET[t]] = info[t], others frozen 0; x = u . F^(x)11 natural order, no bit reversal (x_j = XOR over i superset of j of u_i; implemented as stages where the first half of each block ^= second half); rate matching by circular repetition, coded bit e = x[e mod 2048] for e < 2474 (mother bits 0..425 sent twice). INFO_SET is a committed 142-entry literal (1015..2047), sha256 of its big-endian u16 bytes = 4e064eee...97bb; tools/gen_qrss_polar.py regenerates/--checks it (GA density evolution at Es/N0 = -9.4 dB). Decoder (not format): fold LLRs (mother[i] = sum over e = i mod 2048), recursive SCL with list 8, min-sum f, exact g, LLR path metric PM += log(1+exp(-(1-2u)*lambda)), rate-0 subtrees short-circuited (3717 such (offset,size) nodes; half the code below 1015 is one), returns paths sorted by PM; polar_decode returns first path passing `accept` (default header.unpack).
public_api: N=2048, K=142, E=2474, N_STAGES=11, INFO_SET (tuple), INFO_SET_SHA256
polar_transform(v) -> uint8 (self-inverse, last axis)
rate_match(x) -> (...,2474)
fold(llr[2474]) -> float64[2048]
polar_encode(info[142]) -> uint8[2474]
decode_list(llr, list_size=8) -> (info (m,142) uint8, pm (m,)) most likely first
polar_decode(llr, list_size=8, accept=None) -> uint8[142] | None
numeric_primitives: XOR butterflies
np.bincount fold (sums in ascending e order: (0 + llr[i]) + llr[i+2048])
min-sum f = sign(a1)sign(a2)min(|a1|,|a2|); g = a2 + (1-2b)a1
np.logaddexp(0, -a) (numpy: x+log1p(exp(-(x-y))) branches, LOGE2 on equality)
stable argsort over 2L candidates (decision-0 block first, then decision-1), keep//L = bit, keep%L = parent
numpy .sum(axis=1) (pairwise/unrolled) over softplus in rate-0 nodes
inf placeholders for dead paths at start (pm[1:]=inf)
modules.determinism: Encoder exact (XOR only). Decoder: path metrics depend on libm log1p/exp and numpy's pairwise summation order in rate-0 nodes, so a C++ port agrees on PMs to ~1e-12 relative, not bitwise; the chosen bits agree except at exact or ulp-level PM ties. Tie-break must replicate the stable sort over [all decision-0 candidates, all decision-1 candidates] (std::stable_sort on indices, inf handled as IEEE inf). Python runs a decode in ~15-20 ms; the receiver calls it several times per pass (block, spread, combined, version fallbacks, associate's summed LLRs).
modules.io_state: lru_cache of rate-0 node set; recursion depth 11.
modules.parity_test_idea: Encoder: array_equal over random info vectors and the test headers. Decoder: 2000 random noisy LLR vectors from SNRs spanning failure to success (incl. all-zero LLRs and heavily punctured/erased repeats): decode_list info arrays equal and pm within 1e-9 relative; polar_decode outputs equal. Assert the INFO_SET sha256 in C++ too (static check on the embedded literal).
risks: INFO_SET must be embedded as the literal (generated into the header), never recomputed by density evolution in C++.
Natural order, no bit reversal -- most textbook/library polar code uses bit-reversed order; using one would silently produce a different code.
Rate-0 shortcut must use the softplus sum over the node's INPUT LLRs (not leaf LLRs) to match PMs.
np.sign(0)=0 semantics vs copysign: harmless (min term is 0) but NaN must be impossible (fold rejects non-finite).

modules.determinism: Bit-exact achievable but two traps. (1) float64 -> float16 MUST be a single correctly-rounded conversion: converting via float32 double-rounds and differs on ~5.5e-5 of values (measured 277/5M), i.e. ~8 latents per mode-C picture -> a different picture ID. (2) The RMS uses numpy's pairwise sum; a naive or Kahan sum matched on a synthetic test, and a 1-ulp RMS difference flips an fp16 rounding with probability ~1e-8 per picture, but replicate numpy's pairwise algorithm (block 128, 8 accumulators) to be strict. Encoder output from native codec::encode is already bit-identical to Python's, but image loading is not (PIL LANCZOS vs stb resize), so the same JPEG gives a different picture ID unless the input is a 640x480 PNG.
modules.io_state: Reads/writes .qrsp (.npz, ZIP_STORED, zip64 local extras, entries version/mode/codec_id/segs/picture_id .npy); codec_id_from_onnx opens an ONNX session (CPU) to read custom metadata 'sstvae.source_sha256'.

A station must never re-encode for a repeat (re-encoding gives a different ID); the C++ app must persist and resend the .qrsp, as Python does.
npz writer must produce files numpy can np.load with allow_pickle=False (0-d int64 arrays, '<f2' descr, version 1.0 header aligned to 64 bytes).
framing._TX_PERMS is SSTVAE-private; native exposes framing::tx_perm(group) as uint16 -- reuse it.

notes:
What is normative, in order of strictness:
1. On-air, must be bit-exact: sequences (SHA-256 streams with domain strings, u32be block counter, u64be(q) scrambler prefix, MSB-first, 0->+1), frame layout (refs at j=s-660, j%16==0; header slot i -> coded bit i, spare +1 at the 2475th header non-ref symbol; data non-ref i -> x_i; spread copy sqrt(0.054)*w_i*(1-2*bit[i mod 2474])), precoder (64-blocks + descending binary tail, Sylvester order, 1/sqrt(M)), header bit layout + SSTVAE beacon CRC (0xA69D check value, not CCITT-FALSE), polar encoder (natural-order F^(x)11, INFO_SET literal with sha256 4e064eee...97bb, circular repetition to 2474), Morse keying units, picture ID (SHA-256 of u16be codec || u8 mode || fp16 LE groups), codec ID (source_sha256[:4]). 2. Storage formats: the beacon file is byte-for-byte fixed and timestamp-free (byte-identical to_bytes is the parity bar); .qrsp and PassResult are .npz (ZIP_STORED, numpy writes zip64 extras in LOCAL headers with 0xFFFFFFFF sizes, fixed 1980 timestamps) where array content, not zip bytes, is the contract. 3. Receiver-only but shared with this group: polar CA-SCL decoder, header.unpack/decode, frame.layout/disassemble/spread_signs/spread_symbols, precoder.wht/unprecode/block_mean/block_index, sequences.qpsk/preamble/references, picture maps, render.decoder_planes, types.PassResult. A receive port needs all of them; the transmit port needs everything except polar decoding, render and types.

Bit-exactness traps found by measurement: (a) float64->float16 in prepare_segment must be ONE correctly-rounded conversion; going through float32 double-rounds 5.5e-5 of values, about 8 latents per mode-C picture, so the picture ID changes. MSVC has no _Float16, so write a portable converter and test it on ties and subnormals. (b) The WHT is exact in any order for fp16 .qrsp inputs. For beacon-file or use_int8 inputs (q/20, which is inexact), only the exact butterfly order reproduces Python. Integer WHT, the qrss_beacon_c approach, agrees only to 4.4e-16, and test_qrss_c_ref already compares at atol 1e-12. (c) No FMA contraction in assemble's x + sqrt(rho)*h. (d) A0, K_LIN and CARRIER_FRAC come from math.exp, so generate them as hex-float literals. (e) Polar path metrics differ from Python by ulps because of libm log1p/exp and numpy's pairwise sums. Test that decoded bits are equal and PMs agree to a tolerance, and replicate the stable sort tie-break (decision-0 candidates first).

Reusable pieces already in native/: beacon::crc16, beacon::ALPHABET and callsign_to_codes (the same CRC function; its header comment repeats the wrong CCITT-FALSE name), framing::tx_perm(g) (the uint16 interleaver, which is air_to_canonical), codec::OnnxCodec::encode and decode (already bit- and byte-identical; needs a public accessor for source_sha256 to compute codec IDs), core/testing/npy.hpp (test-only; reads only f8/c16/i8). Missing and needed in the Qt-free core: SHA-256 (vendor qrss_beacon_c/sha256.c, which is FIPS-tested), zlib CRC-32, an npz/npy reader and writer (f2/f4/c8/u1/i8, 0-d arrays, zip64 local extras), a lenient JSON reader and writer (PassResult meta can contain NaN, Infinity and -Infinity, which json.dumps emits), and an exact double->half converter. native/core/dsp/morse is SSTVAE's audio CW ID with different semantics (it drops unknown characters and is case-insensitive). Do not reuse its validation.

An independent oracle already exists: qrss_beacon_c/ (C99, about 1200 lines) generates CE stream symbols, phase and Si5351 steps from a beacon file. It also has a generator, tools/gen_qrss_tables.py, that emits frame presets, domain strings and Q-format tables with --check. The C++ port should get a sibling generator for native/core/qrss/constants.hpp: every constants.py value, the frame presets including LEGACY v1 and PROTOTYPES, the INFO_SET literal and domain strings, with a CI staleness gate. That follows the config.hpp rule.

Parity strategy: extend tools/gen_golden_vectors.py with QRSS vectors. Store the input latents themselves (synthetic_full_latents uses default_rng/PCG64, which must not become a dependency): preamble_ce/l, references 3539, scrambler at Q_TEST=1954752, Q_TEST+1 and 2^40+12345, whitener 50600, FULL layout, header bits for the test headers, polar codewords, slot_symbols for SHORT/TINY, beacon-file bytes, and picture ID 0xD349C671. Then add pytest --native substitutions. Many call sites are from-imports and must be listed explicitly: demod (block_index, block_sizes, wht, scrambler, spread_whitener), precoder (scrambler), ldemod/ltrack (spread_signs), header (polar_decode, polar_encode, INFO_SET), lframe (_data_symbols, _ro, spread_signs, preamble_l, qpsk, references_l), acquire (preamble_ce, preamble_l). The roughly 585-test QRSS fast tier then becomes the acceptance suite.

App-level consequences: picture IDs from C++ match Python only for 640x480 PNG input, because stb and PIL LANCZOS resize differently. That is an acceptable above-modem difference, but the app must persist the .qrsp and never re-encode for repeats. A FULL pass is 1782.678 s and 14.38M samples at 8 kHz (115 MB as float64), so stream it. transmit_audio is chunk-invariant (verified), so any block size works. q = floor(unix/900) at the slot's quarter hour, t0 = QH + 1 s, and the WAV starts 12 s before t0. A pass spans two quarter hours; q names the first. The beacon file has no header-version field, so FORMAT_VERSION is implicit and a bump would invalidate existing files. Its waveform byte must be 0 even when L transmits from it. rules.py's env-var switches are process-global and exist only for old-vs-new comparisons; make them RxConfig flags or drop them deliberately.

Rough C++ size for this group: about 2,200 lines plus about 500 of shared infrastructure (SHA-256, CRC-32, npz, JSON, fp16). That excludes ce.py, lframe.py and lwave.py, which tx.py depends on for audio.

modules.determinism: No RNG. All phase arguments are reduced before trig (turns to [0,1); the closed-form pulse's sin/cos act on |d| <= ½·π(1±α); math.cos(c·j) for j <= 8, i.e. arguments <= ~29 rad, is the only unreduced trig and costs at most an ulp). The table path is a fixed-order upfirdn sum: chunking is bit-invariant (measured: chunk 2^18 and chunk 12345 give identical output). n0 = round(start_s·fs) uses Python's half-to-even round, so a port needs nearbyint. The carrier turns are exact integers, so a C++ port can match those bit for bit (the final int-to-double divide is correctly rounded). phi itself is tolerance-class, about 1e-13 rad (summation order and libm), because upfirdn's accumulation order is not specified. The output is analog, so a tolerance of about 1e-12 on the phase and 1e-12 on z is the right parity class. The C reference (below) is a separate integer oracle with 8e-5 rad rms error against this module.
modules.io_state: Pure functions. No files, threads, env vars or global mutable state. Module-level constants (PULSE_TABLE, PULSE_NORM, G0, _PULSE_TABLE_SQ) are computed at import. Output buffers go through internal chunking (2^18 samples for baseband, 2^19 for phase_at, 2048 positions for the matched filter). tx.transmit_audio builds the whole 8 kHz pass in memory: float64[~14.4M] ≈ 115 MB for FULL, in 120 s complex chunks of 15 MB.
modules.parity_test_idea: Golden vectors from a fixed SHORT slot (tx.slot_symbols of a synthetic beacon file, Q_TEST) plus a keying mask: (1) PULSE_TABLE and PULSE_NORM/G0 to 1e-15; (2) phase_grid(8000, n0=−1940, 60 s) and phase_at at off-grid taus to 1e-12 rad; (3) cw_phase_turns over each window (FSK) and the OOK amplitude bit-exact; (4) baseband + to_audio for the first 60 s with carrier 1500 and Fraction(15003,10) and lead_in 5 s: carrier turns bit-exact, audio to 1e-12; (5) chunked synthesis (to_audio with n0) equals one shot, bit-exact; (6) matched_filter of ones == G0, and loopback_stats gain ≈ 0.581 and dist_db as semantic checks. Run it as pytest --native by substituting the C++ functions into sstvae.qrss.ce, as the SSTVAE modem port does.
risks: Two phase paths (grid table and closed form) must both be ported, because the receiver (track.py remove_spread, the mean templates, the clock-offset channel sim) uses phase_at at arbitrary tau, while TX uses phase_grid.
The singular-point handling in _pulse_offsets (tau = 0 and ±5/3) is easy to get wrong in a scalar C++ loop; the limit formulas must be applied at |den| < 1e-9 exactly as here.

carrier_fraction needs a faithful port of Fraction.limit_denominator (continued-fraction best approximation) for float carriers, or the mixing phase differs from Python's. Also check_carrier's band 300–2700 Hz.
In to_audio, nn·num in int64 would overflow only if a pass ran past ~1e9 samples with a large denominator. At 14.4M samples it is safe, but C++ should use unsigned 128-bit or mulmod to be explicit.
Private helpers (_rrc, _turns_to_phasor, _ramp_envelope, _hann_int, _grid_sum, _loopback_span) are imported by lwave, track, ltrack, acquire, channel and scripts, so the C++ API has to expose them.

exact-path test `abs(start_s*fs - n0) < 1e-9` and `time_scale == 1.0` select different algorithms; a port must keep the same branch condition or the sim/receiver gets the closed form where Python used the table (difference 3e-13, harmless but breaks bit-level vectors).
OOK switches hard (no ramp) inside windows by design; do not 'fix' it with a ramp — the C reference and receivers assume hard switching.

modules.purpose: The waveform-L frame, a format module: LFrameSpec (T_L = 970/16000 s; preamble of 330 QPSK symbols; header of 1320 symbols, with 83 references and 1237 data symbols carrying the 2474 coded bits as QPSK; data symbol k carries precoded latents 2k (I) and 2k+1 (Q) scaled by 1/√2; one reference in 16 counted from the end of the preamble, and the data section does not start on a reference, the first data reference being j = 1328; callsign windows of 192 L symbols after stream symbols (6944, 14175, 21406, 28637)). Presets: L_FULL (n_sym 28637, n_pos 29405, n_ref 1770, 1782.678 s), L_MEDIUM, L_SHORT, L_TINY (no header, no windows). Layout gives the index arrays. The spread header puts latent i on air as (x_i + √rho·h_i)/√(1+rho), rho = SPREAD_RHO = 0.054, a permanent 0.23 dB. Also: assemble/disassemble, pair/unpair, and get/get_any/twin, which pick the waveform by frame name.

N_HDR_SLOTS = 1237
layout(spec) -> Layout(pre, hdr_ref, hdr_sym, data_ref, data, ref, known_idx, known_val complex, pos, win_pos, is_ref) (lru_cache 16, read-only arrays)
pair(v) -> complex[n/2] = (v[0::2] + j v[1::2])/√2; unpair(z) -> float[..., 2n]
data_latents(spec, x, hdr_bits=None) -> float64[n_data]
assemble(spec, hdr_bits|None, x) -> complex128[n_sym]; disassemble(y_sym, spec) -> (hdr bit values, data latent values)

np.argsort(kind='stable') to merge preamble and references into known_idx

depends on frame.spread_signs (SHA-256 whitener × (1 − 2·hdr bit[i mod 2474])), sequences.preamble_l/references_l (SHA-256 of 'QRSSTVAE L preamble' / 'QRSSTVAE L reference')
modules.determinism: Bit-exact is achievable. The indices are integers, the sequences come from SHA-256, and the arithmetic is a few IEEE multiplies and divides by sqrt(2), sqrt(rho) and sqrt(1+rho). With the same operation order, (x + sqrt(rho)*h)/sqrt(1+rho) and then (a + jb)/sqrt(2), C++ reproduces the bits. There is no RNG, and test_qrss_frozen bans seeded draws in format modules.
modules.io_state: Pure. The only state is functools.lru_cache on layout() (16 entries) and the cached read-only sequences in sequences.py. No IO.
modules.parity_test_idea: Through pybind and pytest --native, or golden vectors: for every preset, the scalar counts (n_sym, n_pos, n_ref, n_data_sym, keyed_end_pos) and every Layout array must be bit-identical. assemble() must equal Python bit for bit on Gaussian x plus random header bits, with and without the spread copy (hdr_rho 0 and 0.054). unpair(pair(v)) must round-trip to 1 ulp. get_any and twin must give the same name mapping ('short' <-> 'l-short').
risks: lframe imports frame.spread_signs and frame._ro and duck-types LFrameSpec into it, so the C++ FrameSpec/LFrameSpec should share an interface (n_data, n_sym, waveform) rather than be two unrelated structs.

L test frames are not exact time twins of the CE ones. Only FULL is: CE SHORT has n_pos 8438 = 255.777 s, and l-short has 4218 = 255.716 s, because 7670/2 is not 3834. Do not assert equal durations for the non-FULL presets.

hdr_rho=None resolves to SPREAD_RHO when there is a header and to 0 otherwise. The default 'pending Jeff's call' is noted in the code, so the spread-on-L decision may still move and should be kept as a constant, not hard-coded.
has_header is true when n_hdr > 0 or hdr_rho > 0, so a spread-only frame (n_hdr = 0, rho > 0) needs hdr_bits but has no header symbols. Keep that branch.

modules.purpose: Waveform L, the on-air format for SSB rigs. A linear RRC-shaped QPSK carrier (data: d(t) = Σ a_s p(tau − pos(s)), with p the unit-energy RRC, alpha 0.15, cut at ±8 L symbols, renormalised at T = 970 grid steps; PULSE_TABLE[15521]) mixed down by f_p = 12207/970 Hz, plus a pilot tone at 0 Hz of amplitude A_PILOT = √(3/17) (15% of the power before clipping). The pilot rises to A_ID = √0.63 in the lead-in and in the callsign windows, ramped over 8 units at each end and over the first 8 preamble symbols after a lead-in. The windows key the pilot by FSK, with CE's Hann-integral definition, one unit per L symbol. The whole frame then goes through SSTVAE's 3-pass overshoot clipper at CLIP_FS = 250 Hz. The threshold is A_CLIP = √(20/17), with exponents (1, 1.5, 2); only the correction is filtered, by an FFT mask over [−f_p − EDGE − 1 Hz, +1 Hz] with 1 Hz raised-cosine edges. The frame is zeroed outside the keyed span, scaled by 1/A_ID, and interpolated to 8 kHz by a 481-tap Kaiser(β = 12) FIR (cutoff 125 Hz, up = 32). The module also has the matched filter, the conversion back to data-centred baseband, PAPR, occupied bandwidth, and the loopback statistics (data/ref gain ≈ 0.880, SINR ≈ 11.85 dB, PAPR ≈ 3.2 dB, pilot share ≈ 13.8%).

mix_turns(fs, n0, n, f_hz: Fraction) -> exact turns in [0,1); tau_grid(fs, n0, n)

scipy.signal.upfirdn: interpolation with the 481-tap table, up=32 from 250 Hz to 8 kHz, computed per chunk over a ±240-tap window
scipy.signal.firwin(481, 125.0, fs=8000, window=('kaiser', 12.0)) × up (native has kaiser() and a private firwin_band(); it exposes only a Hamming lowpass)

np.abs (hypot) and the power (thr/|z|)**k for k = 1, 1.5, 2. NumPy fast-paths 1.0 and 2.0 (copy and square), and only 1.5 goes to pow()
raised-cosine ramps 0.5·(1 − cos πy); the Hann integral and the turns-to-phasor helper from ce
exact mixing turns modulo den·fs (970·250 = 242500)

modules.determinism: No RNG, but the result is tolerance-class, not bitwise. The clipper is a whole-frame nonlinearity followed by an FFT filter, and pocketfft (native) and scipy's pocketfft/ducc differ in the last bits. Its output also depends on nfft through the frequency-sampled mask: changing margin_s from 4 to 6 s moves z by up to 2.05e-6 against an RMS of 1.0 (measured on L_SHORT). A port must reproduce n0 = floor((t_lo − margin)·fs), n1, the nfft choice and the pass order exactly to stay near 1e-10. About 35% of samples exceed the threshold on the first pass, so the threshold test (mag > A_CLIP) can flip on a sample sitting at the boundary, a local and tiny effect. pow(x, 1.5) is libm-dependent at the ulp level. The 8 kHz interpolation is chunk-invariant, because every chunk is computed from the stored whole-frame Baseband.
modules.io_state: Pure, apart from memory. frame_baseband holds the whole frame at 250 Hz (L_FULL: 447,809 complex128 ≈ 7 MB, plus three nfft-sized FFT buffers of about 7 MB each), and is built once per pass before any audio. resample then produces 8 kHz chunks on demand. No files, threads or env vars.
modules.parity_test_idea: Golden vectors on L_TINY and L_SHORT with Gaussian latents, random header bits and a keying mask, with and without a 5 s lead-in. (1) PULSE_TABLE, PULSE_NORM and G0 to 1e-15. (2) composite() before the clipper to 1e-12. (3) band_mask on fftfreq(nfft) to 1e-15. (4) frame_baseband z to ~1e-9 absolute, using Python's n0 and nfft. (5) resample(bb, 8000, i0, m) for a few chunks to ~1e-9, and chunked equal to one-shot bitwise in C++. (6) Semantic checks: loopback_stats data_vs_ref ≈ 0.880 ± 0.005, sinr_db ≈ 11.85 ± 0.1, papr_db ≈ 3.2 ± 0.1, pilot_frac ≈ 0.138, and gain_pilot per section ≈ 1. (7) End to end: the test_qrss_lwave genie receiver on C++-generated 8 kHz audio reproduces the loopback.
risks: The clipper is non-causal over the whole frame, so L cannot be streamed sample by sample: the native TX must render frame_baseband (~0.6 s in Python for L_FULL) before keying, then stream the 8 kHz interpolation.

resample's interpolation filter is designed at FS = 8 kHz whatever fs_out is (cutoff 125/4000). It is right only for up = 32 (8 kHz) and up = 1, and channel.py relies on it at FE_FS = 4000 (−60 dB). Port that quirk as it is, or restrict the API to the rates used.

The L pilot is the named carrier, and the data sit 12.58 to 22.07 Hz below it, so tx.check_pilot demands a pilot >= 300 + 22.07 Hz. The GUI's frequency picker (FREQ_MIN_HZ 300) must apply that rule for L.
L_AVG_POWER = 0.63 is a measured constant pinned as a format value (the lead-in and window pilot level). Do not recompute it at run time.

The window FSK reaches 4.6 Hz above the pilot, past the clipper's filter, and passes untouched only because just the clipper's correction is filtered. A port that filters z instead would change the on-air signal.
Three numerically distinct firwin variants are needed in native (Hamming lowpass and bandpass, Kaiser resample_poly, Kaiser(12) here), so expose firwin_band(window) generally.
The welch/quantile/interp stats are only diagnostic; the TX does not need them, but the receiver-side constants (ldemod D_*, ltrack) were calibrated with loopback_stats.

modules.purpose: Reference model of a clock-chip (Si5351) beacon that makes CE's phase by frequency steps with error feedback. Every Tu = 1/f_update it sets f_u = round_half_away((Phi_target(t_{u+1}) − Phi_reached)/(2π·Tu·step_hz)) whole synthesizer steps and advances Phi_reached by exactly that. Updates start at tau = −8 (start of keying). The target is phi + 2π·theta_cw, with FSK windows unwrapped; OOK windows gate the output and add no phase. Also synthesizes the resulting piecewise-linear phase for spectrum and error tests. It is the Python half of the C3 parity test with qrss_beacon_c.

target_phase(tau_pos, sym, spec, keying=None, ook=False) -> rad (ce.phase_at + 2π ce.cw_phase_turns)

modules.determinism: Deterministic; integer output from float64 inputs. Python accumulates `reached` in float64, while the C reference keeps it in exact modular integers (units of 2^-32 turn / (1000·fu_num)). C3 shows the steps are identical when Python is driven by the C phase through phase_fn (FULL SHORT frame, 990 Hz, 0.4 Hz steps, three slots, and fractional rates 1000/3 and 100000/101). A step can still differ when a value lands within float error of a .5 boundary, so integer arithmetic (the C's) is the bit-exact definition to port.
modules.io_state: Pure; no IO or state.
modules.parity_test_idea: In ctest, run the C++ (or the vendored C) qrss_si5351_next over SHORT at 990 Hz and 0.4 Hz steps against golden int32 steps generated by Python si5351_steps with phase_fn fed from the C phase. Equality must be bit-exact, and the reached phase must stay within step/2 + 1e-3 rad of target_phase.
risks: Nothing in the app or the CLIs uses it; only tests use it (test_qrss_beacon M6, test_qrss_c_ref C3). It matters only if native grows a hardware-beacon or Si5351 output feature, so it is low priority for a soundcard-SSB port.
The signature carries an unused q_unused positional argument. Keep it for pybind substitution parity if pytest --native swaps this module.
used_by: tests/test_qrss_beacon.py (M6 error after the matched filter, frequency swing, error feedback)

modules.purpose: Portable C99 reference of a CE beacon's phase generator, and the parity oracle for any port of CE. It has no allocation and uses only integer arithmetic (int64 inside). It binds a beacon file (magic 'QRSB', CRC-32, file version 1, waveform must be CE, int8 latents at offset 366, header bits at 56, keying mask at 32, OOK flag at bit 0 of byte 30) to a slot q, and computes on the fly: preamble, references, per-slot scrambler and spread-header whitener (SHA-256 with two-block caches), the precoder (sign flips plus an unnormalised Sylvester WHT per block of 64/32/…/1 in int16), stream symbols by class, and the spread copy. The phase at tau in Q22 is Σ v·SCALE_Q32[class]·pulse_q22 + h·SPREAD_Q32·pulse_q22, accumulated in 2^-54 turn and rounded to a uint32 phase in 2^-32 turn. The pulse is a Q14 half-table at T/64, linearly interpolated (8e-5 rad rms against Python). It adds the FSK window phase (a Q30 Hann-integral table) and gives the keyed/OOK gate and the exact Si5351 error-feedback steps (qrss_si5351_start/next, exact for fu_num <= 2^21). qrss_tables.h is generated from Python by tools/gen_qrss_tables.py, and a --check mode is enforced by test_tables_are_current.

modules.determinism: Bit-exact and platform-independent by construction: integer-only, no int-width dependence (a test bans shifts of bare literals for 16-bit-int AVR), and UBSan-clean (a test compares UBSan and -O2 bytes). Against Python it is tolerance-class on phase (C2: <= 2e-4 rad rms and <= 1e-3 rad max over 600 s at 990, 250 and 8000 Hz updates, both keyings) and exact on symbols (C1, atol 1e-12 after scaling), sequences (bit for bit) and Si5351 steps (C3, identical when Python uses the C phase).
modules.io_state: The caller owns all memory. qrss_ce_t is 632 bytes: two cache slots for each of the four SHA streams and two precoder blocks, so the 17-symbol pulse span never thrashes. The file must stay resident; it is read through a pointer. No threads, IO or globals in the library. State is mutated on every call (the caches), so one qrss_ce_t must not be shared across threads.
modules.parity_test_idea: Already exercised by tests/test_qrss_c_ref.py, which builds the C with whatever cc is on PATH and runs it under the default pytest (C1–C3, the table check, refusals, UBSan, fractional rates, fu_num up to 2^21). For native: build it into a ctest target that checks C++ ports of ce.phase_grid and the precoder/sequences against qrss_ce_phase and qrss_ce_symbol (with C2's tolerances), and checks a C++ Si5351 path for bit-exact steps. Or vendor it unchanged and keep test_qrss_c_ref as its oracle test.
risks: The C covers CE only and only a beacon file. It rejects waveform L, has no audio path (no carrier mix, no 50 ms key ramp, no lead-in phase beyond 'key early'), and sends int8 latents (the beacon-file values, 37 dB below the fp16 a .qrsp sends by default). Using it for app audio would make a .qrsp pass equal tx(use_int8=True), not Python's default, and adds 8e-5 rad rms phase error. Compatible on air, but not parity with Python's transmit_audio.

Reusable in native as is: qrss_ce.c and sha256.c compile cleanly as C++20 with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic (checked in a scratch build). Or add C to native's `project(... LANGUAGES CXX)`. qrss_ce.h has no extern "C" guard, so a C++ consumer of a C-compiled object needs one, or must compile the .c files as C++. qrss_tables.h defines static const arrays in a header (one copy per TU).
Speed for audio-rate use: 2.048M phase samples at 8 kHz in 0.52 s (measured, -O2), so about 3.6 s for a full 1782.7 s pass. Acceptable offline, not vectorized.
Presets come only from frame.PRESETS. A frame added to Python needs `make tables` (tools/gen_qrss_tables.py), and the C struct caps windows at 4.
The C enforces the callsign room (units 8..183) and a non-empty mask for windowed frames (QRSS_E_CALLSIGN). Python's tx enforces 'callsign required' differently, so a C++ port must keep both checks.
used_by: docs/qrss/README.md 'The Si5351 C reference' (intended for AVR/ESP32 beacon ports)

modules.purpose: Minimal FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 (init/update/final plus one-shot), C99, no allocation, 64 round constants only. The beacon hashes its preamble, reference, scrambler and spread-whitener blocks on the device. Every message is under 64 bytes: a domain string, an optional uint64_be(q), and a uint32_be block number.

modules.determinism: Bit-exact. Checked against the FIPS vectors including one million 'a' fed in uneven pieces, and against hashlib across the 55/56/64-byte padding edges.
modules.io_state: Pure; the caller owns the context.
modules.parity_test_idea: Keep the selftest. For native, a ctest calling sha256 on the FIPS vectors, and on sha_bits blocks of the six QRSS domains ('QRSSTVAE CE preamble', 'QRSSTVAE CE reference', 'QRSSTVAE scramble' with uint64_be(q), 'QRSSTVAE CE spread header', 'QRSSTVAE L preamble', 'QRSSTVAE L reference'), compared with pinned digests from test_qrss_frozen.

notes:
TX audio pipeline as implemented (tx.transmit_audio, 202 lines, is the natural C++ entry point and is what native/gui/qrss_tx shells out to via qrss_transmit.py):
- CE: slot_symbols (frame.assemble of the preamble, the header's polar bits, references and precode(air latents, q)) -> ce.baseband directly at FS = 8000. This is the exact table path: upfirdn(PULSE_TABLE, positions, up=485, down=2), about 16 taps per output sample. Then the keying envelope (50 ms raised cosine outside [t0 − 8T − lead_in, keyed_end]), the window FSK or OOK, and exp(j·2π·frac(turns)). ce.to_audio then forms amplitude·Re{z·e^{j2π(num/den)n/8000}} with exact integer turns. It runs in 120 s chunks, n0 counts from sample 0 = t0 − 12 s, and the audio is pre_s 12 s + keyed span + post_s 3 s. No resampling happens on the TX path: the baseband is generated at 8 kHz.
- L: slot_symbols (lframe.assemble) -> lwave.frame_baseband at 250 Hz, built once for the whole frame. The non-causal FFT clipper runs on the composite (data mixed down by 12207/970 Hz, plus the pilot). The frame is zeroed outside the keyed span and scaled by 1/√0.63. lwave.resample then gives 8 kHz chunks (481-tap Kaiser(12), up = 32, stateless and chunk-exact), and ce.to_audio mixes to the named pilot frequency.
- Time and frequency are exact rationals throughout: T = 485/16000 s (CE) and 970/16000 s (L), and the sample rate must divide 16000. The L offset 12207/970 Hz is mixed in integer turns modulo 242500 at 250 Hz. The carrier is a Fraction (float or str via limit_denominator(2^20)), mixed modulo den·8000. Every trig argument is reduced to [0,1) turns first, which matches the project rule; keep it in C++.

Parity classes for the port plan: (1) frame and layout arithmetic, SHA sequences, QPSK/pair mapping, the precoder and the carrier turns can be bit-exact. (2) The CE phase/baseband/audio is closed-form float, ~1e-13 rad agreement (phase_grid vs phase_at measured 3e-13), so use 1e-12 tolerances. (3) L's clipped baseband is FFT- and nonlinearity-bound, ~1e-9 at best if n0, margin_s = 4 s, nfft = next_fast_len(len + 4·fs) (11-smooth; native dsp::next_fast_len matches pocketfft good_size) and the pass order are reproduced exactly. A different FFT padding alone moved the output 2e-6. Add semantic loopback checks (data_vs_ref 0.880, SINR 11.85 dB, PAPR 3.2 dB) as the robust gate. (4) Si5351 steps are integer and exact via the C's modular arithmetic. Python's float loop matches when fed the same phase.

There are no QRSS golden vectors today. The only cross-implementation oracle is the C reference, and it covers CE beacon-file phase and steps only. Before writing C++ for QRSS, add a gen_golden_vectors-style generator for: ce.PULSE_TABLE, lwave.PULSE_TABLE, phase_grid, cw_phase_turns, baseband + to_audio on SHORT, lframe layouts and assemble, lwave.composite / frame_baseband / resample on L_TINY and L_SHORT, and si5351 steps. Also add a pytest --native substitution list for sstvae.qrss.ce, lwave and lframe, mirroring NATIVE_SUBSTITUTIONS, and watch the from-imports: tx.py does `from .frame import assemble`, and channel.py does `from .ce import check_carrier`.

Reusing the C in native: qrss_ce.c and sha256.c compile cleanly as C++20 with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic (verified in a scratch build), so they can go into sstvae_core unchanged. The C++ build can compile them as C++, or C can be enabled in native's CMake, which is currently `LANGUAGES CXX` only. sha256.c fills a real gap: native/core has no Qt-free SHA-256, and sequences.sha_bits is format-defining. Recommended split: port ce.py and lwave.py float paths as the normative TX and RX implementation. Vendor qrss_ce.c as an independent integer oracle in ctest, and as the engine for any future Si5351/hardware-beacon feature. Do not use the C for app audio: it is CE-only and beacon-file/int8-only, has no ramp or carrier mix, and has 8e-5 rad rms phase error, so a .qrsp pass would become what Python sends with use_int8=True. The C presets come only from frame.PRESETS via tools/gen_qrss_tables.py; the --check mode is enforced by test_tables_are_current. That staleness gate is analogous to native's config.hpp gate; QRSS constants (sstvae/qrss/constants.py: T_NUM/T_DEN, BETA, ALPHA, SPAN, the L_* pilot, the clip values, the window geometry) should get the same generated-header treatment for C++.

Shared surface: ce and lwave are not TX-only. The receiver (track, ltrack, em, acquire, channel sim) uses ce.phase_at, var_grid, matched_filter, mean_template, cw_phase_turns, G0, pulse and _rrc, and lwave.pilot, id_weight, A_ID, PULSE_NORM and G0. Several private helpers (_rrc, _turns_to_phasor, _ramp_envelope, _hann_int, _grid_sum, _loopback_span) are imported across modules, so design one Qt-free core/qrss/waveform layer with CE and L parameterised by symbol length (485 vs 970 grid steps) rather than two copies. The _grid_sum and matched_filter code is the same in both modules apart from the step.

Native primitives to add or expose: upfirdn (polyphase, real taps on real or complex input); firwin with an arbitrary window (dsp.cpp's firwin_band is internal, and only Hamming is public); Fraction.limit_denominator; Python-round (half-even) semantics where round() is used; complex FFT and ifft at next_fast_len (pocketfft is there). welch, quantile and interp are needed only for diagnostic stats.

Resource and streaming facts for the app and Android: a full pass is 1782.678 s, about 14.4M samples at 8 kHz. Python materialises it, about 115 MB as float64. A C++ TX should stream chunks to TxEngine instead. CE can be generated incrementally from any sample index, since it is closed form and bit-chunk-invariant. L needs the ~7 MB 250 Hz frame plus about 21 MB of FFT scratch, built before keying (0.6 s in Python), after which chunks are cheap. The C phase generator runs 2.048M updates in 0.52 s.

Gotchas: lwave.resample's filter is designed for 8 kHz whatever fs_out is; only fs_out = 8000 is right, and channel.py also relies on 4000 at −60 dB. The L pilot is the named carrier, so the data reach 22.07 Hz below it and check_pilot needs >= 322.07 Hz. The native GUI's 300 Hz minimum is not enough for L. On-off keying is CE-only, and L refuses it. Only FULL is an exact CE/L time twin; the test presets differ by one CE symbol pair. L_AVG_POWER = 0.63 is a measured, pinned format constant. NumPy's ** fast paths make clip exponents 1.0 and 2.0 exact; only 1.5 goes through pow(). si5351 rounds half away from zero, while ce.baseband's n0 uses Python's half-to-even round.

modules.determinism: No RNG. In-process fully deterministic. Cross-implementation: the complex64/float32 casts after every stage (FE, FE', keep, level, CH) quantise away nearly all FFT/summation-order differences, so near-bit-exact is achievable: measured direct np.convolve vs scipy oaconvolve in audio_to_fe differ in 1 of 240,000 complex64 samples (1 ulp); live.StreamFE (ALIGN=16 audio samples, HALO=128) vs batch: 0 mismatches over 120k samples. blank/normalise/running_median/interp can be bit-exact if numpy semantics are copied exactly (exact median selection, float32 arithmetic, np.interp's slope*(x-xp[j])+fp[j] formula, and numpy complex64/float32 division which is Smith's algorithm = multiply by the float32 reciprocal: a per-part division differs in 43% of samples by 1 ulp, measured). mix_phasor uses libm cos/sin on arguments already reduced to [0, 2pi): ~1 ulp across libms. resample_poly is a direct polyphase sum (bit-exact possible only by copying upfirdn's summation order; tolerance 1e-13 otherwise, then the complex64 cast). Kaiser windows use Cephes i0 in scipy vs native's power series -> freeze the filter tables instead of re-deriving. noise_psd is tolerance class (~1e-12 rel; FFT 2500 + median) but its flat/skirt masks are threshold comparisons on freqz values (num >= 10^-0.01 den; r >= 0.01) and must match exactly; audio_hz always lies on the 1/64 Hz grid so the set of masks is finite and can be checked exhaustively. PassbandStore is bit-exact (int16; FLAC lossless). Rule switch rules.EDGE_NOISE is read from env var QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE on every noise_psd call.
modules.io_state: Pure functions except PassbandStore. lru_caches: _noise_response(maxsize 8), _fold_power(8), _fe_power(64), _fe_flat(64), _fe_response(64), keyed on (fs_in, fs_out, nfft, audio_hz float, band tuple); returned arrays made read-only. Env var QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE (rules.old(EDGE_NOISE)) inherited by the listener's spawned end-of-slot process. PassbandStore: directory with meta.json {'fs':4000,'scale':8192.0} (re-opened as written), fe_<hour>.i16 (hour=floor(t/3600); fixed-size np.memmap of (3600*fs, 2) int16 interleaved I/Q = 57.6 MB, relies on sparse files), fe_<hour>.json (merged [[lo,hi],...] written sample ranges, rewritten atomically on every write), fe_<hour>.flac (2-ch PCM_16 at 4000 Hz via soundfile/libsndfile, written to fe_<hour>.flac.<pid>.tmp, read back and compared sample for sample, os.replace, raw unlinked unless mtime_ns changed). Packing on a daemon thread 'passband-pack' at most every 60 s of stream time for hours ended >= 120 s ago (pack=True only for the live listener); threading.RLock around write vs pack swap; reads retry once on FileNotFoundError (pack race); a write into a packed hour unpacks it first; expire() deletes hours older than keep_hours relative to stream time (or time.time()). _atomic_write tmp name includes pid and thread id. soundfile optional (ImportError/OSError -> None: hours stay raw, packed ones unreadable). Readers in other processes: qrss_decode.py --retro / em.retro_detect, qrss_receive.py writes captures.
modules.parity_test_idea: Golden vectors from Python: (1) audio_to_fe on a fixed 60 s seeded audio file -> complex64, allow <=1e-5 fraction of 1-ulp mismatches; also StreamFE-style chunked C++ vs batch Python. (2) blank on FE with injected clicks: keep bit-equal, fe*keep bit-equal; normalise on a capture with an AGC gain step: level and output bit-equal (exercise the complex/float32 reciprocal-division rule). (3) channelise at f_mix on the 1/64 Hz grid including n0 negative, n0 ~ 7.2e6 and f near +-1200 Hz: f_mix exact rational, ch complex64 rtol 1e-6 (expect almost all bit-equal); channelise_keep likewise. (4) noise_psd: sweep audio_hz over every 1/64 Hz position in 300-440 and 2560-2700 Hz (w=2500 and a short w) with and without exclude_hz at -95/+95 Hz and with QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE set/unset: expose _fe_flat/_fe_response masks and require exact equality; PSD rtol 1e-9. (5) PassbandStore cross-implementation: Python writes a capture spanning an hour boundary with a gap and a >16383-peak segment, C++ reads (int16, mask, coverage, t0_index exact), C++ packs to FLAC, Python reads; and the reverse. Bind via the pytest --native substitution so tests/test_qrss_frontend.py and the EDGE_NOISE cases in tests/test_qrss_rules.py run against C++.
risks: Python integer semantics: i_a % decim, n0 % P and -(-n//P) are floor-mod/floor-div; C++ % truncates toward zero, so negative FE indices (capture starting after the search span) silently shift the mixing phase or the CH grid. quantise_mix and every int(round(...)) use half-to-even (use std::nearbyint, never std::round).
numpy complex/real division is multiply-by-reciprocal (Smith), not per-part division: normalise's fe/sqrt(level) differs in ~43% of samples by 1 ulp if written as std::complex<float>/float.
NEP 50 dtype rules: float32_array * python_float stays float32 (store quantisation, blanker threshold np.float32(k^2)*nu, medians /ln2 in float32); doing these in double changes bits.
FMA contraction: clang (macOS arm64, Android NDK) contracts x*x+y*y by default; the near-bit-exact claims need -ffp-contract=off on this code (GCC ISO mode and MSVC /fp:precise do not contract).

D43 edge logic is subtle: flatness counts the 16 decimation folds (at 305 Hz only 261 of 702 band bins are flat, all on one side), the FE_MIN_HZ*w/fs clear-bin count, the skirt fallback's geometric mean, and the 'quieter side' fallback; threshold-sensitive masks must match exactly. lead_in_span calls noise_psd on ch[have] (gaps removed, non-contiguous).

resample_poly casts its filter to complex for complex input and uses specific pre/post padding (n_pre_pad=16, n_pre_remove=11); alignment ch[k] <-> fe[16k] is a contract tracked downstream (tau0, PassResult.ch_t0_index).
_FE_TAPS is defined twice (frontend.py and channel.py's fallback, the latter with fftconvolve): one generated table in C++.

PassbandStore depends on sparse files (np.memmap w+ of 57.6 MB per hour; ~2.8 GB raw for 48 h where sparse files are unavailable, e.g. typically NTFS) and on os.replace/unlink of files that may be memory-mapped, which fails on Windows. FLAC needs libFLAC or libsndfile on all five desktop platforms and Android (Qt has no FLAC codec); the format must stay readable by Python's retro decode.
No inter-process lock: the listener writes while qrss_decode --retro may read; correctness rests on atomic replaces, the JSON range index and a retry.
running_median/normalise cost over a FULL slot (7.2M FE samples): 36k medians of 4000 and 180k sorts of 400; fine in C++ but must not run on a GUI thread.

modules.determinism: No RNG and no hashing at run time (preamble sequences come from sequences.py via SHA-256, an exact format constant). In-process deterministic. Cross-implementation it is tolerance-class in the continuous outputs, with discrete decisions (lines, passed, chosen cell, Viterbi paths, alias/ownership/merge drops) expected to agree except at measure-zero near-ties. The spectrogram stores float32 power, which absorbs FFT-backend differences almost always (numpy vs scipy.fft on 448k bins: 0 float32 mismatches, measured), so A1's stat and A3's emissions can be near-bit-exact if numpy's dtype flow is copied (float32 median/ln2, float32 P/med, then /float64 shape and cast back to float32; sequential float32 sum over the 11 frames). A2 is float64 throughout with einsum/oaconvolve/CubicSpline/polyfit/hypot: expect ~1e-12 rel; sensitivity measured: a 1e-6 input perturbation moved df by 1.2e-9 Hz, tau0 by 1.9e-9 s and Lambda by 1.4e-4 (of 187). Tie-break rules to copy: Viterbi strict '>' over d=-2..2 and argmax-first; np.argsort's unstable order matters only for exactly equal float32 stats (A1 stops at the threshold, so zeros are never ranked). Underflow: p-values below 1e-250 switch to argmax Lambda.
modules.io_state: No files, threads or processes. Module-level constants built at import: CE_PRE/L_PRE (preamble_ce() int8 +-1 x660 -> float64, preamble_l() complex128 QPSK x330, read-only; MF taps). lru_cache: _band_cov(maxsize 4). Reads env var QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE indirectly through frontend.noise_psd in lead_in_span. Memory: A3 on FULL (896 frames) holds E float32 896x9601 (34 MB), the channel stack float32 (~54 MB) converted to float64 in tbd_viterbi (~108 MB) plus int8 backpointers (~14 MB): ~200 MB peak (measured 36 MB SHORT, 78 MB MEDIUM). Timing (Python, this box): A1 15 ms; A2 0.04-0.2 s per (line, waveform); joint live acquisition on a SHORT capture with 12 lines and 11 pilot hypotheses (35 A2 searches) 1.85 s; A3 0.31 s SHORT, 0.81 s MEDIUM, ~2.3 s FULL extrapolated.
modules.parity_test_idea: Golden captures generated in Python (seeded channel simulator, FE' complex64 .npy + t0_index): CE and L at TINY/SHORT, SNR -15/-25/-31 dB, drift +2.5 Hz/min, lead-in 5 s, carriers at 340/1500/2660 Hz, a neighbour 16 Hz and 95 Hz away, hints. Compare: CarrierStats.stat (float32, allow a few 1-ulp flips), carrier_lines (bin, drift exact; f_hz 1e-9 Hz; metric rtol 1e-6), pilot_lines exact; per (line, kind) Lambda grid and S rtol 1e-9, preamble_p cell index exact, PreambleHit f_hz 1e-7 Hz, tau0_s 1e-6 s, lam rtol 1e-7, phase 1e-7 rad, passed/n_groups exact; lead_in_s exact; tbd_emissions E float32 with flip tolerance, Viterbi paths exact, Z rtol 1e-9, p_value rtol 1e-9, shape_z/above_z rtol 1e-9, waveform verdict exact; Acquisition.detections order/method/waveform exact, f_hz 1e-7. Then substitute the C++ functions into sstvae.qrss.acquire (the pytest --native NATIVE_SUBSTITUTIONS pattern) and run tests/test_qrss_acquire.py and test_qrss_lacquire.py (A-4..A-7, incl. the Gamma/Gumbel calibration tests) against C++.
risks: A great many tuned interacting constants and order-dependent arbitration (stable sorts by -lam or (p, -lam), first-found wins in dedup); any reordering changes which candidate gate V sees first and so the receive time and result.

A1 threshold needs gammainccinv with a non-integer shape (no special-function library in native/): either freeze 28.296115129334837 for M=11 (A1_SPAN_S fixes M) or port an incomplete-gamma inverse; A2 needs only integer-shape Q(k,x), which has a closed form.

CubicSpline not-a-knot on complex data and the iterative refinement (2 rounds of phase-line + parabola timing) must be reproduced closely; refinement uses the channel's sigma2/local exactly as Python does.

Phase/timing conventions are contracts with track/ltrack: tau0 in CH samples from nominal t0; PreambleHit.phase relative to the exact f_mix mix at t0, with L taking out f_p*tau0 and the pilot's own advance while CE does not take out 2*pi*df*tau0; drift chirp d/120*t^2 turns about t0.
_a2_input/lead_in_span align i_a to a multiple of 16 with Python floor-mod (negative i_a when the capture starts late) so the CH grid matches make_chan's; C++ truncating % breaks it.

L-specific logic: A2-L mixes up by f_p = 12207/970 Hz, pilot hypotheses 3.1-22.1 Hz above each line, hint tries at f and f+-1 Hz when A1 is below threshold, drop_band_owned with 3 T_L timing, merge across waveforms within 5 Hz and T_L/2; A3 shape test excludes callsign windows and pre-keying frames (needs FrameSpec.keyed_start_pos, keyed_end_pos, window_spans_s from frame.py/lframe.py).
lead_in_span uses the CE matched filter for both waveforms and noise_psd(ch[have]) on a gap-compacted channel; easy to 'fix' and diverge.
A3 memory (~200 MB peak at FULL in Python) is a problem on Android: run the Viterbi per channel and keep float32.
TBD_GUMBEL tables are measurements tied to the exact spectrogram/CFAR/Viterbi; any C++ deviation in E's normalisation invalidates the false-alarm calibration (re-run A-7 against C++).
np.einsum, hypot-based np.abs and polyfit/lstsq are not bit-reproducible even across Python machines; parity must be tolerance-based for A2/A3 continuous values.

notes:
1) Where ChanCapture lives: it is in sstvae/qrss/track.py (L159-240), not frontend.py, but in C++ it belongs with the front end. ChanCapture(ch complex64 @250 Hz, fs, t0_index = CH index of nominal t0, f_mix Fraction, keep float32 or None, exclude_hz, a cached _psd). noise_psd_at() runs frontend.noise_psd once with NOISE_WIN_S=10, exclude_hz moved to channel coordinates and audio_hz = 1500 + f_mix. Windows that are less than 90% real samples are replaced by the median of the good ones, and the result is linearly interpolated. make_chan() aligns i_a down to a multiple of 16 (floor-mod) and pads i_b to a whole number of 16s, zero-pads outside the capture, and channelises fe and keep with n0=i_a. PassResult stores ch, ch_fs, ch_t0_index and f_mix_hz for EM, so the channeliser's output is persisted on disk and becomes a contract.

2) Python numeric semantics to replicate exactly. Without them, most of the "near-bit-exact" opportunities below are lost:
- Use half-to-even rounding: Python round and np.rint, i.e. std::nearbyint, never std::round.
- Use floor-div and floor-mod for possibly negative sample indices.
- Follow NEP 50: float32 * python float stays float32.
- numpy complex/real division is Smith's algorithm, which equals multiplying by the reciprocal. Measured: per-part division differs in 43% of samples.
- np.median of an even count returns the mean of the two middle values in the input dtype.
- np.abs(complex) is hypot.
- argmax/argmin return the first index.
- Viterbi ties go to the first step in -2..+2 (strict '>').
- scipy ndimage mode 'reflect' is half-sample symmetric. It matters for spectral_shape's median filter; for the blanker's max-filter dilation it is equivalent to zero padding.
- np.interp's exact formula.
Build this code with -ffp-contract=off: clang on arm64 (macOS, Android) fuses x*x+y*y by default.

3) Quantisation points make cross-implementation near-bit-exactness realistic up to A1/A3. They are:
- FE complex64
- FE' complex64, keep float32, level float32
- CH complex64
- spectrogram float32
- E float32
- A1 stat float32
Measured: OA vs direct convolution gave 1 mismatching complex64 sample in 240k; live.StreamFE vs batch gave 0; numpy vs scipy.fft spectrograms gave 0 of 448k float32 bins. Recommendation: freeze every filter table into generated, committed data (the same generator and CI-staleness pattern as config.hpp and the golden vectors) rather than re-deriving firwin/kaiser in C++. scipy's Kaiser uses Cephes i0; native's bessel_i0 is a power series. The tables are:
- _FE_TAPS: 255 taps, Kaiser 8 at 1250 Hz.
- The resample_poly 1:16 filter: 321 taps, Kaiser 10, cutoff 1/16.
- The notch: 2001 taps, Hann at 0.6 Hz.
- The CE matched filter: 121 taps.
- The L matched filter: 243 taps.
- The Hann windows of 16000 and 2500 points.
- The A1 threshold for M=11: 28.296115129334837.
- The TBD_GUMBEL tables.
native/core/dsp already has pocketfft, a Hamming-only firwin, kaiser, resample_poly (Kaiser 5 only), fftconvolve_valid and next_fast_len. Missing are:
- firwin with a Kaiser or Hann window
- resample_poly with a window argument
- oaconvolve/fftconvolve in mode 'same' (complex input, real taps)
- freqz at arbitrary frequencies
- a numpy-semantics median and selection
- ndimage median/max filters
- a not-a-knot complex CubicSpline
- incomplete gamma (closed form for integer k)

4) Live-path reproducibility is not decided in these modules. live.capture_prepare fills unheard spans and the future with complex Gaussian noise from np.random.default_rng(q), i.e. PCG64 plus numpy's ziggurat standard_normal. Acquisition over a live capture is bit-reproducible against Python only if C++ ports PCG64 and numpy's ziggurat. Otherwise, test parity on fully heard captures and accept statistical parity live. The model's own CLAUDE.md rule (no default_rng in format modules) does not cover this receiver-side use.

5) The rule switch: rules.EDGE_NOISE is the env var QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE, read on every noise_psd call and inherited by the listener's spawned end-of-slot process. The C++ port needs the same switch (an env var or a config flag passed through) if old-vs-new comparisons are to stay possible. GATING (QRSS_OLD_GATING) is receiver.py's.

6) The passband store is a cross-process and cross-implementation file format. Python's qrss_decode --retro and em.retro_detect read what the live listener wrote. Keep its layout byte-compatible:
- meta.json with fs and scale
- fe_<hour>.i16: (3600*4000, 2) int16 interleaved I/Q, fixed size and sparse
- fe_<hour>.json: merged [[lo,hi]] ranges
- fe_<hour>.flac: 2-channel PCM_16 at 4000 Hz, verified before the raw file is deleted
Platform hazards:
- Windows: sparse files are not the default, and replacing or deleting a mapped file fails.
- FLAC needs libFLAC or libsndfile bundled for 5 desktop packages plus Android; Qt has no codec. A header-only decoder such as dr_flac covers reading only.
- Writes clip to +-32767. Captures with a peak above 16383 counts are attenuated by a power of 2, and that gain is returned, not stored.

7) Interfaces a port must preserve:
- Capture(fe complex64 @4 kHz, q, t0_index = FE index of 900q+1 s, fs). WAVs start at t0-12 s by qrss_transmit convention.
- acquire(cap, spec or (CE spec, L spec), live_only, preprocessed, hints, where a hint is f or (f, waveform)) returns an Acquisition. Acquisition.detections(spec) returns Detections that each carry their waveform, method (preamble/hint/tbd), path (FreqPath), Timing (tau0 in CH samples from nominal t0, cov diag) and a3_z.
- receiver.prepare is blank then normalise. A CH-rate (250 Hz) capture passes through unprepared, and the spectrogram then uses 1000-point frames.
- The A1/A2/A3 front end works on FE' = normalise(blank(fe)), so its noise has median power 1 (E|n|^2 = 1/ln 2).

8) Performance and memory for planning (Python on this box):
- audio_to_fe: 0.18 s per 60 s of audio. blank: 0.07 s. normalise: 0.02 s.
- One CE A2 search: about 0.2 s, dominated by the 21x1251x660 einsum and the spline refinement. One L search: 0.04 s.
- Joint live acquisition on SHORT: 1.85 s for 35 A2 searches.
- A3: 0.3 s on SHORT, 0.8 s on MEDIUM, about 2.3 s on FULL.
- A3 peaks at about 200 MB on FULL because the whole 47+-channel x 896 x 321 stack goes to float64. On Android, restructure it per channel.
- Caches (lru_cache on noise-response tables keyed by float audio_hz) must be thread-safe in C++: the live listener runs workers, and in Python the end-of-slot receive is a separate process.

9) Suggested C++ split:
- core/qrss/frontend: audio_to_fe as a streaming block-with-halo, as live.StreamFE does (ALIGN 16, HALO 128), which proved bit-identical to batch; blank; normalise; channelise; ChanCapture/make_chan; noise_psd and its tables.
- core/qrss/passband_store: Qt-free, with a FLAC seam so that a no-FLAC build still reads and writes raw hours.
- core/qrss/acquire: A1, A2, lead-in, A3, arbitration.
Python stays the oracle via pybind and pytest --native substitution. The fast tier of tests/test_qrss_frontend.py, test_qrss_acquire.py, test_qrss_lacquire.py and test_qrss_rules.py then becomes the acceptance suite.

- sequences.preamble_ce/preamble_l (SHA-256 bit streams)
- ce.pulse/_rrc and PULSE_NORM, lwave.PULSE_NORM

- types (CarrierCandidate, Detection, FreqPath, Timing)
- dsp.to_baseband and wrap_cycles, which are already native
These constants should come through the generated config header, never hand-copied.

modules.purpose: CE carrier/timing/complex-gain tracker and gate V. Turns a 250 Hz per-signal channel (ChanCapture, made from the 4 kHz FE by make_chan through frontend.channelise) into the per-position quantities that demod and cwid read: z_d (the channel derotated along a frequency path), m (symbol matched filter at every grid position), c/sf (mean-waveform template and self-noise), u/P (RTS-smoothed complex gain and its error variance), N (noise from 10 s PSD windows), psi (unblanked share). The pipeline is factorised as decision D16. (1) Frequency path: PathFn is a weighted LSQ cubic B-spline with knots every 10 s (or 60 s), extended linearly outside its span, falling back to a weighted line. derotate integrates f(t)-f_mix in float64 turns with cumsum, wraps the result and multiplies by exp(-2 pi j turns). (2) Timing is affine plus an optional quadratic: tau0 + p*sps*(1+ppm e-6) + gamma*(p/n_pos)^2. fit_timing does the coarse search: Im(MF{z_d conj(LP(z_d))}) is correlated with the known symbols over a lag x clock-error grid, for each of 4 carrier low-passes, then _segment_timing walks 20 s segments outward. refine_timing runs a numeric-Hessian Newton on the known-symbol likelihood. (3) symbol_mf is a polyphase RRC matched filter with 512 table points per CH sample and linear interpolation. (4) Measurements are mu = m/(c psi) with R = (N + kappa Pu sf)/|c psi|^2 + 1e-3 Pu. (5) A 2-state constant-velocity complex Kalman filter plus RTS smoother, with q chosen by maximum innovation log-likelihood over a 13-point Doppler grid. (6) The path is re-centred from u_hat's residual rotation in 30 s windows. Gate V (verify, verify_track and z_ref_stat) tracks with the known symbols withheld and accepts at Z_ref > 6. Path measurement on the frame itself: refine_path (20 s then 5 s FFT carrier lines) and line_path (60 s spectra stacked over drift hypotheses). report produces the TrackReport (offset, drift, wander, Doppler, ppm, SNR2500, slip_free).

fit_timing FFT cross-correlation. A blind search covers +-2.5 s of lags (~1255). nfft = next pow2 of nlag+ng: 2^19 for FULL, smaller for SHORT. One rfft per LP; one rfft of a bincount-scattered linearly-interpolated template plus one irfft per clock-error hypothesis. deltas step 0.2/n_pos over +-250 ppm: 147 for FULL, 21 for SHORT, times 4 LPs, so 588 rfft/irfft pairs of 2^19 on FULL. A direct gather path is used when nlag <= 64
np.median: noise sigma^2 = median(x^2)/0.4549, the chi2(1) median; noise PSD windows; the erasure median
np.argmax/argmin peak picking, parabolic 3-point interpolation (_parabola, clipped to +-0.5)
np.linalg.lstsq: 2-column weighted line in _segment_timing, with outlier rejection at 3 sigma

refine_timing: central-difference gradient/Hessian, h=0.3 CH samples, in 2-D (tau0, slip) or 3-D (+gamma when n_pos*t_sym > 10000 T, i.e. MEDIUM/FULL). np.linalg.eigh for the positivity check, solve for the step (clip +-1.5), inv for the covariance, Jacobian diag(1, 1e6/(n_pos sps), 1)

complex Kalman filter: state [u, u'], F=[[1,1],[0,1]], real symmetric covariance (a,b,c), Q = q Pu [[1/3,1/2],[1/2,1]], P0 = diag(10Pu+1e-30, 0.1Pu). loglik = -sum(log S + |inn|^2/S). RTS smoother with 2x2 inverse via det (det<=0 -> 1e-300). Pure Python scalar loops over ~59k positions (FULL)
boxcar smoothing: np.convolve with edge padding; 32 positions for local Pu, 99 positions (3 s) in report

np.fft.fft with Hann window for carrier lines: 20 s segments n=5000 -> nfft 65536; 5 s n=1250 -> 16384; line_path 60 s n=15000 -> 65536, spectra normalised by their median and stacked over 81 coarse drift hypotheses (+-0.4 Hz/min, step 0.01) plus a fine pass, using np.round (half-to-even) bin shifts
_recenter: weighted phase-increment estimator sum u[k+1] conj(u[k]) |u[k]|^2 over 990-position (30 s) windows, then np.angle
_tau_of_rx: 3 fixed-point iterations inverting the quadratic timing

templates: ce.phase_grid/var_grid (scipy.signal.upfirdn up=485 down=64 with the 7761-tap PULSE_TABLE, exact grid), ce.cw_phase_turns (Hann-CDF integral, FSK -16.495 Hz), ce.matched_filter (exact integer-table MF, width 2*3880/64+2), ce.phase_at (closed-form 17-offset RRC) in remove_spread

Fraction arithmetic for f_mix (1/64 Hz grid)
modules.determinism: No RNG and no hashing in this module. Floating-point results are tolerance-class: oaconvolve, rfft/irfft and fft go through pocketfft/ducc FFTs; einsum and np.convolve dot products use SIMD/BLAS summation order; pairwise np.mean/np.sum; libm exp/sin/cos and Python complex exp; numpy complex division (Smith) differs from std::complex operator/ (__divdc3). The LSQ spline QR is tolerance-class too. Bit-exact is realistic only for the scalar Kalman/RTS recursion given identical inputs (sequential double ops; requires -ffp-contract=off because clang fuses a*b+c into FMA on arm64 by default, and GCC C++ defaults to fast), and for cumsum. End-to-end, ulp-level differences feed discrete decisions that can flip near ties or thresholds: the 13-way argmax in select_q, the lag x ppm argmax in fit_timing with runner-up exclusion, segment acceptance c>=4, |dn|<=300e-6, ptp>=300, Newton exit |step|<0.01, refine exit moved<0.02, recenter thresholds 0.002/0.02 Hz, _carrier_lines ratio>=10/40, gate V Z_ref>6, and _lead_supported. So end-to-end parity is tolerance plus statistical (R1/R7/R13-style acceptance), not bit-exact. Note that Python round() and np.round are half-to-even (use nearbyint).
modules.io_state: No file I/O, threads or subprocesses. State: module-level caches _Q_GRIDS and _MF_TABLES (unbounded dicts keyed by float t_sym, read-only arrays), ChanCapture._psd (lazy noise-PSD cache), and lru caches in frame.layout and frontend. TrackResult is mutated in place: track's closures (measure/run) rebuild m, psi, N, meas, u, P, q, timing, freq, z_d; erase() zeroes psi; receiver sets z_ref; demod.extract can replace m. The env var QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE (rules.EDGE_NOISE) changes noise_psd, and with it N, R, SNR and gate V, indirectly. A debug print sits behind _DEBUG_SEG=False.
modules.parity_test_idea: Use golden vectors with oracle injection per stage, taken from a stored PassResult .npz (it carries ch complex64, ch_t0_index, f_mix_hz; EM's capture_from_pass path), e.g. SHORT at -12 dB steady and with mpp-like fading plus +-100 ppm. Dump from Python: PathFn evals at fixed t, z_d, symbol_mf m at a fixed Timing, psi, N, templates c/sf for round A and round B classes, mu/R, select_q's 13 logliks, kalman_rts u/P/ll at a fixed q, fit_timing's (tau0, ppm, z) and n_best list, refine_timing's result with cov, and final TrackResult timing/q/u/P, z_ref, TrackReport. Compare C++ stage by stage, feeding Python's inputs to each stage: u/P rel 1e-10, chosen q index equal, timing within 1e-6 CH samples, z_ref and report within 1e-6, spline coefficients within 1e-9. Also, as `pytest --native` does for the modem, substitute kalman_rts, select_q, symbol_mf, fit_timing, track and verify into sstvae.qrss.track and run tests/test_qrss_track.py, test_qrss_receiver.py and test_qrss_spread.py (slow tier included: R1 genie within 0.2 dB, R7 timing 0.02 T rms, KS test that gate V Z_ref is N(0,1) on noise).
risks: The LSQ cubic B-spline (scipy make_lsq_spline, QR) must be reimplemented, including the Schoenberg-Whitney detection: scipy returns nan/inf coefficients (no exception) for knot spans without data, and PathFn then falls back to a line. A normal-equations/Cholesky port could return finite garbage there, or the reverse.

Near-tie discrete decisions (select_q argmax, fit_timing peak/runner-ups, segment walk thresholds, Newton termination, refine/recenter loop exits) amplify ulp differences into divergent u_hat and timing. Parity tests must inject oracle intermediates.

Hard-coded magic numbers are scattered through the code: 0.4549 (chi2 median), 0.55 and 1/3 in _lead_supported, 0.1 in refine_timing's var, h=0.3, step clip 1.5, det floor 1e-300, 4.0 segment Z, ptp 300, 300e-6, 0.002/0.02 Hz, 10*Pu and 1e-2 initial covariance. Generate them into a header rather than retyping.
Q_SPREADS_HZ = np.round(np.logspace(...), 5) and Q_GRID = x**3 (pow) can differ in the last ulp across libms. Emit them as hex-float constants (gen_config_header-style), as with config.hpp.
Python round() and np.round are half-to-even, so C++ must use nearbyint, not std::round. Affected: lowpass length, window sizes, line_path bin shifts, n3=99, n_w=990.

Performance hot spots, measured in Python: one SHORT pass (gate V + round A + round B) takes 4.6 s, of which 1.48 s is 152 _kf_forward calls and 1.40 s is 62 symbol_mf calls. One blind FULL fit_timing takes 14.8 s (588 FFT pairs of 2^19), and gate V can call it up to 4 times per candidate (3 path bases plus n_best=8). Use pocketfft r2c with plan caching; POCKETFFT_CACHE_SIZE=16 may need checking against the new lengths 2^19/65536/16384/2500.
Thread safety: the module caches and ChanCapture._psd are lazily filled. The C++ live listener receiving several slots concurrently needs thread-safe statics or immutable precomputed tables.

Wide dependency surface. It needs ports of ce (format: upfirdn grid synthesis, cw_phase_turns, phase_at, matched_filter, PULSE_TABLE/G0), frame.layout/spread_symbols, frontend (channelise, channelise_keep, noise_psd, which depends on firwin/freqz responses and the EDGE_NOISE env-var rule), lwave.PULSE_NORM/G0 for L, and dsp.wrap_cycles.

~30 symbols, private ones included, are shared with ltrack. A straight CE-only port would force L to duplicate them. Design the C++ core waveform-parametrised (MfTable and q_grid per t_sym) with CE orchestration separate.

Stale doc: refine_timing's docstring says track passes a known-withheld u_ref, but track() does not. It only chooses q without the known symbols and then runs the KF with them. Port the code, not the doc.

Erased or unheard spans must be filled with noise, not zeros. Zeros drive the gain estimate toward infinity or denormals. Never build with -ffast-math, FTZ or DAZ: demod's erasure logic and the u2<=0 guards rely on IEEE denormal behaviour.

Complex arithmetic: std::complex operator* and operator/ follow C99 Annex G (NaN/inf recovery, __divdc3 scaling), which differs from numpy's in the last ulp and on inf/NaN. Use -fcx-limited-range or hand-rolled arithmetic for parity.

Dead or test-only code that need not be ported, or can go to a test library: PathFn._inside, _DEBUG_SEG, kalman_rts(causal=True) (used only in tests; the docstring calls it the live filter), genie_track (needs channel.Truth).

modules.purpose: CE symbol extraction from a TrackResult (design 6.6). For each stream symbol k at position p: y = Im(m_p conj(u_p)) / (K_LIN |u_p|^2 psi_p), with s2n = [N/2 + (A0^2+K^2) P/2] / (K^2 |u|^2 psi^2) and s2 = s2n + D_PASS (0.0466, the pinned per-pass phase-modulation distortion). A symbol is erased (y=0, s2=inf) when psi < 0.5 or |u|^2 < 1e-4 * median|u|^2 over the frame. For a spread-header frame whose header is unknown, the data is corrected for the gain exp(-beta^2 rho/2) and the extra variance rho. Calibration: kappa is estimated twice, from reference residuals against Im(c)/K and from data E y^2 = 1 + D_PASS + kappa s2n, over symbols with s2n < max(4, 4*median). The two are combined by inverse variance, shrunk toward 1 (prior sd 0.5), clamped to [0.5, 2], with suspect flagged when the raw estimate lies outside by 3 sd. Block estimators per precoder block (64/32/8...) undo the scrambler and WHT: 'plain' gives a = c*WHT(y), v = mean(s2); 'joint' gives d = 1/(1+s2), a = c*WHT(d y)/mean(d), v = [mean(d^2 s2) + mean((d-g)^2)]/g^2. Output is z, w = 1/v as float32[n_data] in air order. The 2474 header LLRs are 2y/s2 on the coded header symbols plus, while the header is unknown, the spread-header LLRs folded mod 2474 over the data symbols.
public_api: D_PASS=0.0466, D_REF=0.009, KAPPA_RANGE=(0.5, 2.0), KAPPA_PRIOR_SD=0.5, KAPPA_S2_MAX=4.0, KAPPA_S2_REL=4.0, U_MIN_REL=1e-4 (also imported by ldemod)
