data_estimates(tr) -> (y, s2n, extra)  # spread-header gain correction when classes.spread_rho > 0
spread_llr(y, s2, spec) -> float64[2474]  # 2 sqrt(rho) y/(s2+1) * spread_whitener, bincount mod 2474
calibrate(tr) -> (kappa: float, suspect: bool)  # CE only (asserts)
block_estimate(y, s2, q, estimator='joint'|'plain') -> (z air-order float64[n], v float64[n])

extract(m, track, spec, q, estimator='joint', *, calibrate_kappa=True) -> (z float32[n_data], w float32[n_data], llr float32[2474 or 0], diag dict(kappa, suspect, y, s2, y_hdr, estimator, llr_block, llr_spread))

np.median (erasure threshold, s2 bound), np.mean (numpy pairwise summation) in calibrate
inverse-variance combination, shrinkage, clamp; sqrt
exp(-beta^2 rho/2) with beta=0.8 and rho=SPREAD_RHO 0.054, giving g=0.98287
precoder.wht: blockwise orthonormal Sylvester FWHT over runs of 64/32/16/8/4/2/1 blocks (50600 = 790x64 + 32 + 8), divided by sqrt(M); precoder.block_index/block_sizes
np.bincount per-block sums (gam, v) and LLR fold mod N_HDR_BITS=2474
sequences.scrambler(q, n) and sequences.spread_whitener(n): SHA-256 counter-mode +-1 streams, which need a SHA-256 in the Qt-free core (none exists in native/core today)
float32 cast of outputs
modules.determinism: No RNG. Hash-based sequences (SHA-256 scrambler keyed by uint64_be q, and the spread whitener) are exact. WHT butterflies, bincount and elementwise ops are exact given the same order. np.mean uses pairwise summation (replicable but fiddly) and np.median is order-independent, so kappa is ulp-close but not guaranteed bit-equal. Final float32 z/w/llr should be bit-identical except for rare rounding-boundary cases. Hard decisions: the erasure thresholds (psi < 0.5, u2 < 1e-4 med), the kappa clamp and the suspect flag (3 sd outside [0.5, 2]). These flip only at exact boundaries. Given identical TrackResult arrays, a C++ port can reach <=1 float32 ulp on z/w/llr.
modules.io_state: Pure functions, except that extract() overwrites track.m when an m other than track.m is passed (a side effect EM relies on). No I/O, no threads, no env. Relies on lru caches in frame.layout, precoder._runs/_block_sizes and sequences._spread_whitener.
modules.parity_test_idea: Inject saved TrackResults: dump m, u, P, N, psi, c, pos and classes (mu, nu, known, spread_rho) from Python round A (header unknown, spread_rho > 0) and round B (header known) on SHORT, MEDIUM, a TINY pass (no header, empty llr) and a format-version-1 frame (hdr_rho=0). Require y/s2n within 1e-13 relative; kappa/suspect equal (kappa within 1e-12); z/w/llr float32 within 1 ulp and >= 99.9% bit-identical, for both 'joint' and 'plain'. block_estimate fuzz on random y/s2 with random erasures (inf s2) and lengths 50600/16384/4096/1024/37 must be bit-exact. Separately check scrambler and spread_whitener against Python for several q. Then substitute demod.extract via pytest --native and run tests/test_qrss_receiver.py and test_qrss_spread.py.
risks: Needs SHA-256 in sstvae_core (Qt-free) for scrambler and spread_whitener. Today only Qt's hash is used, in qt_fetcher; nothing in core.

D_PASS and D_REF are calibrated constants, pinned from ce.loopback_stats. They must be re-measured whenever the CE modulator changes (beta, pulse), the same discipline as the SSTVAE 0.794 gain note. Keep a single source and generate it.
extract has a mutation side effect on track.m. Make it explicit in the C++ API.
calibrate is CE-only (assert); ldemod reuses its constants plus block_estimate and spread_llr. Port those as waveform-neutral helpers.
Denormal gains: the code avoids dividing by tiny |u|^2. A port built with FTZ/DAZ or -ffast-math changes which symbols are erased.
LLR length depends on spec.has_header (0 for TINY); header LLRs feed the polar decoder (another group), so sign stability near 0 matters only statistically.

modules.purpose: Callsign-window reader (spec 2.7, design 6.7). Each window is 192 Morse units: 2 CE symbols or 1 L symbol, 60.625 ms each. The call sits in units 8..183. FSK keying puts key-down at the carrier -16.495 Hz (one cycle per unit below); OOK switches the carrier on in units 5..183. _unit_sums integrates the derotated channel tr.z_d over each unit's receive span [ceil(na), nb), mapped through the tracker's timing (rx_index), at 0 Hz (X0) and at -1 cycle/unit (X1, twiddled by exp(2 pi j x)). The noise variance per sum is noise_psd*fs*count. window_soft gives quadratic soft values: (|X1|^2-|X0|^2)/(sqrt2 s2) for FSK, and (|X0|^2 - s2 - E/2)/s2 for OOK, with E from the plain units. window_llr gives exact Rician per-unit LLRs, ln I0(2a|X1|/s2) - ln I0(2a|X0|/s2) for FSK. The amplitude a comes from a 15-unit boxcar of |X0|^2+|X1|^2-2s2; L uses only call units. OOK uses ln I0(2a|X0|/s2) - a^2/s2. read_ml is a maximum-likelihood dynamic programme over the 37-character Morse alphabet: 1..8 chars, starting exactly at unit 8, exact 3-unit gaps. Its margin is the LLR against the nearest rival (DP rerun with each read character forbidden), capped by the no-call LLR. read accepts at margin >= 6. match returns Z = sum s_u soft_u / sqrt(176 n) for a known call, and keying_type decides FSK vs OOK. Windows and passes add before reading.
public_api: CALL_UNITS = slice(8, 184); PLAIN_UNITS = units 0..4 and 184..191; AMP_SMOOTH_UNITS = 15; READ_LLR_MIN = 6.0
window_soft(ch, ch_fs, track, spec, ook=False) -> float32[n_win, 176]  # ch None = track.z_d
window_llr(ch, ch_fs, track, spec, ook=False) -> float32[n_win, 176]
read_ml(llr, max_chars=8, margin=False) -> (callsign|None, Z) or (callsign|None, Z, margin)
read(llr, ook=False) -> str | None
match(soft, callsign) -> float
keying_type(ch, track, spec, callsign=None) -> 'fsk' | 'ook'  # L always 'fsk'
decode_units(hard) -> str | None  # run-length decoder, tests only
_unit_sums(tr, spec, z=None) -> (X0, X1, s2) each (n_win, 192)  # private, the core measurement
numeric_primitives: per-unit sums over ~15-16 CH samples (2*7.578 for CE, 15.156 for L), with a complex twiddle exp(2 pi j (n-na)/(nb-na)) per sample; sample membership n in [ceil(na), nb) with nb exclusive
rx_index (affine+quadratic timing) at unit edges, giving fractional CH indices
ChanCapture.noise_psd_at (np.interp of 10 s noise_psd windows)
boxcar np.convolve(ones(15), 'same') per window row, with an edge count normaliser (call-units-only mask for L)
scipy.special.i0e: ln I0(x) = log(i0e(x)) + x (Cephes Chebyshev expansions)

Morse DP: 37 patterns (sorted: '/', '0'-'9', 'A'-'Z'; lengths 1..19 units). Gains g[c, start] = 2*sum of LLR over on-units. Characters of equal length are collapsed by argmax (first index wins). best[k, e] for k <= 8 and n=176, transitions st = e + 3. Traceback from the row-major argmax over (k, e). Margin: up to 8 extra DPs with one (char, start) forbidden
sqrt normalisers (sqrt(176 n), sqrt(size)), dot products
modules.determinism: No RNG and no hashing. _unit_sums depends on exp() per sample (libm), on interp of the noise PSD, and on float rx_index unit edges, where a sample sitting exactly on an edge could change unit. All tolerance-class, ~1e-14 relative. i0e: porting Cephes' coefficients and evaluation order gives near-bit agreement apart from exp. The DP itself is exact given equal inputs, but argmax tie-breaking must be replicated: first maximum in sorted char order per length, and row-major (fewest characters first) in _trace. The gain sums of >= 8 terms use numpy pairwise summation, ulp-level. Hard decisions: the read() margin >= 6, keying_type z > 3, and the receiver's match Z > 6. They are stable except near those thresholds or in exact ties.
modules.io_state: Pure. Module-level constant tables (_INV, _CHARS, _PATS) are built at import from morse.MORSE. Reads tr.z_d, tr.chan (t0_index, fs, noise_psd_at; this fills ChanCapture's lazy PSD cache) and tr.timing. No I/O, threads or env vars, except indirectly the EDGE_NOISE rule through noise_psd.
modules.parity_test_idea: (1) From a stored SHORT pass with known FSK and OOK keying, at -12 and -6 dB: dump tr.z_d, timing, t0_index and the noise PSD table. Compare C++ X0/X1/s2 (rel 1e-12), window_soft and window_llr (float32 within 1 ulp), match Z (1e-9) and keying_type (equal). (2) Run read_ml/read fuzz over ~10k synthetic LLR stacks: random valid calls of 1-8 chars from the 37-char alphabet, 1-8 rows, a range of mu, plus pure noise. Require identical text, Z within 1e-12 relative, margin within 1e-9 absolute, and identical read() accept/reject; drop cases whose top-two DP scores are within 1e-9. (3) decode_units round trip over the same calls. (4) Substitute via pytest --native and run tests/test_qrss_cwid.py (the R18 slow tier included) and test_qrss_smoke.py's -6 dB window read.
risks: ln I0 needs an exponentially scaled Bessel I0. std::cyl_bessel_i is absent from libc++ (macOS, Android NDK) and overflows for large x anyway. Port Cephes i0e (two Chebyshev tables, 30 + 25 coefficients) and test it against scipy over [0, 1e4].
Argmax tie-break semantics in _dp and _trace must match numpy's first-occurrence order, or margin and read can differ on symmetric or degenerate inputs.

The DP's timing model is rigid: exact 1/3-unit elements, 3-unit gaps, first char at unit 8. That is a format assumption tied to morse.keying_units. Use QRSS's own Morse table, which rejects characters outside [A-Z0-9/] and allows at most 8. Do not reuse native/core/dsp/morse.cpp, whose table is lenient and drops unknown characters.
OOK on an L frame must raise, as _fsk_only does. L uses only call units for the FSK amplitude.

Unit-edge sample membership uses ceil(na) and strict < nb on float values computed from timing. A C++ rx_index that differs in the last ulp can move an edge sample, giving a small LLR difference. Keep the exact expression order of rx_index.
decode_units is not on the receive path (tests only). Porting it is optional.

notes:
Cross-cutting notes for planning the port of track/demod/cwid:

1. **Port order is forced by dependencies.** track needs:
   - ce (format): upfirdn grid synthesis with up=485, down=64 and the 7761-tap PULSE_TABLE; var_grid; cw_phase_turns; the closed-form phase_at; the exact matched_filter; G0.
   - frame.layout, pos_of and spread_symbols.
   - frontend: channelise (1/64 Hz rational mixer, resample_poly by 16 with kaiser(10), 321 taps), channelise_keep, and noise_psd (2500-point periodograms; the firwin/freqz aliased response; the env-var rule QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE).
   - lwave.PULSE_NORM and G0 for L tables, and dsp.wrap_cycles.

   demod needs precoder (blockwise FWHT) and sequences (SHA-256 counter-mode scrambler keyed by uint64_be q, and the spread whitener). native/core has no SHA-256 yet. cwid needs track plus morse.

   Suggested order: constants/frame/sequences(+SHA-256)/precoder/morse → ce → frontend → track core (MfTable, symbol_mf, templates, Kalman/RTS/select_q, derotate, PathFn) → demod → cwid → fit_timing/refine_timing → gate V and path refinement (refine_path, line_path) → ltrack/ldemod.

2. **The L receiver is built on track's internals.** ltrack imports ~30 names from track, privates included (`_recenter`, `_tau_of_rx`, `_window_unknown`, `_lowpass`, `_mf_taps`, `_parabola`, `_smooth`, `_flat_path`, `_keying_tuple`, `_Known`). ldemod imports demod's constants, block_estimate and spread_llr. LTrackResult subclasses TrackResult, and cwid reads L windows unchanged through z_d derotated on the pilot.
   - Make the C++ core waveform-parametrised: MfTable per t_sym (CE sps 7.578125, half 62; L sps 15.15625, half 123), q_grid per t_sym, and positions in spec symbols.
   - Keep CE-specific orchestration (track, fit_timing, refine_timing, verify) separate from it.
   - Put the 'refuse the other waveform' guards (_ce_only, _fsk_only) in the C++ API too.

3. **Parity class.** Everything here is tolerance-class end to end:
   - pocketfft vs scipy's FFTs (oaconvolve; 2^19 rfft/irfft; 65536/16384/2500-point FFTs);
   - BLAS/SIMD dot-product order in np.convolve and einsum;
   - numpy pairwise sums in mean and sum;
   - libm exp/sin/cos;
   - numpy's complex division vs std::complex (`__divdc3`, Annex G);
   - scipy's QR LSQ spline.

   Those small differences reach many discrete decisions: select_q's 13-way argmax, fit_timing's lag x ppm argmax and runner-ups, the segment-walk thresholds, Newton and loop exits, gate V's Z>6, cwid's margin>=6 and keying z>3. Adopt the modem port's discipline:
   - golden vectors at every stage boundary, with the Python intermediates injected (one stored PassResult .npz is a self-contained input: ch, ch_t0_index, f_mix);
   - stage tolerances of ~1e-10 to 1e-12 relative;
   - statistical end-to-end acceptance through `pytest --native` substitution of the existing suites (R1 genie within 0.2 dB, R7 timing within 0.02 T, gate V KS test, R18 Morse).

   Bit-exact is realistic only for the scalar Kalman/RTS recursion, the WHT/block_estimate and the Morse DP. Even those need `-ffp-contract=off` on their TUs: clang fuses a*b+c into FMA on arm64 by default, and GCC C++ defaults to `-ffp-contract=fast` even with extensions off. They also need numpy's argmax tie-break order replicated.

4. **Rounding and constants.**
   - Python round() and np.round are half-to-even: use std::nearbyint.
   - Generate Q_SPREADS_HZ (np.round(logspace, 5)), Q_GRID, KAPPA_SELF=0.94, KAPPA_SELF_KNOWN=0.14, D_PASS=0.0466, D_REF=0.009 and the many thresholds into a header (gen_config_header-style, hex floats). Never retype them.
   - D_PASS, KAPPA_SELF and KAPPA_SELF_KNOWN are calibrations (ce.loopback_stats) tied to the CE modulator's beta and pulse. Re-measure them if ce changes.

5. **Performance (Python, measured here).**
   - One SHORT pass (gate V + round A + round B) takes 4.6 s. Of that, 1.48 s is 152 `_kf_forward` calls (pure-Python loops over ~8.4k positions; FULL is ~59k positions, 0.055 s per pass and 0.68 s per select_q) and 1.40 s is 62 `symbol_mf` calls (125 taps per position; 0.57 s on a FULL grid).
   - A blind FULL `fit_timing` takes 14.8 s (588 rfft/irfft pairs of 2^19). Gate V can run it up to 4 times per candidate (3 path bases, then an n_best=8 call). EM's rereceive runs track 2-3 times per pass per round, and the live listener re-receives every refresh.
   - This is the main win of the port. pocketfft (already vendored, plan cache 16) is adequate; check the cache against the new lengths.

6. **State and API semantics to preserve.**
   - TrackResult is mutated in place: track's measure/run closures, erase→psi, extract→m, and receiver setting z_ref.
   - ChanCapture lazily caches its noise PSD, and module caches (_MF_TABLES, _Q_GRIDS) are filled lazily. In C++ make these immutable precomputed tables or thread-safe statics, since live slots run concurrently.
   - Gate V's validity depends on reproducing 'withhold_known' exactly: known mu=0/nu=1 in templates, KAPPA_SELF everywhere, `meas & ~is_known`, and q chosen without them. Z_ref is N(0,1) on noise only if that holds.
   - Unheard spans must be noise-filled, not zero-filled (zeros send u_hat to infinity or denormals). Never build with -ffast-math, FTZ or DAZ.

7. **Dead or test-only code** (can be skipped or kept in a test library): PathFn._inside, _DEBUG_SEG, kalman_rts(causal=True), genie_track (needs channel.Truth from the simulator), cwid.decode_units.

8. **Doc/code mismatch.** refine_timing's docstring says track passes a known-withheld u_ref. track does not: it only selects q without the known symbols, then refines against u_hat computed with them. Port the code's behaviour.

9. **Two pieces of numerics with no ready C++ equivalent need real implementations:**
   - a weighted LSQ cubic B-spline with derivative and linear extrapolation. It must reproduce scipy's behaviour when knot spans hold no data: non-finite coefficients, so the line fallback fires. Use a FITPACK-style banded Givens QR rather than normal equations.
   - an exponentially scaled Bessel I0 (port Cephes i0e; std::cyl_bessel_i is missing in libc++ and overflows).

   The 2x2/3x3 eigh/solve/inv in refine_timing and the 2-column lstsq can be closed-form. native/core/modem.cpp's jacobi_eigen exists but is overkill.

10. **Morse table.** The QRSS Morse table and validation (morse.MORSE: 37 chars A-Z, 0-9, '/', at most 8 chars, rejection rather than dropping) is a format module. The existing native/core/dsp/morse.cpp is a lenient TX-only CW-ID table and must not be reused for the reader.

modules.purpose: Waveform L tracker and gate V. Models the channel as one complex gain u (the data band's reference gain) fed by two measurement streams fused per position by inverse variance. (D) The data band is mixed up by f_p in sender time (z_dd = z_d*exp(+j2pi*(12207/16000)*tau(n)), tau from the timing model), then L's RRC matched filter runs at every grid position against a closed-form template c = g_class*mu with variance N + Pu g^2 (nu + D_class). (P) The pilot is read through an RRC at 2*T_L (pilot_filter: a 489-tap FIR at integer CH samples, then linear interpolation), at even positions only, against lwave.pilot scaled by the clipper's per-section pilot gain. delta, the complex pilot/data ratio, is fitted by shrunk LS (DELTA_PRIOR_SD 0.25) on a pilot-only track and is never fitted inside gate V. The fused (mu,R) go to track's constant-velocity complex Kalman filter and RTS smoother; q is picked on q_grid(L_T_SYM). Timing comes from a coarse fit (fit_timing_l: coherent complex correlation of the known QPSK symbols with MF_D{z_d e^{+j2pi f_p t}}*conj(LP z_d) over lags and clock-error steps of 0.2 T/frame, then 20 s segment line refits in _segment_timing_l), then refine_timing_l (Newton with numeric derivatives, h=0.3 CH samples, on the known symbols' correlation against the pilot-only track, with delta's phase profiled out in closed form). Gate V is verify_l/verify_track_l: track with the known symbols withheld, delta=1, Z_ref = track.z_ref_stat with signature d=c_known, divided by sqrt(max(1,resid_ratio)) so that a CE signal taken for L is refused. report_l moves SNR2500 onto the frame's keyed power.

phasors from turns reduced by floor: data_mix (tau*12207/16000), _lag_phase (lag*12207/242500 per CH sample), _clock_phase (pos*d*12207/16000). Python uses np.exp(2j*pi*turns), not an exact integer reduction

np.median(|x|^2)/ln2 noise scale; np.median(N_pl) in pu_initial

_segment_timing_l: 20 s segments (3/13/33/90 per frame), lags = np.arange(-sps, sps+1e-9, 0.1) (304 values, float-arange semantics), local argmax >= 4.0 plus parabola, weighted 2-column np.linalg.lstsq with 3-sigma outlier refit, |d| <= 300 ppm guard

refine_timing_l: central differences h=0.3 for gradient and Hessian in 2 or 3 dims (gamma only when n_pos*T_L > 303 s), np.linalg.eigvalsh/solve/inv on 2x2/3x3, step clip +-1.5, gradient fallback with 4 halvings, Jacobian rescale of the covariance (ppm = slip/(n_pos*sps)*1e6)

track.kalman_rts / track._kf_forward: constant-velocity complex gain, scalar covariance (a,b,c), Q = q*Pu*[[1/3,1/2],[1/2,1]], loglik with math.log; RTS backward pass; select_q is argmax over a 13-point q_grid(L_T_SYM) (q from 6.9e-9 to 0.187); _q_near takes the 5 neighbours by |log q| distance
_fit_delta: weighted complex LS with Gaussian shrinkage towards 1; _Model.fused: inverse-variance fusion with inf handling, then + R_FLOOR*Pu_loc
track._smooth boxcar n=int(1.0/T_L)=16 with asymmetric edge pad (8 left, 7 right), np.convolve direct; _pu_local caps P at its measured mean
resid_ratio and z_ref_stat: weighted sums over the known symbols

shared via track: derotate (cumsum of f(t)/fs over the whole capture, dsp.wrap_cycles), PathFn (scipy.interpolate.make_lsq_spline cubic with knots every 10/60 s, linear extension, np.polyfit fallback), _recenter (30 s windows, np.angle), refine_path/_carrier_lines (Hann-windowed FFT segments padded 8x to a power of two, np.median over med_band (1, 18) Hz), line_path (60 s FFT stack, drift search in 0.01 Hz/min steps), ChanCapture.noise_psd_at (frontend.noise_psd, 10 s windows, np.interp), report (np.polyfit, smoothed angle)
modules.determinism: No RNG anywhere, and no hashing except through lframe.layout's known_val (SHA-256 sequences), which is exact. Bit-exact parity is not realistic for the module as a whole. The following all introduce ulp-level differences: libm sin/cos/exp (in _rrc, the np.exp phasors, np.hanning and np.sinc), numpy pairwise summation (np.sum and np.mean in norms, fused sums and ell's B), einsum in symbol_mf, the FFTs (scipy's oaconvolve and np.fft), LAPACK (lstsq, eigvalsh, solve, inv), scipy's LSQ B-spline, and the finite-difference Newton with h=0.3. The chain then amplifies those differences. Measured: a 1e-15 relative perturbation of chan.ch moves the final u_hat by 1.2-1.5e-10 relative, tau0 by about 1e-12 CH samples, ppm by 3e-11 to 3e-10, Z_ref by up to 4e-12 and kappa by 2e-12, with q unchanged. The float32 outputs (z, llr) move by at most about 2 float32 ulp, and w does not move (l-tiny at -12 dB and l-short at -20 dB). So tolerance parity of about 1e-8 relative on u, P and m, and 1e-9 samples on timing, is realistic. Discrete decisions can flip only at boundaries: the select_q argmax, the coarse-fit argmax and runner-up ordering, Newton's indefinite-H branch, refine's 'moved < 0.02' break, the recenter thresholds 0.002 and 0.02 Hz, Z_ACCEPT=6 and the per-path early exit in verify_l, and the PSI_MIN/C_MIN masks. The Kalman/RTS recursion itself is plain sequential scalar double arithmetic, so it can be bit-exact given bit-identical (mu, R, q, Pu), provided C++ is built with -ffp-contract=off (no FMA) and the same log().
modules.io_state: No files, threads, environment variables or subprocesses. Module-level caches: _PILOT_TABLE (a lazily filled singleton list), track._MF_TABLES and _Q_GRIDS dicts, lframe.layout lru_cache(16), sequences lru_caches. track_l keeps a local cache keyed on the timing tuple (tau0, ppm, gamma) and on Python object identity id(tr.z_d); C++ needs a generation counter in its place. LTrackResult is mutated in place throughout (timing, freq, z_d, delta, u/P, u_pl/P_pl, m/c, psi). ChanCapture.noise_psd_at fills a lazy _psd cache on the shared channel object; this is shared mutable state if C++ tracks passes on one channel concurrently. The receiver mutates tr.psi afterwards through track.erase. Memory per L_FULL track: z_d about 470k complex128 (about 7.5 MB), and about 20 grid-length arrays of 29,413 + n_lead positions; pilot_wave is evaluated over the whole capture on every timing change and again in _lead_supported_l.
modules.parity_test_idea: Use stage-wise golden vectors from fixed channelised captures: npz of chan.ch, t0_index, f_mix, keep and the noise PSD, plus the Detection, from qrss_fakes.l_scenario for l-tiny and l-short at -12 and -20 dB, one with a lead-in, one with a blanked hole and one with keying known. Compare in order: (1) pilot taps and L MF table entries exactly or to 1e-15. (2) pilot_filter, data_mix, data_mf and pilot_wave at a fixed Timing, to 1e-12 relative. (3) kalman_rts and select_q fed Python's (mu, R, q, Pu), bit-exact target, same q. (4) _fit_delta and refine_timing_l started from a Python LTrackResult state: theta to 1e-9 samples, covariance to 1e-6 relative, and the same None/branch outcome. (5) Blind fit_timing_l on l-short: the same (delta, lag) cell and runner-up set, tau0 within 1e-6 samples, ppm within 1e-6. (6) verify_l plus track_l in round A and round B (header bits and keying known): z_ref and resid_ratio to 1e-8, identical q and n_lead, u and P to 1e-8 relative, delta to 1e-9. Then run tests/test_qrss_ltrack.py and test_qrss_lreceiver.py under a pytest --native substitution. The NATIVE_SUBSTITUTIONS list must name ltrack.kalman_rts, select_q, derotate, freq_path_spline, _smooth, _parabola, _flat_path and _keying_tuple, because ltrack imports them by name.
risks: It cannot be ported in isolation. Roughly 30 names come from track.py: ChanCapture plus frontend.noise_psd, PathFn (make_lsq_spline), derotate, MfTable/mf_table/symbol_mf/psi_at, rx_index/_tau_of_rx, kalman_rts/select_q/q_grid, _smooth, _parabola, _lowpass, _mf_taps, _window_unknown, _recenter, refine_path/_carrier_lines, line_path, z_ref_stat (d_known branch), erase, report, TrackResult and _Known. It also needs lwave.pilot/cw_turns/id_weight/A_ID/PULSE_NORM/G0, lframe.layout/pair (SHA-256 sequences), sequences.qpsk and frame.spread_signs, which takes an LFrameSpec duck-typed. The waveform-neutral track core has to be ported first.

Discrete decisions sit on noisy continuous values: the select_q argmax over 13 q, the fit_timing_l 2-D argmax and its n_best=8 runner-ups, Newton's eigvalsh <= 0 branch and halving, 'moved < 0.02', the recenter thresholds (df_max < 0.002, RECENTER_MIN_HZ 0.02), verify_l's Z_ACCEPT break order across three paths, and the PSI_MIN 0.5 / C_MIN 0.1 masks. A parity test must assert the decisions and avoid boundary scenarios.

Hotspot: a blind fit_timing_l on l-full runs 4 LP cutoffs x (1 + 2 x 73) FFTs of 2^19 points, about 590 FFTs at about 34 ms each in numpy (about 20 s). verify_l can run the blind fit up to four times per candidate (three paths, then n_best=8). pocketfft in C++ is no faster per FFT. The correlation only needs nlag = 1255 lags against a template with about 4,200 nonzeros, so the direct gather form (Python's own nlag <= 64 path) is about 10-20x cheaper and equal up to rounding. Recommend it for C++, with tolerance parity against the FFT path.

The 0.03 Hz lowpass is 33,333 taps over about 470k samples, so C++ must use FFT convolution. scipy oaconvolve 'same' alignment (full[(n-1)/2:]) and zero padding must be reproduced exactly; all tap counts are odd (489, 245, 33333/3333/1001/501).

Float semantics traps: np.arange(-sps, sps+1e-9, 0.1) length (304) and its values start+i*step; np.floor for negative fractional indices (the grid starts at -SPAN-n_lead, n_lead up to 131); Python floor-mod in grid % 2 on negative positions; int() truncation (int(1.0/T_L) = 16); lags derived from math.floor/ceil of +-(2.5*fs+2).

The Python cache key id(tr.z_d) and the in-place mutation of LTrackResult (and of track.m in ldemod) must become explicit ownership and generation counters. The lazy PSD cache on a shared ChanCapture is a race if passes run concurrently.

Calibrated constants are pinned in three modules: ltrack (K_PL_*, L_KEYED_POWER keyed by the frame-name string, which falls back to 1.0 silently), ldemod (G_*_L, PILOT_GAIN_*, G_REF_ABS, D_*_L) and track (C_MIN, PSI_MIN, R_FLOOR, PU_SMOOTH_S, LEAD_KEEP_S, Q_SPREADS_HZ rounded to 5 decimals, MF_RES 512). Hand-copying them invites drift, so they should be generated into a header the way config.hpp is.

_l_only is a bare assert, stripped under python -O, whereas ldemod raises explicitly. tests/test_qrss_lunits.py expects AssertionError messages naming 'ltrack.track_l'. C++ should refuse explicitly with the same wording if the shim is to pass those tests.

refine_timing_l returns None in five places (fewer than 8 known symbols, A <= 0, non-finite theta, no movement without a Hessian). track_l breaks its refinement loop on None, so any C++ divergence in those guards changes the control flow.
genie_track_l needs channel.Truth (u_data, t_pos_s) and np.polyfit. It is test-only: skip it in the app and port it only into the parity harness if wanted.

modules.purpose: Symbol extraction, per-latent noise, kappa calibration and header LLRs for an L pass, as the L counterpart of demod.py. From the tracker's data-band m, u, P, N and psi: r = m*conj(u)/(|u|^2*psi*g) and s2n = (N + g^2 P)/(g^2 |u|^2 psi^2) per latent, with no halving. r is split by lframe.unpair (sqrt(2)*Re and sqrt(2)*Im, interleaved) into two latents per symbol. A symbol is erased where psi < 0.5 or |u|^2 < 1e-4 * median(|u|^2 over pos >= 0). The x scale handles the linear spread header (rho = 0.054). While the header is unknown: y_x = sqrt(1+rho)*y and extra = rho. Once it is known, sqrt(rho)*h is subtracted here, because L cannot de-spread on the channel. s2 = kappa*s2n_x + D_PASS_L*(1+rho) + extra feeds demod.block_estimate (WHT joint or plain). Header LLRs are 2*y_h/(kappa*s2n_h + D_HDR_L), plus spread_llr while the header is unknown. calibrate_l is CE's combination (inverse variance, shrunk to 1 with prior sd 0.5, clamped to [0.5, 2], suspect at 3 sigma outside) over two estimates. The reference estimate allows for each measured reference's pull on u (variance R - P, using tr.meas). The data estimate uses the unit-RMS contract. The module also owns the pinned clipper constants the tracker uses.

numeric_primitives: elementwise complex multiply/divide and |.|^2 with masked division (only usable symbols are divided)
np.median of |u|^2 over pos >= 0 (erasure threshold) and of the finite s2n_x (kappa's s2 bound, max(4, 4*median)); order statistics, exactly reproducible (average of the two middle values for even n)
np.mean (numpy pairwise summation) in the kappa estimates; var formulas 2*res^2/(2n)/den^2 and 2*(1+extra+dx+den)^2/n/den^2
lframe.unpair (sqrt(2) scale, I/Q interleave), np.repeat(s2n, 2), np.searchsorted(known_idx, ref)

demod.block_estimate: blockwise orthonormal WHT (precoder.wht, Sylvester butterflies, blocks 64 then the binary tail, e.g. 790x64+32+8 for 50600), np.bincount sums per block, joint estimator d=1/(1+s2), gamma=block mean of d, v=[mean(d^2 s2)+mean((d-gamma)^2)]/gamma^2; scrambler(q, n) = SHA-256 bits keyed by q as uint64 BE
demod.spread_llr: 2*sqrt(rho)*y/(s2+1) * spread_whitener(n_data) (SHA-256), folded with bincount(i mod 2474); frame.spread_signs
inf/nan handling: np.isfinite masks, np.where with errstate, 1/v where v>0 and finite else 0
float32 casts of z, w and llr (round to nearest even)
modules.determinism: No RNG. The scrambler and spread whitener come from SHA-256 and are exact. Given bit-identical tracker arrays (m, u, P, N, psi, meas, pos, classes.hdr_bits), the module is nearly bit-exact. The elementwise arithmetic, sqrt(2), np.median (an order statistic), the WHT butterflies in fixed order and np.bincount (sequential index-order sums) can all be reproduced exactly. Only np.mean and np.sum (pairwise summation) in kappa_estimates_l and the combination differ at ulp level, about 1e-16 relative in kappa, unless C++ reimplements numpy's pairwise sum. The float32 outputs then agree apart from rare 1-ulp rounding flips. Against the whole receive chain, a 1e-15 perturbation upstream moved z by at most 2 float32 ulp and llr by at most 1 ulp, and left w unchanged. kappa's clamp to KAPPA_RANGE [0.5, 2] and the suspect test are the only discrete branches.
modules.io_state: Pure functions with no IO, threads or environment. extract_l mutates track.m when a different m is passed. It reads tr.spec, pos, gi(), m, u, P, N, psi, meas (optional; it may be None on a genie) and classes.hdr_bits through getattr, so the C++ input struct must allow 'no meas' and 'no hdr_bits'.
modules.parity_test_idea: Serialise LTrackResult inputs to npz: the genie fixture from tests/test_qrss_ldemod.py at s2n 0.02 and 0.3, with the header known and unknown, a real track_l pass of l-short at -12 dB with erase_s spans (psi=0), an l-tiny frame (no header, llr length 0), and a suspect pass (noise scaled 3x). Feed each to the C++ extract_l with both estimators ('joint' and 'plain') and calibrate_kappa on and off. Check: kappa and suspect equal (kappa to 1e-14 relative), y and s2 to 1e-14, z, w and llr float32 within 1 ulp (exact in most elements), and llr_block and llr_spread separately. Then run tests/test_qrss_ldemod.py under --native with ldemod.extract_l, calibrate_l and the by-name imports block_estimate and spread_llr substituted.
risks: It depends on demod.block_estimate and spread_llr, precoder.wht/block_index/block_sizes, sequences.scrambler and spread_whitener (SHA-256) and frame.spread_signs, all shared with CE. Port them once in a common C++ unit and pin the WHT block decomposition and butterfly order.

The y_x/s2n_x spread-header algebra differs between header unknown (scale by sqrt(1+rho), extra = rho, add spread_llr) and header known (subtract sqrt(rho)*h, zero y where s2n is inf). A sign or order slip here still decodes in round A and degrades round B silently. The parity test needs both rounds.

The LLR contract crosses waveforms. Positive means bit 0, coded bit 2j goes on I and 2j+1 on Q of header symbol j, and L and CE LLRs of one segment are summed (associate/EM). The block term is scaled by G_HDR_L, not G_DATA_L.
The kappa reference estimator needs the tracker's meas mask. Python silently uses CE's form when tr.meas is None. The C++ struct must keep that optional, or the gate-V and genie cases change.
inf arithmetic (s2n = inf for erasures, v = inf for empty blocks) relies on IEEE semantics. Never build with -ffast-math.
The pinned calibration constants here (G_*, PILOT_GAIN_*, G_REF_ABS, D_*) are consumed by ltrack and by lwave's loopback_stats documentation. They need one generated source of truth for C++.

notes:
1. The L layer is thin; the work is underneath it. ltrack plus ldemod is about 1,640 Python lines, roughly 40% docstrings, so about 1,600 C++ lines. Both sit on the waveform-neutral core of track.py, which a C++ port needs first: ChanCapture with frontend.noise_psd, PathFn (scipy make_lsq_spline cubic; C++ needs a B-spline basis plus banded LSQ, since native has no linear algebra library), derotate, MfTable/symbol_mf/psi_at, rx_index/_tau_of_rx, kalman_rts/select_q/q_grid, _recenter, refine_path/_carrier_lines, line_path, z_ref_stat, erase, report and the TrackResult base. That core is about 1,000 C++ lines. The L layer also needs the format pieces: lframe.layout (SHA-256 preamble and references), lwave.pilot/cw_turns/id_weight, sequences, precoder.wht, demod.block_estimate/spread_llr. Suggested order: format pieces, then track core (Kalman/RTS first; it is trivially testable), then ldemod (testable early from npz'd track results), then ltrack. LTrackResult extends TrackResult and track.erase/report/z_ref_stat work on it duck-typed, so C++ wants one TrackResult struct with optional L fields (m_pl, c_pl, N_pl, psi_pl, meas_pl, delta, u_pl, P_pl, resid_ratio).

2. The pytest --native substitution needs these names listed explicitly, because ltrack binds them at import: kalman_rts, select_q, derotate, freq_path_spline, _smooth, _parabola, _flat_path, _keying_tuple, plus the constants C_MIN, PSI_MIN, R_FLOOR, PU_SMOOTH_S, LEAD_KEEP_S, RECENTER_MIN_HZ and V_TIMING_TRIES. ldemod binds block_estimate, spread_llr and the KAPPA_*/U_MIN_REL constants from demod, and spread_signs from frame. Everything else is reached as T.xxx and substitutes automatically. The signature trap CLAUDE.md records applies here too. fit_timing_l's and verify_l's first argument named `ch` is actually a ChanCapture, and ch_fs is effectively fixed at 250.

3. The parity floor is measured. A 1e-15 relative perturbation of the CH capture moves u_hat by about 1.5e-10 relative, tau0 by about 1e-12 samples, ppm by up to 3e-10, Z_ref by up to 4e-12 and kappa by 2e-12. q is unchanged, z and llr move by at most about 2 float32 ulp, and w does not move. This held on l-tiny at -12 dB and l-short at -20 dB. Set C++-vs-Python tolerances around 1e-8 relative on the tracker's arrays, and assert discrete decisions separately: q, the argmax cells, the Newton branch, verify accept/reject and the paths tried.

4. Generate the constants rather than hand-copying them. That covers constants.py (format: L_T_NUM 970, T_DEN 16000, L_PILOT_HZ = 12207/970 as a rational, SPAN 8, ALPHA 3/20, CH_FS 250, SPREAD_RHO 0.054, N_HDR_BITS 2474, Z_ACCEPT 6) and the calibrated, non-format receiver constants in track, ltrack, demod and ldemod. The model is native/core/config.hpp's generator and CI staleness gate. There are about 40 constants across four files today, including the 13-point Q_SPREADS_HZ logspace rounded to 5 decimals, L_KEYED_POWER keyed by frame name, and CARRIER_LP_HZ_L.

5. Phase reduction. Python reduces turns by a float multiply then floor (tau*12207/16000, lag*12207/242500), not by exact integer modulo. C++ should copy the same float formula, which gives identical turns, rather than the "exact (n*f) % FS" idiom CLAUDE.md recommends for new DSP: Python is normative and the two differ by about 1e-11 turns. Build the phasors with cos/sin of the reduced angle (as ce._turns_to_phasor does); the remaining difference from numpy's complex exp is ulp level.

6. Performance. Python on 4 shared CPUs: l-tiny verify_l 0.26 s + track_l 0.39 s; l-short 0.73 s + 1.2 s; extract_l 2-3 ms. Hotspots are symbol_mf (einsum gather), the Python-loop _kf_forward (99 calls per pass), psi_at and the pilot filter, and on l-full the blind fit_timing_l: about 590 FFTs of 2^19 points, about 20 s, and up to four blind fits per candidate inside verify_l. The direct sparse gather correlation (1255 lags x about 4,200 template nonzeros x 73 clock steps x 4 cutoffs) is mathematically the same, roughly 10-20x cheaper, and is what C++ (and Android) should use. pilot_wave is re-evaluated over the whole capture (about 470k samples on l-full) on every timing change: cache it per timing.

7. State and threading. The only shared mutable state is ChanCapture's lazy noise-PSD cache and the module-level table caches. The tracker mutates its result in place, the receiver then erases (psi = 0) after tracking, and extract_l may replace track.m. Keep that order: track, erase, extract. Python's id(z_d) cache key becomes a generation counter.

8. Two smaller items. Python's floor-mod (grid % 2) and np.floor on negative positions (the grid starts at -8 - n_lead, n_lead up to 131) and np.arange float lengths (304 lags of step 0.1) are easy off-by-one traps. And only ltrack's L-only guard (`_l_only`) is a stripped-under-`-O` assert, while ldemod's raises; the refusal messages are asserted by test_qrss_lunits.py.

modules.purpose: Orchestrates one slot's reception. It prepares FE' (blanker plus inverse AGC). Acquisition gives candidates, gate V verifies them, and the verified detections are merged, alias-filtered and ghost-filtered. Each detection then gets two-round tracking and demod (round A: track, extract, decode_header, callsign windows; round B: header and keying known, re-track, re-extract). The result is one PassResult per signal. It dispatches CE (track/demod) against L (ltrack/ldemod) per frame. The 'joint' receiver listens for both waveforms at once and compares signals by band centre (CE carrier, or L pilot + L_EXCLUDE_OFFSET_HZ = -9.5 Hz). The module also has small helpers for EM re-receive (detection_from_pass, capture_from_pass), WAV input and the tile confidence trace (confidence_db).

modules.determinism: No RNG. The orchestration is deterministic given its inputs and can be bit-exact for identical stubbed gate/track outputs. Four things limit that. (1) detect/_detect_joint stop verifying after a wall-clock budget_s (time.monotonic). The live end-of-slot path uses FINISH_BUDGET_S=180 with FINISH_MAX_CANDIDATES=12, so a faster C++ gate verifies more candidates and returns a different set; parity runs must pass budget_s=None. (2) Every decision compares tracker floats (f_hz, tau0, z_ref, a3_z, R) against thresholds. The DSP below (resample_poly, splines, Kalman/RTS, polar SCL) can only match to tolerance, so outcomes flip only near boundaries; end-to-end parity is tolerance or statistical. (3) PassResult.uid = f'{q}_{round(f_hz*1000)}_{sha256(float32 z)[:8]}' with Python round (half to even). Any 1-ulp difference in z changes the uid, so uids are not stable across implementations. (4) confidence_db is exact apart from Python's round(x,1) (correctly rounded decimal; not std::round(x*10)/10 at ties) and linspace edges i*(end/n) with the last edge forced to end.
modules.io_state: Pure compute apart from capture_from_wav/receive_wav (8 kHz WAV via sstvae.wavio). Reads env var QRSS_OLD_GATING on every _owned call (rules.old(rules.GATING)); the end-of-slot child process inherits it. Mutates its inputs in place: verified Detection.lead_in_s is set; TrackResult.z_ref is overwritten with det.z_ref. Uses time.monotonic for the budget. No threads, but live.py runs receive_slot in a spawned child process (_FinishProcess), so PassResult/Detection must be picklable or serialisable there.
modules.parity_test_idea: (a) Orchestration, bit-exact. Keep _gate/verify/lead_in_span/_ce_resid_ratio/receive_pass/prepare as std::function seams, mirroring the rx-engine decoder seam. Under a --native substitution, rerun the existing stubbed tests: test_joint_detect_merges_by_centre_and_ghosts_per_waveform, test_joint_receive_slot_takes_each_frame_and_merges_by_centre, test_joint_aliases_and_ghosts_at_each_waveform_symbol, test_suspect_neighbour_of_a_strong_pass_is_dropped and test_qrss_rules _owned cases. Add a randomized generator of candidate lists (f_hz, tau0, z_ref, method in {preamble,hint,tbd}, a3_z, waveform) with stub gate outcomes, asserting identical gate call order, `others` tuples and output lists. Note that the CE-only detect has no _gate seam (it inlines channel_for + track.verify), which the port should fix. (b) decode_header: feed noisy_llr vectors for sum/spread/block × CE/L/FULL_V1/TINY (test_l_header_is_version_2_from_the_sum_or_either_copy) and require identical (header, which LLR kept, frame name). (c) confidence_db on stored PassResults: equal to 0.1 dB, same None pattern. (d) End to end, tolerance: tests/test_qrss_smoke.py's TINY blind pass and SHORT at -6 dB through Python and C++ receive_slot. Compare pass count, frame, waveform, header exactly, f_hz within 0.01 Hz, tau0 within 0.5 CH samples, latent SNR of z within 0.1 dB. Never compare uid.
risks: The wall-clock budget makes results CPU-speed dependent. Live uses 180 s × 12 candidates, so a faster C++ gate finds different signals than Python on the same recording.

Budget accounting is subtle and must be copied exactly. `taken += 1` happens BEFORE the 'already found within MERGE_HZ' skip, and (joint) before the 'waveform not listened for' skip, so those consume max_candidates. `_owned` skips do not count.

The CE-only path and the joint path differ on purpose: CE-only compares f_hz, joint compares centres; ghost rules are per waveform at its own t_sym; the CE residual veto (_ce_resid_ratio) runs only in joint. The docs promise the CE-only receiver is 'call for call' the pre-L one, so a C++ port must not unify the two paths.
decode_header can switch the frame (CE version-1 block -> frame.plain(spec)), which changes PassResult.frame and round B's spec. FULL_SPREADONLY has n_hdr=0 but has_header=True.
Timing.cov shape varies: 2x2 from acquire (preamble), 3x3 from track. It is serialised as-is (timing_cov), so a C++ Timing needs a dynamic shape.
Detection and TrackResult are mutated in place (lead_in_s, z_ref). A C++ port that copies by value must reproduce the visible effects (live keeps SlotState.dets and passes them back as `dets`).

The polymorphic arguments make an attribute-substitution (pytest --native) binding awkward: hints may be floats or (f, waveform) pairs; skip_hz may be floats, Detections or PassResults (_centres); spec may be a frame, tuple or list.
Two different mean_w_db functions (receiver: floor 1e-30, i.e. -300 dB; store: -99 dB for mean <= 0) look interchangeable but are not.
L_EXCLUDE_OFFSET_HZ, MERGE_HZ and GHOST_HZ are imported by live.py, em.py and store.py (store lazily, to avoid loading DSP). They need one shared C++ definition.
capture_from_wav hardcodes t0 = 900q + 1 s and a 12 s lead.
Ghost and suspect-neighbour rules deliberately drop a genuine second station within 20 Hz and 3 symbols. That is behaviour to preserve, not a bug to fix.

modules.purpose: Files a received PassResult into the multi-pass store under the first rule that succeeds. Rule 1 (header): the pass's own decoded header, validated by latent correlation once the segment's median W > 0.1. Rule 2 (soft-header): the pass's header LLRs summed with each provisional cluster's, then pairwise with every pass within 10 Hz and 7 days, polar-decoded, and filed only for the passes whose own LLRs agree with that header. Rule 3 (corr): latent correlation t against every open accumulator segment. Rule 4 (prov): join or start a provisional cluster. resolve_provisional attaches whole clusters that now correlate. Its statistic is also used by Store.merge to verify foreign accumulators.
public_api: corr_stat(z, w, m, W) -> (t: float, M: int)  # v = wW/(1+w+W); t = sum(v z m)/sqrt(sum((v z m)^2)) over common prefix where w>0, W>0, all finite
expected_t(w, W, kurtosis=KURTOSIS=3.0) -> float  # sum v / sqrt(sum(v + k v^2))
corr_accept(t, t_exp) -> bool  # t > 6 and t >= 0.5*t_exp
validate_header_match(store, key, mode, segment, z, w) -> (ok: bool, details: dict)  # reject if mode != acc.mode, or t < 3 while t_exp > 8
header_agrees(h: HeaderFields, llr) -> bool  # T = sum llr(1-2c) over heard bits vs midpoint/3-sigma rule, f = 0.3
associate(p: PassResult, store: Store) -> (key: (callsign, picture_id) | None, rule in {'header','soft-header','corr','prov',''})  # stores the pass first
resolve_provisional(store) -> list[(cluster_id, key)]

modules.determinism: No RNG or hashing. Arithmetic can be made bit-exact except that np.sum (pairwise, 8-way unrolled blocks of 128) and np.dot (BLAS) are not reproduced by a naive C++ loop. That costs about 1e-15 relative, which flips a decision only exactly at t=6, t=0.5*t_exp, or the header_agrees midpoint. Rule 2's LLR sums are sequential and reproducible if the order is kept (cluster members in JSON order starting from 0, then the own llr + that). Polar SCL decoding of the sum is exact only if the polar port is bit-exact. Iteration order is load-bearing (best = first maximum): open_keys and prov_clusters are sorted file names, members are in JSON list order. Python's Path sort is case-sensitive on POSIX and case-insensitive on Windows.
modules.io_state: All state lives in the Store (reads every accumulator JSON/NPZ and prov JSON per call; writes via attach/prov_add/log). associate() always writes the pass file first (add_pass), even when it ends provisional. Collisions append to log.jsonl. No threads. Called under LiveListener.lock in the listener's parent process.
modules.parity_test_idea: (a) Unit level: random z, w, m, W with erasures, NaNs and unequal lengths into corr_stat/expected_t/header_agrees; require 1e-12 relative and identical booleans away from thresholds. (b) Scenario level: rerun the rules-1-4 scenarios of tests/test_qrss_multipass.py and add a scripted generator of genie passes (qrss_fakes.make_pass_result: same picture or different pictures, SNR -20..+10 dB, decoded/undecoded headers, collisions, mode B segments, L vs CE waveform). Feed the same sequence to Python associate on store A and C++ on store B with the same fake Clock. Assert the same (key, rule) return per pass, and identical acc/*.json members (uid, segment, method), prov/*.json clusters and log events; S/W float32 bit-identical.
risks: The rule strings are a de facto GUI contract. live.py writes note=f'stored ({rule or "already a member"})' or 'stored (provisional)' into state.json, and native/gui/qrss_window.cpp maps those exact strings to user text.

Scaling: _best_accumulator loads every accumulator's NPZ from disk (4 × float32[3,52800] = 2.5 MB plus foreign parts) for every pass. resolve_provisional repeats that per provisional cluster, so cost is O(N_prov × N_acc) full loads per header attach. A C++ cache must invalidate on any write, including writes by Python tools sharing the store (qrss_decode.py --em takes no lock).

Rule 2's pairwise f-window compares raw f_hz with no band-centre conversion, so an L pass (pilot) is compared with a CE pass (carrier) 9.5 Hz off, whereas Store.twin does convert. This inconsistency is normative until Python changes.

A header decoded on the pass that fails rule 1's check returns (None, 'prov') without trying rules 2-4. Rule 2 returns 'prov' if its own pass was refused but goes on to rules 3-4 if the pass merely does not carry the found header. Easy to get wrong.

Rule 2 only uses LLRs of size N_HDR_BITS=2474: headerless frames (TINY, l-tiny) store a size-0 hdr_llr, and CE frames without a decoded header store 2474 zeros, which count as 'not heard' in header_agrees (llr != 0).
Association depends on header.decode (polar SCL) being ported bit-exactly or near; a summed-LLR decode near threshold is the most sensitive case.

modules.purpose: The on-disk multi-pass store. Root is $QRSSTVAE_HOME, else ~/.local/share/qrsstvae. It holds per-pass .npz files (PassResult.save), one accumulator per (callsign, picture_id) and provisional clusters. S = S_ext + sum(w*z) and W = W_ext + sum(w), over canonical float32[3, 52800] with each member placed at its segment's interleaver offsets, are recomputed from the members on every change. The store also does one-member-per-transmission deduplication (twin), foreign-accumulator merge with sha256 dedup and per-source replacement, the due-segment schedule (due), expiry, and an event log. It is not an on-air format, but the meaning of an accumulator is a cross-receiver contract.

modules.determinism: Bit-exact is achievable and should be the bar. rebuild/loo/merge are elementwise float64 sums in a defined order (members in JSON list order; foreign parts in list order) cast to float32. The merge digest is SHA-256 over the float32 C-order bytes, so a duplicate is detected only for byte-identical arrays. median_w on float32 is exact with nth_element and a float32 average. The only non-determinism is the injected clock (created/updated/merged/log time); tests pass a fake. JSON bytes need not match, but both implementations must read each other's files, and Python writes NaN/Infinity tokens.
modules.io_state: Directory layout under the root: passes/<uid>.npz; acc/<CALL>_<pid:08x>.json (callsign, picture_id, mode, codec_id, created, updated, members [{uid, segment, method, z_ref, mean_w_db, em_round}], foreign [{source, sha, t, M, merged, replaced}]); acc/<...>.npz (S, W, S_ext, W_ext float32[3,52800] plus Sx_<sha16>/Wx_<sha16>); prov/<cluster>.json ({cluster, created, updated, members}); log.jsonl. Pass npz contains meta (uint8 bytes of JSON: uid, q, frame, waveform, f_hz, timing{tau0, ppm, gamma, z}, report{10 TrackReport fields}, header{callsign, grid, picture_id, mode, segment, codec_id, version, reserved}|null, cw{text, z_match, keying, agrees}|null, ch_fs, ch_t0_index, f_mix_hz as a Fraction string like '-1235/64', estimator, em_round), z/w float32[n_data], hdr_llr float32[2474 or 0], ch complex64 (about 449,958 samples for FULL, 3.6 MB), psi float32[n_pos], timing_cov float64 2x2 or 3x3. A FULL pass is about 4.3 MB uncompressed; an accumulator is 2.5 MB plus 1.27 MB per foreign part. Writes go to .<name>.<pid>.tmp, fsync the file (not the directory), then os.replace. An accumulator commit is two independent atomic writes (npz, then json), so it is not transactional. log.jsonl is appended without fsync. In-memory caches: _zw is an LRU of 128 float64 (z, w) pairs, about 100 MB; _light (pass_info) is unbounded and evicted only on add/expire. There is no internal locking: qrss_listen.py takes live.dir_lock(root) (fcntl.flock / msvcrt.locking on .lock), but qrss_decode.py and qrss_receive.py open the store without it.
modules.parity_test_idea: (a) Cross-implementation round trip: Python writes a store from genie passes (qrss_fakes); C++ opens it, rebuilds every accumulator and requires S/W float32 bit-identical; same in reverse with Python reading the C++-written store (PassResult.load, Store.accumulator, pass_info, due, expire with a fake clock). Include a pass whose report.snr2500_db is NaN/inf (Python writes NaN/Infinity into the meta JSON), a callsign with '/', mode C with three segments, an L member and a twin. (b) merge: identical digests, acceptance and per-source replacement for the same foreign arrays. (c) Rerun the P1 tests in tests/test_qrss_multipass.py (rebuild, loo exactness, merge sum, expiry, atomic writes via monkeypatched replace failure, update_pass, attach moves a pass, one transmission is one member, due) against the C++ store.
risks: The store is the shared persistence layer during a mixed transition: the C++ app and the Python CLIs (qrss_decode.py --em/--retro, qrss_receive.py) will read and write the same $QRSSTVAE_HOME, so formats must interoperate in both directions, not merely round-trip within C++.

NPZ needs a production zip+npy reader/writer in native/core. Only the test-only native/core/testing/npy.hpp exists (it reads .npy, not zip, and only <f8/<c16/<i8). numpy's savez writes ZIP_STORED members with force_zip64=True local headers (size fields 0xFFFFFFFF plus a zip64 extra field), so a minimal reader must handle that.

Python's json.dumps emits NaN/Infinity (report fields, cw z_match, timing.z can be non-finite) and json.loads accepts them; nlohmann::json rejects them by default. Both directions need a policy (e.g. a lenient parser, or null with a custom rule) without breaking Python's reads.
SHA-256 is needed Qt-free in sstvae_core (merge digest here; also pass_uid and picture_id). Today native only uses QCryptographicHash in Qt-layer code (qt_fetcher, java_fetcher).

There is no store-level lock and the caches are per process, so a C++ listener plus a Python qrss_decode.py --em on the same root can interleave read-modify-write of acc JSON (lost member updates) and leave stale _zw/_light caches. Temp names include the pid, so files never collide.
os.replace on Windows needs MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) and fails if a reader holds the target open. The directory is never fsynced, so a power loss can lose the rename.
Store.twin imports receiver.L_EXCLUDE_OFFSET_HZ, a layering inversion (store -> DSP constant) to resolve in C++ with a shared constants header.

attach's twin rule (keep the copy with the higher mean_w_db, log 'duplicate') and the move-out-of-other-accumulator plus prov_remove side effects are order-sensitive. Rebuilds happen on every attach/detach/update and reread up to every member pass (cache of 128).
Iteration and tie-break order comes from sorted globs (open_keys, prov_clusters, pass_uids). A C++ port must sort the same way.
expire deletes pass files whose slot is older than the cutoff and that nothing holds. A clock mismatch (fake vs real) or a timezone bug deletes data.

sstvae/qrss/em.py (accumulator, loo via em_prior, load_pass, update_pass, pass_info, pass_uids, canonical_index)
qrss_receive.py, qrss_decode.py (open_keys, accumulator, pass_info, has_accumulator, canonical_index, acc.seg_snr_db/members/foreign)

notes:
Cross-cutting notes for planning the port of receiver.py, associate.py and store.py.

1. Data that crosses module boundaries.
- Detection (types.py): f_hz, path FreqPath(t_s, f_hz, weight), timing Timing|None, z_ref (nan until gate V passes it), method ('preamble'|'hint'|'tbd'|'template'), lead_in_s, waveform (0 CE / 1 L), a3_z. Flow: acquire → receiver (candidates/detect/_gate → track.verify/ltrack.verify_l) → receive_pass. live.py keeps SlotState.dets/cands and hands them back as `dets=`/`cands=`. em.py builds Detections itself (detection_from_pass, template_search).
- Timing: tau0 is in CH samples (250 Hz). cov is 2x2 from acquire and 3x3 from track.
- PassResult (types.py) is the one record that crosses everything: receiver → live tiles, qrss_receive, em → associate/store (on disk as passes/<uid>.npz) → render. Fields: uid, q, frame name, waveform, f_hz (tracker frequency at t0), timing, report (TrackReport, 10 fields), z/w float32[n_data] in air order, hdr_llr float32[2474|0], header HeaderFields|None, cw CwIdResult|None, ch complex64 @250 Hz, ch_fs, ch_t0_index, f_mix_hz (a Fraction on the 1/64 Hz grid), psi float32[n_pos], estimator, em_round. Its npz layout is a work-package contract, and the store makes it a persistence contract.
- Prepared (FE' or CH capture) is built directly by live.capture_prepare and em (capture_from_pass), not only by prepare().
- TrackResult leaks out via receive_pass(return_tracks=True), for EM.
- Store dicts are the de facto schema: members {uid, segment, method, z_ref, mean_w_db, em_round}, foreign {source, sha, t, M, merged, replaced}, prov {cluster, created, updated, members}, due() → {key, segment, f_hz, q, waveform, frame}. live turns due() into acquisition hints.
- Tiles (live.Tile → state.json + tiles/*.png) are the only thing the native GUI reads today. native/gui/qrss_window.cpp parses tile keys (picture_id, passes, confidence, note). The note strings come from associate's rule names ('stored (header|soft-header|corr|already a member|provisional)'), so renaming a rule breaks the GUI.

2. Seams. Python tests monkeypatch receiver._gate, _ce_resid_ratio, receive_pass and prepare, and get fast, DSP-free orchestration tests (tests/test_qrss_lreceiver.py, test_qrss_rules.py). Port the orchestration as a Qt-free layer over std::function seams, as native/core/rx/engine.cpp does with its decoder, so these scenarios run against C++ with stubs and in a --no-codec build. The CE-only detect inlines channel_for + track.verify rather than calling _gate; give it a seam in C++ without changing its call order.

3. Python stays normative, but these parts cannot be bit-exact end to end:
- The wall-clock budget (time.monotonic, FINISH_BUDGET_S=180, FINISH_MAX_CANDIDATES=12) makes the live end-of-slot result CPU-dependent. Parity runs must use budget_s=None. A faster C++ gate will legitimately find more weak signals in the field.
- pass_uid hashes the float32 bytes of z (sha256[:8]) and rounds f_hz*1000 half to even. The same slot received by Python and by C++ gets different uids, so two pass files. Store.twin (same q and segment, |Δcentre| < 5 Hz, keep the higher mean_w_db) is what keeps one member per transmission. Never key parity on uid.
- The store, the association arithmetic and the confidence trace can be bit-exact and should be tested that way. The orchestration is exact given stubbed inputs; DSP-derived decisions are tolerance or statistical.

4. Infrastructure missing from native/core:
- A production NPZ reader/writer: zip STORED with numpy's force_zip64 local headers, .npy v1.0, dtypes <f4/<c8/|u1/<f8. Only a test-only .npy reader exists.
- A Qt-free SHA-256, needed for pass_uid, the merge digest and picture_id; today only QCryptographicHash in Qt-layer code.
- A JSON policy for NaN/Infinity. Python writes and accepts them; nlohmann rejects them.
- Atomic replace with fsync, portable to Windows (MoveFileExW).
- A directory lock equivalent to live.dir_lock (flock / msvcrt).
- A small rational type for f_mix_hz strings.
nlohmann/json is already a core dependency. The interleaver map (air_to_canonical = framing::tx_perm) already exists in native/core/framing, so canonical_index is free.

5. Shared constants. MERGE_HZ, GHOST_HZ and L_EXCLUDE_OFFSET_HZ are used by receiver, live, em and store (store via a lazy import). Constants such as Z_ACCEPT=6, CH_FS=250, FE_FS=4000, N_HDR_BITS=2474, SLOT_S=900 and the frame presets should come from one generated header, the way native/core/config.hpp is generated from sstvae/config.py, rather than being hand-copied. Frame sizes:

| Frame | n_pos | n_data | Keyed duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 58,810 | 50,600 | 1782.7 s |
| MEDIUM | 21,545 | 16,384 | 653 s |
| SHORT | 8,438 | 4,096 | 255.8 s |
| TINY | 1,753 | 1,024 | 53.4 s (no header) |
| L FULL | 29,405 | 50,600 | 1782.6 s |
| L SHORT | 4,218 | 4,096 | 255.7 s |

Shorter frames carry an air-order prefix of the 50,600 latents.

6. Environment-variable rules (QRSS_OLD_GATING here, QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE in frontend) are read at call time and inherited by the spawned end-of-slot process. The CLIs set them with --old-gating/--old-edge-noise. A C++ port needs the same switches, or must decide explicitly to drop them.

7. Concurrency and process model. live.py runs finish_receive (receive_slot) in a child process (_FinishProcess) and does association in the parent under LiveListener.lock. A C++ port would likely use a worker thread instead: receive_slot is pure compute, but the store is not thread-safe and has unsynchronised caches. qrss_decode.py and qrss_receive.py open the store without the dir lock, so a mixed C++ app plus Python CLIs can race on acc JSON read-modify-write. Add a store-level lock that both implementations honour (e.g. the existing root/.lock taken for each write transaction), or document single-writer use.

8. Cost hot spots to keep in mind (not to change semantics).
- Gate V on a non-signal costs about 1 minute on FULL in Python.
- Each associate() opens every accumulator NPZ (2.5 MB each) and every JSON. resolve_provisional repeats that per provisional cluster.
- Every attach/detach/update rebuilds S/W by rereading all member passes (LRU of 128).
- A FULL pass file is about 4.3 MB, mostly the 250 Hz ch kept for EM. With 7-day expiry, disk use is roughly passes per day × 4.3 MB × 7.

9. em.py (CE-only EM, retro search) depends on receiver.receive_pass(prior=, return_tracks=, f_mix_hz=), channel_for, decode_header, detection_from_pass and capture_from_pass, and on Store.loo/update_pass. Port those entry points with EM in mind, even if EM itself comes later. associate.associate is also called from em.retro_detect.

10. Existing fast tests that can serve as the C++ acceptance suite through a --native substitution:
- tests/test_qrss_multipass.py: P1/P2/P6 and rules 1-4; 29 fast tests in about 6 s with .venv/bin/python.
- tests/test_qrss_lreceiver.py: stubbed joint detect, receive_slot and decode_header.
- tests/test_qrss_rules.py: _owned.
- tests/test_qrss_receiver.py: test_suspect_neighbour_of_a_strong_pass_is_dropped.
- tests/test_qrss_smoke.py: the end-to-end TINY blind pass and SHORT at -6 dB.
Substitution is by attribute assignment, so the bindings must accept the polymorphic Python arguments: hints as floats or (f, waveform) pairs; skip_hz as floats, Detections or PassResults; spec as a frame or a tuple/list of frames.

modules.purpose: The live QRSSTVAE listener. It takes 8 kHz audio chunks in, streams them to the 4 kHz complex front end (FE), keeps the FE in an in-memory ring (and optionally the 48 h passband store), and schedules work per 15-minute slot. During a frame it runs live receives (acquisition on the preamble, then round-A receive with the unheard spans erased). When the frame ends it runs a whole-slot receive (round B plus the whole-slot search), associates the passes into the multi-pass store and renders the accumulator. It also restores state after a restart (state.json reload, backfill of the ring from the passband store, recover of slots that ended unfinished) and splits time into dial epochs from the app's dial_changes.jsonl. Every result goes to a state directory: state.json, tiles/<id>.png and listener.log.

numeric_primitives: StreamFE framing around frontend.audio_to_fe: dsp.to_baseband's exact 16-phasor table (FCENTER 1500/FS 8000 = 3/16), sqrt(2) gain, firwin(255, 1250 Hz, fs 8000, kaiser beta 8) applied with scipy.signal.oaconvolve(mode='same'), decimate by 2 -> complex64. Blocks of 8000 audio samples with a 128-sample halo each side, block starts aligned to multiples of 16 on the absolute 8 kHz grid, FE index = audio index / 2
FeRing: ring of n = int((dur+15+5+300)*4000) = 8,410,651 complex64 samples (67 MB) plus a bool mask (8.4 MB), modular int64 indexing

digital-silence detector: |x| < 2^-24 for >= 1.0 s (8000 samples), with runs tracked across chunks
clock: a = round(t_end*8000) - len + 1 (Python round is half-to-even); RESYNC_S 1.0; an early-audio deque over EARLY_WINDOW_S 30 s (0.9 factor)
DialLog: sort, dedupe consecutive equal dials, np.searchsorted(side='right'), DIAL_GUARD_S (2, 50) s
