receiver.confidence_db: 120 bins (CONF_BINS), np.linspace edges, searchsorted, floor -30 dB; received = mean(w>0); receiver.mean_w_db
PassbandStore.write (frontend): int16 I/Q = clip(rint(x*8192), +-32767), memmapped one file per UTC hour; FLAC packing (libsndfile, 2-channel PCM_16 at 4000 Hz) 120 s after an hour ends
modules.determinism: There are no hashes in this module (pass uids come from types.pass_uid, sha256 of float32 z, made by the receiver). The FE stream can be bit-exact in practice: StreamFE equals batch audio_to_fe exactly after the complex64 cast (the test asserts np.array_equal). A C++ FIR computed in float64 will differ in float64 rounding, so a complex64 value flips by 1 ulp only rarely (tolerance: 1 ulp of complex64). capture_prepare is NOT reproducible without numpy's PCG64 plus ziggurat standard_normal: the unheard samples are filled from default_rng(q). Those spans are erased in the receive, but acquisition and the whole-slot search still see the noise. So detections on partly heard slots are parity-checkable only statistically unless the noise is injected (add a seam). blank and normalise use medians and float32 power, so they need tolerance parity (1e-6 relative). Everything downstream (detect, receive_slot) is the receiver's tolerance or statistical parity. The scheduling and bookkeeping (slots, refresh times, erase spans, heard shares, tile merging, hints, plausibility, state.json fields) is deterministic given a synchronous run (background=False) and a fixed `now` sequence, so it can be exact. Python round() is half-to-even in tile ids f"{q}-{round(f_hz)}" and in the audio index, so C++ must use nearbyint. utc_iso truncates seconds. In background mode, refresh outcomes depend on thread timing: a live refresh is skipped while the worker is busy, and progress is captured at read time. Wall-clock time.time() also enters log lines, `updated` and t_start.
modules.io_state: Inputs are (a) stdin: raw mono 8 kHz audio, little-endian float32 (--format f32, the default the app uses) or s16, no header and no timestamps. A reader thread does read1 of 0.25 s (8000 bytes for f32) and stamps each chunk with time.time() at read. The Stamper holds the first audio, and any chunk that reads > RESYNC_S late, for up to 5 s, then emits the held chunks as one with the earliest implied start. EOF means audio ended: the listener writes listening=false and exits. Or (b) WavSource: a replay stamped from its start time, realtime=False, which waits for idle workers before each chunk. (c) <state>/dial_changes.jsonl, written by the native app (gui/dial_log.cpp): one {"t": unix s, "dial_hz": int, "why": str} per line, appended and trimmed atomically with QSaveFile. It is re-read when (st_mtime_ns, size) changes; bad lines and extra keys are ignored. (d) The multi-pass store (store.due, pass_uids, accumulator, has_accumulator, find_member, twin, associate) and the PassbandStore (read/write). Outputs go to the state dir (default STORE/live, STORE = $QRSSTVAE_HOME or ~/.local/share/qrsstvae): .lock (flock'd, holds the pid); state.json, written atomically through state.json.<pid>.tmp and os.replace after every change and at least every 2 s; tiles/<id>.png, written atomically through tiles/.<id>.<pid>.png.tmp and never deleted; listener.log, rotated to listener.log.1 past 2,000,000 bytes. Log lines are also printed to stderr (the app merges stdout and stderr into its log panel). state.json keys: version=1, updated, now, now_utc, listening, source, frame (cfg.spec.name), waveforms ['CE','L'], audio_utc, slots[{q, slot_utc, progress, signals}], codec_error, busy (e.g. 'refresh 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z; finish ...'), tiles[Tile...], log (last 20 lines), finished (q within 48 h). Tile keys: id, q, slot_utc (quarter hour = t0-1), frame, f_hz, dial_hz (int|null), status (receiving|finishing|complete|lost), snr_db, z_ref, callsign, grid, picture_id (8 hex), mode (A|B|C), segment, cw_text, progress, heard, received, mean_w_db, confidence[120 float|null], passes, image ('tiles/<id>.png'), image_rev, updated, note, uid, waveform (CE|L). The native app reads: tiles[].{id,callsign,grid,f_hz,status,progress,confidence,mean_w_db,dial_hz,waveform,slot_utc,picture_id,passes,mode,cw_text,note,image,image_rev}, plus top-level listening, source, slots[].{slot_utc,progress}, busy, codec_error and log[-1]. It also string-matches the note values 'stored (header|soft-header|corr|already a member|provisional)', 'store failed: ', 'render failed: ' and GUESS_NOTE (duplicated verbatim in qrss_window.cpp). It polls state.json every 1000 ms by mtime in ms, and a parse failure is treated as mid-write (it retries next time). Threads in Python: the main run loop (feed, step and write_state under listener.lock); the stdin reader; a 'live' worker; a 'finish' worker; the PassbandStore packer thread. Processes: a spawned child 'qrss-finish' (nice +5) running finish_receive over a multiprocessing Pipe. It is sent the whole capture, about 7.2M complex64 (58 MB) plus the mask, once per dial epoch. The child watches its parent every 2 s and os._exit(0)s when the parent is gone. Environment: QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE and QRSS_OLD_GATING (sstvae.qrss.rules, inherited by the spawned child); OPENBLAS/OMP/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 (set by qrss_listen.py); QRSSTVAE_HOME; the app sets PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and honours SSTVAE_QRSS_LISTEN as the command override.
modules.parity_test_idea: Use three layers. (1) Pure units, exact or 1-ulp: StreamFE on a scripted chunking (the existing test's lengths 100, 3000, 777, 5000, 16000, 5123 plus a restart at a non-aligned index) against the C++ StreamFE; FeRing wrap and hole reads; _spans, restrict and DialLog spans/by_dial/span_at on the same jsonl fixture; Stamper fed a scripted (chunk, read-time) list covering a startup backlog, a burst after a stall, real missing audio and the first audio; feed()'s resync, early-clock and digital-silence decisions, checked by the resulting ring ok-mask. (2) Bookkeeping, exact: drive LiveListener synchronously (background=False, render=False) on a TINY slot with receiver.detect, receive_slot and candidates monkeypatched to stubs that record their arguments (erase_s, heard, the dets and hints passed, the step times) and return canned PassResults. Run the same scripted feed/step sequence through the C++ listener with the same stubs, then compare the recorded call logs and the state.json tile fields key by key (allowing for updated/now). Cover merge by band centre (MERGE_HZ 5), a waveform switch by larger Z_ref, _plausible ghosts (GHOST_HZ 20, |dq|==1), the headerless SNR cut (-6 dB), the known header surviving a missed decode, the hints from store.due and earlier tiles with a USB dial shift, dial-epoch splitting into one finish per dial, recover's skip of q already in the store, and _load_previous's headerless filter. (3) End to end, tolerance: replay a simulated TINY or SHORT recording (WavSource-style stamping, realtime=False) through both. Compare tile f_hz (<0.1 Hz), snr_db (<0.3 dB), callsign, picture_id and segment, and the picture PSNR between the PNGs. Inject the unheard-noise fill from Python (a seed hook) so the C++ side does not have to reimplement PCG64. Finally, test_qrss_window.cpp's state.json fixtures check that the C++ writer emits what the app's reader expects (no NaN tokens).
risks: Data race that Python survives only by luck: _refresh calls _candidates -> _hints -> self.tiles() (iterating self.slots and every s.tiles) and store.due() OUTSIDE listener.lock, while the main thread inserts and pops slots and the finish worker adds tiles. In Python this can raise 'dictionary changed size during iteration'. In C++ it is undefined behaviour. Snapshot the hints under the lock.

_keep(s, d) mutates s.dets, and _candidates writes s.cands/s.hints, outside the lock; step() and _finish read s.dets. The worker also writes _busy without the lock. All of these need explicit synchronisation in C++.

Any exception in a live refresh makes _worker set s.done=True. The next step() then retires the slot into `finished` WITHOUT its end-of-slot receive, so nothing is stored, and recover() skips it later because q is in finished. A transient error in a live receive therefore loses the whole slot. Decide deliberately whether to copy this.

Heavy work runs under listener.lock: _render (ONNX decode + PNG encode), the first codec load, associate() (store I/O + latent correlation), _identify_provisional and the passband writes in feed() (memmap + flush + an atomic JSON index rewrite about once a second). Feeding and state writes stall meanwhile. Audio queues in StdinSource. The app's QProcess backlog cap is 4 MiB (~131 s of f32 at 8 kHz), after which the app drops audio.

With finish_process the 58 MB capture is pickled across a pipe per dial epoch. A C++ port can use a lower-priority thread instead (the process exists only because of the GIL), provided the receiver has no unsynchronised shared caches. Python has lru_caches in sequences, precoder, frame, lframe, frontend, acquire and polar, and the Store keeps a ZW OrderedDict cache.

The tile-id and log-line formats look cosmetic but are not: tile id f"{q}-{round(f_hz)}" with 'b' suffixes on collision uses banker's rounding. The _refresh log line is emitted once per accepted pass, not once per refresh (an indentation slip), and the app shows log[-1].

Python json.dumps would write NaN or Infinity tokens, which QJsonDocument rejects. The app would then silently ignore state.json until the value goes away. snr_db, z_ref and f_hz are guarded; progress, heard, received and mean_w_db rely on their arithmetic. A C++ writer must never emit non-finite numbers.

The lock files must use the same primitive as Python (flock on POSIX, msvcrt.locking of byte 0 on Windows, on <dir>/.lock) for mutual exclusion with a concurrently run qrss_listen.py. QLockFile is NOT compatible. qrss_decode.py and qrss_receive.py take no lock and may write the store concurrently.
On Windows, os.replace of state.json while the app holds it open may fail. write_state does not catch that error, so it would end run().
tiles/*.png are never cleaned up (tiles leave state.json after keep_done_s = 6 h, but the PNGs stay). The passband store is ~57.6 MB per raw hour (sparse) and 48 h are kept.

FLAC packing of the passband store needs an encoder. native/third_party has only dr_wav (no dr_flac, no libFLAC), so reading packed hours or packing them is a new dependency, or else the C++ keeps raw .i16 hours (up to ~2.8 GB for 48 h).
used_by: qrss_listen.py (dir_lock, LiveConfig, LiveListener, StdinSource, WavSource, run, backfill, recover, write_state, close)

native app (native/gui/qrss_window.cpp) indirectly: it spawns qrss_listen.py --state DIR, pipes f32le audio to stdin every 250 ms, polls state.json and tiles/*.png every 1 s, and writes dial_changes.jsonl (gui/dial_log.cpp)
tests/test_qrss_live.py, tests/test_qrss_live_l.py, tests/test_qrss_rules.py, tests/test_qrss_acquire.py, tests/test_qrss_lacquire.py, tests/test_qrss_lunits.py (frame_seconds, in_band, slot_capture)

modules.purpose: Offline multi-pass refinement, CE only. (1) Leave-one-out EM: each member pass of an accumulator is re-tracked and re-demodulated from its stored 250 Hz capture. The other members' LMMSE latents serve as soft data templates, the header is known from the accumulator, and data is read per precoder-block parity so a pass's own reference cannot steer it. Rounds repeat until mean W gains < 0.05 dB (at most 3). (2) Template (retroactive) search: a stored slot capture is correlated against the picture's expected waveform over a frequency x timing x clock grid. The statistic is A2's chunked Gamma(K,1), Bonferroni-corrected to a normal Z (accept Z > 6). Then receive_template and retro_detect search the 48 h passband store and associate what they find. Nothing here goes on the air.
public_api: EM_ROUNDS=3, EM_TOL_DB=0.05; TS_CHUNK_S=2.0, TS_NFFT=2048, TS_DF_HZ=1.0, TS_TAU_S=2.5, TS_PPM_STEPS=2, TS_SLIP_SAMPLES=2.0, TS_CH_REACH_HZ=100.0; RETRO_MIN_COVERAGE=0.9, RETRO_SAME_HZ=1.0
lmmse_latents(S, W) -> (S/(1+W), 1/(1+W))  # float64, W clamped >= 0
prior_from(S, W, q) -> EmPrior(x_hat=precode(a,q), v=block_mean(1/(1+W)))
em_prior(acc, uid, store, q, spec) -> EmPrior  # from acc.loo (recomputed without the pass, not subtracted)
acc_mean_w_db(acc) -> float  # 10log10 mean W over W>0
known_header(store, acc, segment) -> HeaderFields | None  # a member's decoded header matching the key, else per-segment summed hdr_llr -> header.decode
known_keying(store, acc, call, waveform=CE) -> (keying_units, ook) | None  # vote over members with cw.agrees and z_match > Z_ACCEPT
pass_spec(p) -> FrameSpec  # lframe.get_any(p.frame); frame.plain() if a CE header says version 1
is_l(p) -> bool
pass_path(p, chan=None) -> FreqPath  # best of track.line_path and track.refine_path by verify_track z_ref
rereceive(p, prior, hdr=None, cw_known=None, estimator=None, em_round=None, path=None, return_path=False, split=True) -> PassResult | None
em_refine(store, key, rounds=3, tol_db=0.05, *, estimator=None, use_header=True, log=None) -> list[float] mean-W history  # writes store.update_pass as it goes
template_z(lam, n_chunks, n_cells) -> float Z
template_search(store, key, cap, spec, *, freqs=(), segments=None, tau_s=2.5, df_hz=1.0, ppm_steps=2, z_accept=6, f_mix_hz=None, q=None, return_stats=False) -> Detection | None [, Z, info]
receive_template(store, key, cap, spec, det=None, estimator='joint', segment=None, **search) -> PassResult | None
retro_detect(store, key, pb: PassbandStore, spec, *, slots=None, estimator='joint', log=None, **search) -> list[(PassResult, key|None, rule)]
numeric_primitives: LMMSE: S/(1+W), 1/(1+W) in float64; precoder.precode(a, q) (orthonormal block precoder plus the q scrambler), precoder.block_mean, block_index parity split (% 2)
header.encode/header.decode (Golay/polar header of N_HDR_BITS=2474 bits) on summed LLRs

track.make_classes, track.track (the tracker, run 1 + 2 times per pass per round with split), track.line_path, refine_path, verify_track, track.report; demod.extract; receiver.capture_from_pass, channel_for, detection_from_pass, decode_header, receive_pass

template: ce.mean_template(tau, mu, nu, spec, keying, ook) on the CH grid (CH_FS=250 Hz), tau = (n - t0_index)/(T_SYM*250*(1+ppm*1e-6)); chunks of 500 samples (2 s); drops chunks with energy <= 1e-6 * max

_search_chan: per chunk, a numpy FFT of R (chunk + 2*lag_max = 500 + 1250 samples, zero-padded to nfft 2048, doubled while smaller) and of E. Frequency hypotheses come from cyclically rolling FT by m in [-m_max, m_max], m_max = ceil(1.0*2048/250) = 9 (19 bins of 0.122 Hz). C = ifft(FR*conj(FTm))[:, :1251] (lag_max = ceil(2.5*250) = 625), lam = sum_k |C|^2/(N0*E_k), argmax. That is about 19 x K(~891) IFFTs of length 2048 per (segment, candidate, ppm)
clock grid: ppm_step = 2/(dur*250)*1e6 ~ 4.49 ppm, k = -2..2; drift dechirp exp(-2j*pi*frac(drift/60 * t^2/2)) and a mix exp(-2j*pi*((f_ch*t) % 1)), with the phase reduced mod 1 before exp
N0 = chan.noise_floor()*CH_FS (frontend.noise_psd)

template_z: scipy.stats.gamma.logsf(lam, K) (log regularized upper incomplete gamma, K up to ~900), falling back to the leading-term asymptote (K-1)ln(lam) - lam - lgamma(K), plus ln(n_cells) for Bonferroni; _gauss_z: scipy.stats.norm.isf(exp(log_p)) for log_p > -700, else 4 Mills-ratio fixed-point iterations
candidate dedupe: |df| < 0.25 Hz, |ddrift| < 0.05 Hz/min, |dppm| < 1
receive_template result uid = types.pass_uid(q, f_hz, z): sha256 of the float32 z bytes, first 8 hex
modules.determinism: No RNG. FFTs (numpy pocketfft; native/third_party has pocketfft_hdronly, the same library family) and the tracker make it tolerance parity. lam agrees to ~1e-9 relative, but the argmax over (lag, m, ppm, candidate, segment) can flip between near-equal cells, and Z near Z_ACCEPT=6 can flip accept/reject. So compare the accept decision only away from the boundary. template_z and _gauss_z are deterministic closed forms (boost::math::gamma_q / erfc_inv or hand-written continued fractions reach 1e-10). The EM history is tolerance parity, since it depends on track.* and demod.*. pass_uid is a sha256 of float32 z, so a C++ re-receive will never reproduce a Python uid bit for bit. Files written by the two implementations name the same pass differently. The store's twin(), RETRO_SAME_HZ and recover()'s q-prefix check are what dedupe across implementations. em_refine updates the store pass by pass (not atomically per round).
modules.io_state: Reads the multi-pass store: accumulators (acc.S/W float32 [3,52800], members, loo), passes/<uid>.npz (np.savez uncompressed, including the 250 Hz capture `ch`, f_mix_hz, psi, hdr_llr, cw). known_keying loads every member pass in full. retro_detect reads the PassbandStore (fe_<hour>.i16 memmaps or .flac) through PassbandStore.capture/slots. Writes: em_refine -> store.update_pass (rebuilds accumulators); retro_detect -> associate.associate (attach or provisional). No threads, no processes, no env vars (except the rules env inherited through receiver/frontend). Used only from the qrss_decode.py CLI (--em N, --retro), which takes no directory lock. It is NOT used by live.py or by the native app.
modules.parity_test_idea: (1) Closed forms: lmmse_latents and prior_from on random S, W, q against the C++ precoder (1e-12). template_z over a grid (lam 10..1e5, K 1..1000, n_cells 1..1e7), including the logsf-underflow branch and log_p < -700 in _gauss_z (|dZ| < 1e-6); the existing test_template_z_is_the_gamma_tail_bonferroni_corrected gives reference values, e.g. template_z(1500,891,1e6)=16.2058, (3000,891,5e5)=45.0552, (50,10,100)=6.3258, _gauss_z(-800)=39.8847. (2) _search_chan on seeded random z, E, en, N0: the same (lag, m) and lam to 1e-9 relative. (3) template_search on a simulated weak TINY/SHORT CE pass in a temp store (as test_template_search_finds_a_weak_short_pass): the same segment, f_hz within one 0.122 Hz bin, tau0 within 1 sample, Z within 0.05; and null on noise. (4) em_refine on the p4 TINY smoke fixture: history within 0.02 dB per round and the same number of rounds, with the per-pass z/w correlation > 0.999 against Python's.
risks: CE only: it refuses L frames and skips L members. Any L EM work is new design, not a port.

Low priority for the app: only qrss_decode.py uses it, so it can stay Python while the listener is ported. But it shares Store, track, demod, precoder and header with the receiver, so their C++ APIs must expose what rereceive needs (make_classes with prior and known header bits, track with timing/freq/outer, extract, report, a block-split track).
rereceive with split=True runs the tracker 3 times per pass per round. em_refine is minutes per picture.
known_header sums hdr_llr per segment across members and decodes. Header decode false-accept behaviour (<1e-8) must hold in the port.
Dead code and unused fields that a literal port would carry: the `lam = np.zeros` overwritten in _search_chan, _Search.cells, and drift_bins (always zeros).

template_search's Bonferroni n_cells counts every (seg, cand, ppm) grid actually searched, including candidates skipped by TS_CH_REACH_HZ (those are not counted). The Z changes if the C++ enumerates the grid differently.
scipy.stats.gamma.logsf for large K and lam needs a log-space incomplete gamma. A naive series/continued fraction underflows; keep the asymptotic fallback.
em_refine writes passes into the store while it iterates acc.uids, and nothing locks the store directory against a running listener.
used_by: associate.py references its known_header convention in a docstring (no import)

notes:
THE EXTERNAL CONTRACT THE NATIVE APP DEPENDS ON TODAY (native/gui/qrss_window.cpp, dial_log.cpp). (1) Process: the app runs `<python> qrss_listen.py --state DIR`. The command defaults to the venv python plus the script found up to 4 directories above the app; SSTVAE_QRSS_LISTEN overrides it. The app sets PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and the working directory to the script's directory, and merges the child's stdout and stderr into its log panel line by line. Stop is closeWriteChannel (EOF on stdin, so the listener writes listening=false and exits), then terminate after 3 s and kill after 8 s. A SIGTERM skips write_state, so state.json can be left saying listening=true. (2) stdin: raw float32 little-endian mono at 8 kHz, written every 250 ms from the receive pane's RingBuffer (read_since). No timestamps: the listener stamps arrival time and relies on NTP. The app drops audio once QProcess has 4 MiB unwritten. Half duplex replaces the ring, which the listener sees as a gap > RESYNC_S and erases. (3) dial_changes.jsonl in the SAME state dir, written by the app: {t, dial_hz, why} lines, appended with one write per line, trimmed atomically by QSaveFile every 50 writes (24 h kept). (4) Outputs read by the app: state.json, polled every 1 s by mtime in ms; tiles/<id>.png, reloaded when image_rev or the path changes. The keys it reads are listed in the live.py io_state field. The app also duplicates GUESS_NOTE, the note vocabulary from associate rule names, PASS_S=1782.7 (= frame_seconds(FULL) rounded) and the L marker band. The default state dir is $QRSSTVAE_HOME/live, else GenericDataLocation/qrsstvae/live, which equals store.default_root()/live on Linux; check macOS and Windows agree with Python's default_root before an in-process port changes who resolves it. (5) native/tests/test_qrss_window.cpp (915 lines) holds state.json fixtures: a C++ listener's writer can be checked against the reader with them.

PORT SHAPE. An in-process C++ listener would delete the stdin pipe, the Stamper/StdinSource, the subprocess and the spawned finish process. Keep a CLI with the same stdin, --state and file contract (and the same state dir layout and lock files), so (a) the app can still show a listener started from a terminal, (b) Python's qrss_decode.py, em and associate keep reading and writing the same store, and (c) Python-vs-C++ A/B runs on one recording stay possible. Keep a synchronous mode (LiveConfig.background=False), like rx::poll_wait, so the bookkeeping is testable without threads. Model the receiver as a std::function seam, as rx/engine.cpp does for its decoder, so the whole slot state machine builds and tests with stub receivers and --no-codec. Most of live.py is bookkeeping, and that layer has no oracle in golden vectors; its tests must be written the way test_rx_engine.cpp's were.

CONCURRENCY MODEL TO PRESERVE AND TIGHTEN. There are three contexts: the feed/step loop (takes the lock for feed, step and write_state); one live worker (one refresh in flight, never queued: a refresh is submitted only when the worker is idle and its queue empty, except the forced final refresh at finishing); one finish worker (FIFO, processes recover() slots one at a time when idle). The workers copy the capture under the lock (capture_read is a ring read of ~7.2M complex64 = 58 MB per call), compute outside it, and apply results under it. Python also reads shared state outside the lock (_hints/tiles(), s.dets, s.cands, _busy). In C++ that is a data race; snapshot under the lock. The receiver must be reentrant across two threads: Python's lru_caches (sequences, precoder, frame/lframe layouts, frontend noise responses, acquire, polar) become immutable-after-init or call_once tables, and the Store needs a mutex (ZW cache, accumulator writes). ORT sessions may be shared (Run is thread-safe), but the Python code renders under the listener lock. Move rendering, associate and the first codec load out of the lock in C++, or the feed path stalls for seconds. PassbandStore writes and expiry (an iterdir every write) and the FLAC packer thread also contend.

FILE-FORMAT DEPENDENCIES A PORT INHERITS. npz (np.savez, uncompressed zip) for passes and accumulators; JSON (nlohmann is vendored); PNG (stb_image_write is vendored, or Qt in gui); FLAC for the passband store. Only dr_wav is vendored: FLAC reading needs dr_flac, and packing needs libFLAC or a small fixed-predictor encoder. Without one, a C++ listener must leave hours raw, and Python then cannot be relied on to have packed them.

NUMERIC PARITY NOTES. StreamFE/audio_to_fe is the one heavy DSP item in live.py. It reuses dsp.to_baseband (already ported) and a 255-tap Kaiser(8) FIR at 1250 Hz with decimation by 2. Because outputs are complex64, a float64 C++ FIR matches numpy's oaconvolve bit for bit except for rare 1-ulp flips. Keep block starts at absolute 8 kHz index ≡ 0 mod 16 (the to_baseband table phase) and a halo of 128. capture_prepare's noise fill uses default_rng(q). Either inject it in parity tests or accept statistical parity for partly heard slots. Python round() is half-to-even everywhere ids are made (tile id, pass_uid's mHz): use nearbyint. Time is integer FE index = round(t*4000) on an absolute unix grid (~7.2e12), int64 throughout. slot_t0(q) = 900q + 1; slot_utc = t0 - 1. Two FULL slots overlap at any time (frames last ~29.7 min).

SCHEDULE CONSTANTS (LiveConfig and module): first receive at t0+25 s; refresh 120 s (--refresh); re-detect until 300 s; recheck gate-V-refused hits until 900 s; empty slots every max(refresh, 300) s after 300 s. Candidates are final once heard past acquire.live_end_s()+1 = 29.5 s. A live receive needs >= 50% of the first 20 s (the preamble) heard on the start dial. At finish: whole-slot search only if >= 50% heard, at most 12 candidates, 180 s budget. One finish per dial epoch (DIAL_GUARD_S 2 s before / 50 s after a change). Tiles merge within MERGE_HZ=5 by band centre on the same dial. Ghost rule: GHOST_HZ=20 against decoded tiles of slots q±1. A headerless pass with SNR > -6 dB and no CW callsign is dropped. Done tiles are kept 6 h; finished q are kept 48 h in state.json; recover looks back 3 h; backfill refills the whole ring from the passband store at start; the log rotates at 2 MB.

em.py is offline-only (qrss_decode --em/--retro), CE-only and not on the app's path. Defer it until the receiver core (track, demod, precoder, header, store) is ported, then port it on top. Its only new numerics are the chunked FFT correlator and the Gamma/normal tail functions.

modules.purpose: Encode an image once into a stored picture (.qrsp): the fp16 latents every pass of that picture sends. Prints the picture ID. Codec ID = first 16 bits of the ONNX artifact's `sstvae.source_sha256` metadata (v5 = 0xD1D8), else --codec-id HEX is required.
public_api: main() -- argv: image output.qrsp [--model DIR|.onnx] [--precision fp32|fp16|int8 (default fp16)] [--mode A|B|C (default A; 1/2/3 segments)] [--codec-id HEX]
stdout: 'wrote OUT: mode A (1 segment), codec d1d8, picture ID xxxxxxxx' (the GUI and tests look for 'picture ID')
numeric_primitives: ONNX encoder (onnxruntime; native/core/codec already calls the same runtime and artifact bit-identically)
sstvae.images.load_image (PIL LANCZOS fit to 640x480; native uses stb, so it only matches for a 640x480 PNG)

picture.prepare_segment: per group of 52,800, zero the 2,200 never-sent latents (framing._TX_PERMS), then float64 RMS over the 50,600 sent ones (np.mean = pairwise summation), divide, cast float64->float16 round-half-even
picture.picture_id: SHA-256(uint16_be codec_id || uint8 mode || each segment as '<f2' bytes), first 4 bytes big-endian
np.savez (ZIP_STORED) writer for the .qrsp
modules.determinism: No RNG. Bit-exact is achievable and required, because the picture ID hashes the fp16 bytes. Two hazards: (1) the RMS sum order. numpy's pairwise sum against a naive C++ loop differs by ulps, which can flip a half-even fp16 tie and change the ID. (2) Converting double->half via float double-rounds; convert double->half directly, as numpy's npy_double_to_half does. Image decode and resize differ between stb and PIL except for a 640x480 PNG, so the same JPEG gets a different picture ID from each implementation.
modules.io_state: Reads the image and the ONNX model (resolve_onnx: --model, else the cache). Writes a .qrsp, an npz with keys version(i8)=QRSP_VERSION, mode(i8), codec_id(i8), segs(f2[mode+1,52800]), picture_id(i8). Mode C is 318,080 bytes. No env or threads.
used_by: native/gui/qrss_tx.cpp encode_args() -> 'python qrss_encode.py PNG QRSP --mode M' (subprocess)
modules.parity_test_idea: Encode a 640x480 PNG with the v5 fp16 encoder through the native path. Python picture.load_qrsp must accept the file (check() recomputes the ID), its segs bytes must equal Python's, and the IDs must be equal. Golden: StoredPicture.from_latents(closed-form tensor, 0xD1D8, mode 0).picture_id == 0xD349C671 (test_qrss_format::test_picture_id_by_hand); feed the same float64 tensor to C++ and require that ID.
risks: The fp16 tie flip from summation order silently changes the picture ID: the store then keys the picture differently and a receiver's accumulator cannot match it
native/core/testing/npy.hpp reads only .npy <f8/<c16/<i8 with no zip, so the .qrsp needs an npz writer and reader (<f2, <i8)
The codec-ID refusal must survive the port: a model without metadata needs an explicit ID
The encode default is fp16 while qrss_receive, qrss_decode and qrss_listen default to fp32; only the checkpoint must match, but keep the defaults identical

modules.purpose: Write the beacon file for a clock-chip (Si5351) CE beacon: one segment of a .qrsp as 50,970 bytes (fits a 24LC512): header coded bits, callsign Morse keying, int8 latents in air order (x20), CRC32. The beacon computes the preamble, scrambler, precoder and phase itself.

stdout: 'wrote X: picture P segment S, CALL GRID|-, FSK|OOK ID, 50970 bytes'
numeric_primitives: header.encode: 142 info bits (callsign 8x6 bits, grid 15 bits, picture_id 32, mode 2, segment 2, codec 16, version 4, reserved 7) + CRC-16 (SSTVAE beacon variant, check 0xA69D), polar N=2048 with a literal INFO_SET, rate-matched to 2474 bits
morse.keying_units: uint8[192]
picture.to_int8: clip(rint(20*a), -127, 127), round half even
np.packbits; zlib.crc32
modules.determinism: Integer only. Output is byte-identical by construction.
modules.io_state: Reads a .qrsp (npz) and writes a .bin. Layout, little-endian: 'QRSB', version 1 @4, waveform @5, mode @6, segment @7, picture_id u32 @8, codec_id u16 @12, callsign 8 bytes @14, grid @22, n_latents u32 @24 (50600), scale u16 @28 (20), ook @30, keying packbits 32..56, header packbits 56..366 (2474 bits, zero padded), int8 latents 366..50966, CRC32 last 4.
used_by: qrss_beacon_c/ (the C reference reads its output)
not used by the native GUI
modules.parity_test_idea: Byte equality between native and Python .bin files for synthetic_picture(3, mode 1), segments 0 and 1, FSK and OOK, grid set and unset. Also require native BeaconFile::from_bytes to reject every single-byte flip that test_m10_crc_detects_a_flipped_byte flips.
risks: rint must be round-half-even (std::nearbyint in FE_TONEAREST), never std::round
A lowercase callsign is refused, not upper-cased (test_cli_refusals)
from_bytes also re-derives the keying and header from the fields and refuses a mismatch even with a valid CRC (test_m10_keying_mismatch_raises). Port that check, not only the CRC

modules.purpose: Write one QRSSTVAE pass as 8 kHz transmit audio for one quarter-hour slot (the slot fixes the scrambler). Input is a .qrsp plus --callsign, or a .bin. Waveform CE (constant envelope, about 50 Hz wide) or L (pilot plus linear data, about 22 Hz wide, 3.2 dB PAPR). The WAV starts 12 s before t0 = QH + 1 s and ends 3 s after keying.
public_api: parse_slot(s) -> q (SystemExit on a bad time or one off a quarter hour)

main() -- argv: input output.wav --slot ISO8601Z (required) [--callsign] [--grid] [--segment] [--freq Hz (default 1500; the pilot for L)] [--waveform CE|L] [--lead-in 0..10 s] [--ook (CE only; refused for an FSK .bin)] [--frame full|medium|short|tiny (L maps to 'l-'+name)] [--float]
stdout: 'wrote OUT: slot q=..., waveform W, frame F (D s), CALL (FSK|OOK callsign windows), carrier|pilot F Hz[, N s lead-in], T s of audio starting 12 s before t0'
numeric_primitives: sequences.scrambler(q, n): SHA-256 counter-mode bit stream, 'QRSSTVAE scramble' || uint64_be q
precoder.precode: blockwise Walsh-Hadamard transform plus scrambler
frame.assemble / lframe.assemble; header.encode (polar); morse keying
CE: ce.baseband. RRC pulse alpha 3/20 cut at +-8 symbols, T = 485/16000 s, phase modulation beta 0.8 rad rms, exp(j phi), raised-cosine 0.05 s key ramps, evaluated in 120 s chunks
ce.to_audio: exact rational-turn mixing to the carrier (ce.carrier_fraction num/den), amplitude 0.5

L: lwave.frame_baseband (QPSK, pilot share 3/20, three-pass clipper with overshoot (1.0, 1.5, 2.0) at 0 dB headroom, each correction band-masked by a whole-frame scipy.fft of size next_fast_len, guard 1 Hz)
lwave.resample: firwin(2*INTERP_HALF+1, 125 Hz, Kaiser 12) interpolator via upfirdn
wavio: float32 IEEE WAV, or int16 peak-normalised to 0.95
modules.determinism: No RNG. Carrier mixing is exact integer turns. The CE baseband is float64 with sin/cos/exp, so parity is to a tolerance of about 1e-12 in float64; the existing CLI test compares at atol 1e-7 after float32 storage. L's clipper is a threshold nonlinearity, so samples near the clip threshold can differ more; measure before fixing a bound. A WAV is valid only for its slot q.
modules.io_state: Reads the .qrsp or .bin (sniffs the first 4 bytes for 'QRSB'). Writes a WAV of ceil((12 + keyed_end_pos*t_sym + 3)*8000) samples: FULL is about 14.38 M samples, 57.5 MB as float32. Takes about 5 s of CPU in Python for FULL, CE or L (measured).
used_by: native/gui/qrss_tx.cpp transmit_args() (always --float, upper-cased --callsign, --segment, --freq '%.1f', --waveform only when L, --grid when it is a locator), then audio::read_wav and tx::condition_for_output
modules.parity_test_idea: Cross {CE, L} x {full, short, tiny} x lead-in {0, 5} x {FSK, OOK (CE)} x freq {1200, 1500, 2650} at Q_TEST. Compare native float64 audio to tx.transmit_audio: CE max abs error < 1e-9; L by the measured bound. Re-point test_qrss_beacon::test_cli_beacon_and_transmit and test_cli_transmit_refusals at the native binary with the same argv. Stream symbols are already pinned bit for bit against the C reference (test_qrss_c_ref C1), so the symbols themselves need exact equality.
risks: native/gui/qrss_tx.hpp hand-copies the slot constants (PASS_S = 1782.7, AUDIO_LEAD_S = 12, AUDIO_TAIL_S = 3, T0_OFFSET_S = 1, FREQ 300-2700). Python's FULL keyed end is 1782.678125 s. Generate these, as config.hpp is generated

L's pilot must be at least 300 + 22.07 Hz (check_pilot); L refuses OOK, both by flag and from a .bin
The whole-frame FFT clipper for L-FULL needs a large non-power-of-two FFT; pocketfft and FFTW sizes may differ, so match next_fast_len or prove the result does not depend on it
Clock correctness: transmitting a WAV in the wrong slot sends the wrong scrambler

modules.determinism: The receiver modules draw no random numbers, so a run is deterministic. A C++ port matches only to a tolerance (FFT searches, Kalman smoothers, accumulation order) and, near thresholds, statistically: candidate counts and gate decisions can flip.

Writes to the store (default $QRSSTVAE_HOME or ~/.local/share/qrsstvae): passes/<uid>.npz, acc/*.json/.npz, prov/, log.jsonl; to passband/fe_<hour>.i16, .json and meta.json; and an optional PNG. The rule env vars QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE and QRSS_OLD_GATING are set by the flags. A SHORT CE pass at -8 dB took 7.6 s end to end (measured); -12 dB takes 10-15 s; a FULL slot takes minutes.

Each signal becomes a tile in --state DIR (state.json, tiles/<id>.png, listener.log) that fills in as the pass arrives. Live receives every --refresh s; a whole-slot receive (round B plus the whole-slot search) runs in a spawned child process at the end of the slot. Results go to the store and the 48 h passband store.

modules.purpose: QRSSTVAE channel simulator (design section 4, WP4), working at the receiver's front-end format (complex FE_FS = 4000 Hz, 0 Hz = 1500 Hz audio). Steps in link order: exact clock time scale; frequency trajectory (offset, linear or warm-up drift, OU wander) with phase integrated in closed form; two-path Watterson Gaussian-Doppler fading; neighbours (CE or L, own random latents); AWGN in the 2500 Hz convention; impulses and crashes; peak-detector AGC. Records Truth for scoring receivers.

Trajectory(...).f(t) / .theta(t) / .wander_f(t)

numeric_primitives: nominal_turns: Fraction(f).limit_denominator(1<<16) and exact (n*num mod den*fs)/(den*fs) integer turns, else a float product wrapped by dsp.wrap_cycles
Trajectory: OU process at 20 Hz via scipy.signal.lfilter([1],[1,-a]) with a = exp(-dt/tau); trapezoid cumsum for the exact integral of piecewise-linear wander; closed-form warm-up drift integral

_Taps: complex Gaussian noise at lowrate = max(64*spread, 8) Hz, np.fft.fft/ifft of length n_low = ceil(n*lowrate/fs)+2 (arbitrary length; about 115k for 1 Hz on FULL), shaped by exp(-f^2/(4 sigma^2)) with sigma = spread/2, linearly interpolated, normalised to unit mean power over n
_Fading: two equal paths, the second delayed round(delay_ms*fs/1000) samples, summed / sqrt(2); per-position composite gain with the carrier-phase lag of the delayed path
impulse_noise: Poisson counts, sorted uniform times, log-normal levels, exponentially decaying complex Gaussian bursts of 8*tau length
_AgcDetector: causal boxcar (cumsum), decay-hold as np.maximum.accumulate in the log domain, one-pole attack via lfilter with zi
AWGN: noise_var = P*fs/(2500*10^(snr/10)); P = mean power over keyed samples (CE: |x| > 0.1 rms; L: the keying span in receive time)
L source: lwave.frame_baseband once per transmission, lwave.resample on exact grids, else an FS resample plus linear interpolation (-96 dB)
WAV path: hfchannel.sample_clock_offset (FFT resampling) and frontend.audio_to_fe
modules.determinism: Seeded and reproducible in Python: default_rng(cfg.seed), with neighbour latents and headers from default_rng(nb.seed) and their channel from default_rng([cfg.seed, nb.seed, 7]) (a SeedSequence list). Processing is chunked (CHUNK = 65536), so float order is fixed. A C++ port could only agree statistically unless it reimplemented numpy's PCG64, ziggurat normal, poisson and integers. Deterministic pieces that could be held to a tolerance: nominal_turns (exact), Trajectory without wander, the steady channel, and the AGC detector on a given input.
modules.io_state: Pure functions plus .npz I/O (save_npz/load_npz); no env or threads. A FULL slot is about 7.19 M complex64 samples (115 chunks).

modules.purpose: The portable C99 reference beacon (qrss_beacon_c/, about 1.1k lines) built with $CC and driven through its qrss_ce_test CLI. C1: SHA-256 FIPS vectors and hashlib; preamble, references, scrambler (3 slots, one past 2^32) and the spread-header whitener bit for bit; stream symbols from a .bin equal tx.slot_symbols. C2: integer phase within 2e-4 rad rms and 1e-3 max of si5351.target_phase. C3: Si5351 steps identical. Also UBSan-clean, no shift of a bare int literal, fractional update rates, and qrss_tables.h current against tools/gen_qrss_tables.py. 27 tests, none slow, 8 s; all but the tables check skip without a compiler.

notes:
I read the 7 CLIs, channel.py and all 28 tests/test_qrss_*.py files, and timed every test file's fast tier separately (each under 60 s, 4 CPUs). I also ran qrss_transmit on a FULL slot (CE and L), qrss_simulate on a FULL slot, and simulate + receive on a SHORT slot, all with scratchpad outputs. Nothing in the repo was modified.

1. What the native app shells out to today
- qrss_encode.py: PNG -> .qrsp.
- qrss_transmit.py: always called with --float. It writes a 57.5 MB float32 WAV per FULL pass, about 5 s of CPU. The GUI reads it back with audio::read_wav and keys it through TxEngine.
- qrss_listen.py: f32 audio on stdin; results come back through --state DIR as state.json, tiles/<id>.png and listener.log. dial_changes.jsonl is written by the GUI and read by the listener.
- qrss_beacon, qrss_simulate, qrss_receive and qrss_decode are not used by the app.
- native/gui/qrss_tx.hpp hand-copies slot constants: PASS_S 1782.7 (Python's FULL keyed end is 1782.678125 s), AUDIO_LEAD_S 12, AUDIO_TAIL_S 3, T0_OFFSET_S 1, 300-2700 Hz.
  - The first port step should generate a qrss config header from sstvae/qrss/constants.py and frame.py, the way tools/gen_config_header.py does for config.hpp.
  - tools/gen_qrss_tables.py already generates qrss_beacon_c/qrss_tables.h with a --check gate. Extend it rather than adding a second generator.

2. Suggested order: transmit first
- encode, beacon and transmit form the format path. No RNG; SHA-256 bit streams, the polar header, WHT precoder, exact rational-turn mixing.
- The C99 reference in qrss_beacon_c/ (about 1.1k lines, UB-free, SHA-256 included) already reproduces the sequences and the stream symbols bit for bit (test_qrss_c_ref C1, C3). Reuse its sha256.c and sequence code in native/core/qrss.
  - native/core is Qt-free and has no SHA-256 today; qt_fetcher uses QCryptographicHash.
- The native codec already reads sstvae.source_sha256 (the codec ID) and encodes bit-identically to Python.
- Then the front end (audio_to_fe, StreamFE, channelise, blanker, normalise), then the receiver.

3. Bit-exact hazards in the format path
- picture_id hashes fp16 bytes. Convert double -> half directly with round-half-even, never via float. Match numpy's pairwise sum for the per-group RMS, or one ulp can flip a fp16 tie and change the picture ID.
- int8 storage uses rint (half-even): std::nearbyint, not std::round.
- The same JPEG gives a different picture ID from Python and native (PIL LANCZOS against stb); only a 640x480 PNG matches.
- .qrsp files and simulator captures are .npz (zip). native/core/testing/npy.hpp reads only .npy <f8/<c16/<i8 with no zip. Python interop needs <f2, <i8, <c8, |b1, <f4, <U.

4. A pytest --native for QRSS
- It needs its own substitution table; docs/qrss/design.md rule 3 says the QRSS work must not edit NATIVE_SUBSTITUTIONS.
- sstvae/qrss has 66 module-level from-import bindings of functions or lru_cache wrappers. Each would need an explicit entry or the test keeps exercising Python. Notable sites:
  - tx.py: assemble, encode, keying_units, air_values, from_int8, to_int8, precode.
  - frame.py: preamble_ce, references_ce, spread_whitener.
  - lframe.py: preamble_l, qpsk, references_l, spread_signs.
  - ltrack.py: eight track helpers, some underscore-private.
  - demod.py: scrambler, wht, block_*.
  - header.py: polar_encode, polar_decode.
  - beaconfile.py: seven bindings.
  - channel.py: check_carrier.
  - frame.layout and lframe.layout are lru_cache'd and from-imported into ce, demod, track, receiver and lwave.
- Function-local imports resolve at call time and are safe: channel's check_pilot and keying_units, the CLIs' associate, Store and canonical_index.
- FrameSpec and LFrameSpec are Python dataclasses, and tests build custom ones (n_data, n_hdr, cw_after, hdr_rho, plus the v1 and spread-only frames). Bind a POD spec struct with an adapter, as SSTVAE's framing takes a mode index.
- Cached sequence arrays must come back read-only (a test asserts it).
- Several tests monkeypatch module functions to count calls or stub them (lchannel, lacquire, lreceiver, live), which interacts with configure-time substitution.

5. Golden vectors ready to commit (exact pins in the suite)
- test_qrss_frozen.py SHA-256 digests:
  - CE preamble (660 int8): 41deb0c5…
  - references_ce(3539): 715b6ad7…
  - scrambler(Q_TEST = 1954752, 50600): a6f36677…
  - keying_units('K1ABC/P') (192 uint8): 46c4fb45…
- test_qrss_lwave.py SHA-256 digests:
  - L preamble bits: 51917ffc…
  - L references 1770 bits: 1d490636…
- Header: polar INFO_SET sha256 4e064eee…, header CRC check 0xA69D, header bit-field offsets.
- picture_id 0xD349C671 (mode A, closed-form tensor); codec ID 0xD1D8 (v5).
- Beacon file: 50,970 bytes with fixed offsets.
- Frame preset counts:

  | Frame | n_sym | n_pos | Duration (s) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | full | 57274 | 58810 | 1782.678 |
  | medium | 20777 | 21545 | 653.083 |
  | short | 7670 | 8438 | 255.777 |
  | tiny | 1753 | 1753 | 53.138 |
  | l-full | 28637 | 29405 | 1782.678 |
  | l-medium | 10388 | 10772 | 653.053 |
  | l-short | 3834 | 4218 | 255.716 |
  | l-tiny | 877 | 877 | 53.168 |

- Exact rationals: L_PILOT_HZ = 12207/970, L_EDGE_HZ = 920/97.
- Tolerance pins: CE loopback gain 0.5788 and distortion 13.16 dB; D_PASS 0.0483; G_CE 17.09 dB; TBD_GUMBEL_* calibration.
- Good new vectors to generate from Python:
  - tx.slot_symbols for full, short and tiny at Q_TEST from synthetic_picture(3, mode 1). Exact for CE; complex for L.
  - transmit_audio chunks for CE and L (tolerance).
  - audio_to_fe and channelise of a fixed input.
  - StreamFE against batch (exact).

6. channel.py stays Python
- All its randomness is numpy PCG64: default_rng(seed), default_rng(nb.seed), and default_rng([seed, nb.seed, 7]) with SeedSequence lists. A C++ version could only agree statistically.
- Its value to the port is as the fixture and truth generator. Feed Sim.fe to native code through pybind, or read the npz: a FULL slot is 7.19 M complex64 samples, 95 MB with AGC and impulse truth.
- Its internal fallbacks (_tone_stub, its own firwin + fftconvolve front end) are dead code now that ce.baseband and frontend exist. Do not port them.
- Under substitution of ce.baseband, lwave.* and frontend.audio_to_fe/fe_to_audio, test_qrss_channel and test_qrss_lchannel still check that native transmit and front-end code compose with the simulator.

7. Receive side is tolerance and statistical only
- The receiver modules draw no random numbers.
- live.capture_prepare fills unheard FE with default_rng(q) noise, so partial-slot live receives are also RNG-dependent.
- Acceptance is by score: same pass count, header and cw text, f within 0.01-0.05 Hz, mean W within 0.1 dB, latent SNR against truth.
- False-alarm calibrations must be re-verified on the native statistic, not inherited: TBD_GUMBEL_*, the A2 Gamma tails, the template_z Bonferroni correction.

8. Runtime budget
- Fast QRSS tier: 579 tests, about 200 s single-process, measured per file.
  - Biggest files: test_qrss_beacon 24 s (subprocess CLIs), test_qrss_acquire 23 s, test_qrss_live 22 s, test_qrss_em 16 s, test_qrss_channel 10.6 s.
- Slow tier: 149 tests collected with -m slow, about 2 h (CLAUDE.md says about 120). It is dominated by test_qrss_receiver (55 slow; one SHORT pass is 10-15 s at -12 dB, 7.6 s at -8 dB measured) and test_qrss_acceptance (18, FULL slots, codec and COCO).
- Codec tests resolve models from $QRSSTVAE_MODEL_DIR, then /home/user/qrss-data/models; COCO comes from /home/user/qrss-data. Elsewhere they skip unless SSTVAE_REQUIRE_CODEC=1.

9. On-disk interop contracts (needed if Python tools and a native app share data)
- .qrsp: npz with version, mode, codec_id, segs f2[m+1, 52800], picture_id.
- .bin: 50,970 bytes, little-endian, CRC32.
- Passband store: fe_<hour>.i16 interleaved int16 I/Q, fe_<hour>.json written ranges, meta.json; optional FLAC packing via soundfile.
- Store: passes/<uid>.npz (meta JSON bytes plus a complex64 ch capture), acc/<CALL>_<pid:08x>.json/.npz (S, W, S_ext, W_ext float32[3, 52800]), prov/*.json, log.jsonl. Writes are atomic via os.replace.
- Live state directory: state.json, tiles/<id>.png, listener.log (rotated at 2 MB), dial_changes.jsonl, and .lock files (fcntl/msvcrt) for one writer per directory.
- The two receiver-rule switches travel as env vars QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE and QRSS_OLD_GATING so spawned children inherit them.

10. CLI text is an interface
- Tests grep exact stdout substrings: 'header     K1ABC FN42 picture 12345678', 'stored     K1ABC 12345678 by header', 'Hz at t0', 'retro: 1 pass found', 'by corr', 'EM: mean W', 'segment 0: effective SNR +5.0', 'OOK callsign windows', '3 s lead-in', 'picture ID'.
- They also grep error strings: 'outside the 300-2700 Hz', 'time zone', 'quarter hour', 'callsign', 'FSK', 'no picture', 'no decoded header', 'codec 1234'/'codec d1d8', 'decoding anyway'.
- Exit codes: refusals exit non-zero with no traceback and no output file; qrss_receive exits 1 when it finds no signal.
- A native CLI meant to reuse these tests must reproduce the strings. Parametrising tests/test_qrss_cli.py::run() over {script, native binary} gives the cross-implementation chain test, the QRSS counterpart of the SSTVAE native<->Python loopback.

11. Python-only architecture to drop in C++
- qrss_listen pins BLAS threads to 1 and runs the end-of-slot receive in a multiprocessing spawn child to escape the GIL.
- Stdin audio is stamped by arrival time (Stamper: hold 5 s, resync 1 s).
- In-process C++ should use worker threads and sample-accurate capture timestamps from the app's RingBuffer, while keeping end-of-slot work off the audio path. An end-of-slot FULL receive costs 10-30 s of CPU per signal.

12. Quirks and inconsistencies found (not fixed)
- qrss_simulate --ook on a .bin silently overrides the file's FSK flag, where qrss_transmit refuses.
- qrss_simulate ignores --post for WAV input.
- qrss_transmit and qrss_simulate --frame accept only CE names (mapped to 'l-' for L); qrss_receive accepts both, and qrss_listen accepts any name, including full-v1.
- Precision defaults differ: encode fp16; receive, decode and listen fp32.
- One open xfail in E3: a spurious second pass of one transmission gets attached by correlation. One strict xfail in CE M5: the 80 Hz skirt is -60.4 dB against the design's -65.

notes:
Interpretation: cpp_loc_estimate for existing native files is the NEW or CHANGED C++ the QRSS port needs in that area, not the file's current size. Line counts are measured (wc -l) except where marked 0 (dial_log/proposed files) or aggregated (schedule family ~4300 incl. headers).

1. What exists to reuse (concrete): pocketfft c2c/r2c (fft.hpp, double only, 16-plan LRU cache); dsp::to_baseband (exact 16-phasor heterodyne at FCENTER=1500 = qrss FE_CENTER_HZ, so frontend.audio_to_fe's sqrt(2)*to_baseband is portable bit-for-bit up to the FIR), wrap_cycles, kaiser/bessel_i0, next_fast_len (== scipy), hilbert, fftconvolve_valid, real resample_poly (Kaiser 5 only); framing::tx_perm(g) == picture.air_to_canonical; latents::N_LATENTS/pad_to_full; OnnxCodec encode/decode (exact vs Python under the same ORT version); images::load/fit/to_array/save_png; audio::read_wav/write_wav_float; tx::TxEngine with transmit_wave/wait/report/TxPhase::Waiting and PttWatchdog; rx::RingBuffer::read_since; util::Event; log::StatusLog/FileWriter; nlohmann/json (vendored, already used by core/settings and core/overlay); dsp morse table (needs hoisting, semantics differ).

2. What does NOT exist and is format-critical (bitwise): Qt-free SHA-256 (sequences.sha_bits drives CE/L preambles, references, scrambler, spread header; picture_id; polar INFO_SET checksum), IEEE float16 RNE conversion (prepare_segment, picture_id hashes '<f2' bytes; C++20 has no std::float16_t), npz read/write (np.savez = ZIP_STORED + force_zip64: local header sizes 0xFFFFFFFF + 20-byte zip64 extra, version 45; needs CRC32), npy dtypes <f2/<f4/|i1/|u1/<c8/|b1, a generated qrss_constants.hpp with exact Fractions (T 485/16000, ALPHA 3/20, BETA 4/5, L_PILOT_HZ 12207/970) plus a CI freshness gate like gen_config_header.py --check, UTC slot parsing (q = floor(unix/900), 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ'), and dir locks interoperable with Python (flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on <dir>/.lock; msvcrt on Windows).

3. scipy/ndimage/special primitives the QRSS Python uses that native lacks, with exact call sites: firwin with fs + windows ('kaiser',8) 255 taps @1250 Hz fs=8000; ('kaiser',10) 2*10*decim+1; ('kaiser',12) lwave interp; 'hann' notch at fs=250. Complex resample_poly(.,1,16,('kaiser',10)) and ce.py resample_poly(z, FS//g, fs//g). upfirdn real/complex (ce up=485, lwave up=970). oaconvolve mode='same' (acquire x4, track x2, ltrack x2, frontend x2), fftconvolve 'same' (channel), lfilter 1st-order with zi, freqz at arbitrary worN, windows.hann(sym=False), welch(return_onesided=False), ndimage median_filter(reflect)/maximum_filter1d, CubicSpline, make_lsq_spline(k=3), special gammaincc/gammainccinv/i0e, stats norm.isf/gamma.logsf. Existing firwin_band is in an anonymous namespace and takes any window, so exposing it covers most firwin needs.

4. Determinism classes for the port: bitwise -- sequences, polar/header, morse keying, air maps, fp16 store, int8 beacon (rint half-even of 20*a, clip +-127), picture_id, keying; tolerance (~1e-12, golden PLATFORM_TOL 1e-11) -- FIR design, FFT convolutions, modulation, front end, channeliser; statistical only -- acquisition argmaxes/thresholds (gammainccinv gates, Z_ACCEPT 6.0), EM, association, anything after a decision on an FFT-derived value. Python casts to complex64/float32 at stage boundaries (audio_to_fe -> complex64, channelise -> complex64, accumulators float32, decoder_planes -> float32); C++ must round at the same points to stay within tolerance. decoder_planes uses np.median over 50,600 sent W (even count: mean of the two middles).

5. The app<->Python contract to replace. TX (gui/qrss_tx.cpp): `python qrss_encode.py IN.png OUT.qrsp --mode A|B|C` (fp16 encoder, codec ID from 'sstvae.source_sha256' first 4 hex chars, v5 -> 0xD1D8) and per pass `python qrss_transmit.py OUT.qrsp pass.wav --slot ISO --callsign CALL --segment k --freq F.1 --float [--waveform L] [--grid GG99]`; exit 0 = success; WAV float32 8 kHz = tx.slot_samples(FULL) = 14,381,304 samples (1797.663 s) starting 12 s before t0 = slot+1 s. Typed replacement: encode(Picture640x480, mode) -> StoredPicture{mode, codec_id u16, segs f16[mode+1][52800], picture_id u32}; transmit_audio(StoredPicture, q, freq_hz, waveform, segment, HeaderFields{callsign, grid, picture_id, mode, segment, codec_id}, lead_in_s=0, ook=false) -> vector<double>. RX (gui/qrss_window.cpp): child `qrss_listen.py --state DIR` (defaults: frame full, both waveforms CE+L, --refresh 120, --precision fp32, store $QRSSTVAE_HOME or ~/.local/share/qrsstvae, passband STORE/passband, --recover-hours 3), stdin float32 LE 8 kHz mono pumped every 250 ms with 4 MiB backlog cap, EOF = stop; outputs state.json (schema listed in the qrss_window entry), tiles/<id>.png with image_rev, listener.log, and reads dial_changes.jsonl. Typed replacement: a LiveListener with feed(x, t_end), step(now), tiles() snapshot, dial-change input, and a Decoder seam (std::function like rx::Decoder) so it builds/tests with --no-codec; keep writing state.json/tiles/store files in Python-compatible formats so qrss_decode.py --retro, qrss_receive.py and terminal-run listeners keep working on the same $QRSSTVAE_HOME.

6. Env vars in the contract: SSTVAE_QRSS_DIR, SSTVAE_QRSS_PYTHON, SSTVAE_QRSS_LISTEN, QRSSTVAE_HOME, QRSSTVAE_MODEL_DIR (Python only), SSTVAE_MODEL_CACHE (native only), PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 (set by app), OPENBLAS/OMP/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 (set by qrss_listen.py).

7. Layering: put QRSS DSP/format/receiver logic in core/qrss/ (Qt-free; sstvae_core links no Qt so QJson/QDateTime/QCryptographicHash are unavailable there even though check_layering's regexes only forbid QtWidgets/QtGui/QtMultimedia/QtNetwork/jni/Python.h). Keep codec use behind std::function seams. qrss_tx::run itself uses only QtCore (QProcess, QTemporaryDir, QDateTime) and could move into core once its Runner seam is typed. Add any new library before add_subdirectory(tests).

8. Parity harness status in this container: pybind11 is NOT importable from /usr/bin/python3 or .venv/bin/python and is not in pyproject.toml; apt pybind11-dev 2.11.1-2 is available but not installed. native/build exists (GUI/codec/rig built, 40 ctest tests, onnxruntime prebuilt in _deps) with SSTVAE_BUILD_PYMODULE=OFF cached; a fresh configure defaults the option ON and FAILS at find_package(pybind11 CONFIG REQUIRED) because build_native.sh only warns. onnxruntime mismatch: .venv has 1.31.0, native pin and uv.lock say 1.28.0, so codec byte-identity tests are not trustworthy here until the venv is re-synced. Under --native today, sstvae.modem.dsp.to_baseband is already substituted into the QRSS front end/channel simulator (attribute access), so `pytest --native -k qrss` exercises one C++ function without any QRSS port; wrap_cycles and framing._TX_PERMS are not substituted.

9. Memory/CPU: one FULL pass is 14.4 M samples (115 MB as double); qrss_tx double-buffers two. Python generates audio in 120 s chunks; consider a streaming Player. Python listener: live receives cost 10-30 s CPU per signal; end-of-slot receives run in a niced child process; an in-process C++ listener needs low-priority bounded worker threads and a mutex around the shared OnnxCodec (its lazy session map is unsynchronised).

10. Hand-duplicated Python facts in the GUI that a port should source from generated constants: PASS_S 1782.7 (actual 1782.678125), AUDIO_LEAD_S 12, AUDIO_TAIL_S 3, T0_OFFSET_S 1, PREAMBLE_S 20, CONF_FLOOR_DB -30, MARK_L_BELOW_HZ 22.1 / MARK_L_ABOVE_HZ 3.1, FREQ 300-2700 (CARRIER_BAND_HZ), and the listener's note strings matched textually by plain_note()/GUESS_NOTE.
